That context is genuinely useful as you move up.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor (Kensington Place)
job.description:
Prometheus Real Estate Group has been quietly building one of the most respected apartment portfolios in the Bay Area since 1965. As the largest privately held apartment owner in the region, with more than 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle, they take a long view on real estate. That philosophy shapes how they operate their properties, how they invest in their people, and how they define the role you'd be stepping into at Kensington Place in Sunnyvale.

The title here is Neighborhood Service Manager, not Maintenance Supervisor. That's not just branding. It reflects a real difference in scope. You're not just keeping things running. You're accountable for the full physical operation of the property: budget stewardship, vendor relationships, capital projects, safety compliance, inventory, and the team that makes it all happen. You'll hire, train, and mentor your maintenance staff, and you'll set the tone for how the team shows up every day. That means being someone your crew can learn from and trust, not just someone who can fix things fast.

Residents (Prometheus calls them Neighbors) interact with your team more than almost anyone else on site. A slow work order or a clumsy interaction can undo a lot of goodwill that the leasing team worked hard to build. So communication matters here as much as technical skill. You'll field questions from residents, coordinate with contractors, and report to property leadership, often all in the same morning.

The on-call reality is worth naming directly. This isn't a role where evenings and weekends are entirely yours. Emergencies happen. Your team will need backup sometimes. Prometheus does offer standby pay and on-call premium pay to reflect that, but if hard boundaries around off-hours are a priority for you right now, it's worth weighing that honestly.

What separates strong candidates here from technically capable ones is the ability to run a team, not just a punch list. Someone who can diagnose a failing HVAC unit is valuable. Someone who can also coach a newer tech through the repair, document it properly, and build a vendor relationship that prevents the next failure is who this role is actually for.

What You'll Bring

  • At least five years of apartment maintenance experience, with two or more in a supervisory role
  • A minimum of three certificates from recognized maintenance or trades programs (BOMA, IREM, vocational, or equivalent)
  • Working knowledge of federal, state, and local safety regulations, with the ability to interpret operating manuals and compliance documents
  • Strong communication skills across a range of audiences, from residents to contractors to ownership
  • Physical capability to handle the demands of the role, including lifting up to 50 lbs. occasionally
  • High school diploma or GED required

Compensation runs between $38.75 and $45.00 per hour, depending on experience and qualifications. Prometheus also offers a discretionary semi-annual bonus, a referral bonus, and additional incentives tied to training and renovations. Benefits are genuinely competitive: fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage (including eligible dependents), 401(k) with employer matching, paid holidays including your birthday, and tenure-based housing discounts that grow over time.

Prometheus holds B Corporation certification, which means they've met verified standards for social and environmental performance. For some people, that's meaningful context about the kind of company they're joining. For others, the work itself is what matters. Either way, the culture here tends to attract people who take their craft seriously and want to stay somewhere long enough to actually see the results of their work.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The Assistant Community Manager role sits at an interesting inflection point in a property management career. You're past the purely transactional work of a leasing consultant, but you're still close enough to daily operations that the fundamentals compound fast. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, a top-50 multifamily operator based in the Southeast, this position at Hawthorne Ocean Isle in Ocean Isle Beach, NC puts you at the center of both the leasing cycle and the financial mechanics that keep a community performing.

What the Work Actually Covers

On the leasing side, you'll handle the full prospect journey: responding to leads, conducting tours, closing applications, and processing renewals accurately and on time. Occupancy and retention are shared goals, and you'll contribute to both. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which means translating resident events and community culture into content that drives traffic.

The financial work is where this role separates itself from a standard leasing position. You'll own rent collection, payment posting, and ledger reviews on a regular basis. Delinquency management is part of the job too, including weekly follow-up calls and coordinating eviction procedures when necessary. Reviewing billing accuracy and supporting financial reporting for the Community Manager and regional leadership gives you real exposure to how a property's NOI gets protected month to month.

When the Community Manager is out, you step into that leadership seat. That's not a footnote; it's one of the most valuable reps this role offers.

Qualifications Worth Noting

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months in an assistant community manager capacity is a plus
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP designation is a bonus, not a barrier

Where This Role Leads

Hawthorne runs a formal Career Path Program, and the trajectory from Assistant Community Manager to Community Manager is the most direct one in multifamily. The skills that compound fastest here are financial literacy and conflict resolution. Candidates who get comfortable reading a delinquency report and making confident decisions around collections will find that those same instincts transfer directly into a Community Manager role, where budget accountability is constant. Strong candidates aren't just pleasant with residents; they're organized under pressure and can hold a team's rhythm steady when the manager is away.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday with Saturday hours, one weekday off per week, and occasional evening availability for resident events. Commission eligibility on leasing and renewals, quarterly performance bonuses, and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid parental leave, and pet insurance round out the total compensation picture.

job.title: Future Leasing Call Center Opportunities in Maitland, FL
job.description:
Centralized leasing operations have become one of the more significant structural shifts in multifamily over the past several years. Rather than staffing each community with its own leasing team, companies like Hillpointe route prospect and resident communication through a dedicated hub, which creates consistency, scalability, and faster response times across a portfolio. That's exactly what this team in Maitland does, and it's worth understanding that context before you apply.

Hillpointe builds and manages market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and they operate at significant scale. Their centralized leasing and customer care team handles the full arc of the resident relationship: from the first inquiry about a unit all the way through lease execution, move-in, and ongoing service requests. This posting covers multiple levels within that team, both National Leasing Specialists on the leasing side and Customer Care Specialists on the resident services side.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On any given day, you're moving across multiple channels simultaneously. A prospect comes in via chat asking about availability at one community while you're wrapping up a phone call about a maintenance escalation at another. You'll convert inbound leads into scheduled tours (in-person or virtual), run outbound follow-up sequences to keep prospects warm, and keep CRM records accurate enough that the next person who touches that contact has full context. On the resident side, you're fielding service inquiries, routing issues to the right property team, and handling the occasional escalated situation that needs both patience and judgment.

Weekend availability, including Sundays, is required. That's not a footnote; it reflects the reality that prospects shop for apartments on weekends and residents don't pause their needs for Monday morning.

Who Fits Well Here

  • High school diploma or equivalent; some call center, customer service, sales, or property management experience is preferred
  • Clear verbal and written communication across phone, text, chat, and email
  • Accurate, consistent data entry habits and comfort working inside CRM platforms
  • Ability to stay calm and professional when a resident is frustrated or a situation is genuinely complicated
  • Comfort working in a metrics-driven environment where response time and conversion rates are visible
  • Strong enough multitasking skills to manage competing queues without things slipping through

What separates strong candidates here isn't just speed or phone presence. It's the ability to de-escalate a tense resident call, document it accurately, and move cleanly into the next interaction without carrying the friction forward. That's a real skill, and it's one Hillpointe is specifically building for across multiple levels of this team.

Because this is an ongoing pipeline posting, Hillpointe reviews applications continuously and reaches out as roles open at various levels. If you're building toward a leasing or property management career and want to develop skills that transfer directly to on-site leasing, assistant manager, or regional roles, a centralized team handling volume across a Sun Belt portfolio is a genuinely useful place to start.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Cottonwood Residential is filling an Assistant Property Manager role at Cottonwood Ridgeview Apartments in Plano, TX. If you want to attend in person, Cottonwood is hosting a walk-in hiring event at Stonebriar of Frisco Apartments (5200 Town and Country Blvd, Frisco, TX 75034) on Friday, May 22nd from 12 to 4pm. No appointment needed.

This is a front-line operations role. Day to day, you're processing rent payments, tracking delinquencies, keeping resident files current, and coordinating with vendors. When legal notices need to go out, you're preparing and delivering them. When the property manager is out, you run the community. That last part matters more than it sounds. Stepping into that seat, even temporarily, means understanding how every moving part connects: occupancy, collections, traffic, lease activity, and resident relations all land on your desk at once.

Cottonwood was an early mover on Self-Guided Tours, which changed how their sites handle traffic and convert prospects. That means the leasing side of this role isn't purely transactional. You'll be thinking about the full prospect-to-resident arc, not just answering phones and handing out keys. Candidates who've worked in sales or service environments tend to adapt to that model faster than those who haven't.

Entrata Core is the platform here. If you've logged time in it, great. If not, comfort with property management software in general goes a long way. A working understanding of basic accounting is genuinely required since rent collections, ledger accuracy, and delinquency management are core to the job. Fair Housing knowledge is expected at any professional level in this industry, and this role is no exception.

What Cottonwood is looking for

  • Prior leasing, sales, or customer service experience
  • Strong written and verbal communication
  • Basic accounting fluency (collections, ledgers, charges)
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing Laws
  • Entrata Core experience is a plus
  • Weekend availability is required

The compensation package includes a competitive base plus a quarterly bonus structure, full health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits (available within the first 30 days), a 401k with company match, HSA match, 120 hours of PTO in year one, and 10.5 paid holidays.

Plano is a competitive submarket with strong renter demand. For someone building a career in multifamily, an APM role at a company that invests in leasing innovation is a reasonable path toward a property manager seat. The skills you build here, collections discipline, vendor coordination, delinquency management, leasing conversion, carry directly into that next step.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

The Property Manager role at Summer Park Apartments in Buford, GA draws on a specific combination of skills that don't always show up together: financial discipline, team leadership, and front-line sales instinct. Cottonwood Residential wants someone who can read a budget line and coach a leasing consultant in the same afternoon. If you've spent time as a Property Manager at a conventional multifamily community and you understand how occupancy, delinquency, and concession decisions connect to NOI, this role will feel like familiar territory with room to grow.

Cottonwood is a REIT-backed operator, which shapes how the work actually gets done. REIT experience is preferred here for a reason: these environments tend to require tighter reporting cadences, clearer documentation of cost control decisions, and a sharper eye on variance from budget. If you've operated in that context before, you already know how annual operating budgets get built and defended. If you haven't, it's worth being honest about that gap before applying, because the expectation around financial accountability is real.

What You'll Be Managing

Day-to-day, this role covers the full scope of property operations at Summer Park. That means overseeing both the office and maintenance functions, staying close to resident communication, and keeping vendor relationships productive. You'll lead the on-site team, which requires you to hold people accountable without micromanaging, a skill that takes real practice to develop well.

  • Minimum three years of property management or closely related experience
  • Demonstrated strength in leasing, sales, or customer service
  • Knowledge of Fair Housing Laws
  • NALP designation preferred
  • Familiarity with Entrata Core is a plus
  • REIT experience preferred

Cottonwood was among the first apartment operators to roll out Self-Guided Tours at scale. That's not just a marketing footnote. It reflects how they think about the leasing experience, and it means the Property Manager here needs to be comfortable with tech-forward leasing workflows and willing to champion them with the team. The customer journey at this community has been deliberately redesigned, and your job is to keep that standard consistent.

Where This Role Takes You

Property Manager roles at REIT-affiliated companies tend to be strong career accelerators because the reporting expectations sharpen your financial fluency faster than most third-party management environments. Managers who develop a track record of hitting NOI targets, maintaining occupancy, and controlling turns often move into Regional Manager roles or asset-level advisory positions. The skills you build here, particularly around budget development and team leadership, transfer directly to larger assets and more complex portfolios.

What separates strong candidates in this kind of role from average ones usually comes down to how they handle the tension between resident experience and cost control. It's easy to spend your way to good reviews or cut your way to a clean variance report. Doing both at once, consistently, is the actual job.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Community Manager. Jeffersonville, IN. Waypoint Management Services.

This is a full-scope community manager role at a Class A multifamily property. You own the building: operations, team, financials, leasing, and resident experience. Waypoint wants someone who has already done this job, not someone learning it here.

What the Job Covers

Day-to-day, you're running all property operations and keeping the resident lifecycle moving cleanly from initial lease through renewal. That means staying ahead of delinquency, managing vendor relationships, overseeing maintenance response, and making sure your team is executing at a high level consistently, not just during peak season.

On the financial side, you'll handle budget prep, track NOI performance, manage capex projects, and report on property metrics with enough analytical depth to identify problems before they show up in the numbers. Collections, expense control, and rent growth strategies all sit on your desk.

Leasing and marketing are part of the role too. You'll conduct market surveys, monitor competitive communities, and develop outreach strategies to keep occupancy strong and traffic converting. Yardi and CRM proficiency are expected from day one.

You'll also recruit and develop your team: leasing staff, maintenance technicians, and service professionals. Building accountability into the culture is part of the job description, not a bonus.

What Waypoint Is Looking For

  • At least 3 years as a property manager, with 5 or more years total in multifamily
  • Direct experience at Class A communities
  • Budgeting, AR/AP, and capital project management experience
  • Strong working knowledge of Fair Housing laws
  • Yardi proficiency and comfort with CRM platforms
  • Demonstrated track record leading and developing a site team
  • Bachelor's degree preferred but not required

Compensation and Growth

Waypoint offers a quarterly manager bonus plus monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, which means your pay moves with your performance. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on day one, a 401k with company match, 120 hours of PTO in year one, two floating days, an employee housing discount, commuter benefits, and a referral program. Professional development is supported.

One thing worth noting for candidates evaluating this role: community managers at well-run third-party management companies like Waypoint often develop faster than their counterparts at single-owner portfolios. Exposure to ownership reporting, capex oversight, and cross-property benchmarking tends to build the kind of financial fluency that translates directly into regional or portfolio-level roles. If you're thinking two steps ahead, this kind of platform gives you real material to work with.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing in Daytona Beach with Waypoint Management Services

Leasing consultant roles at smaller, regionally focused management companies tend to carry more autonomy than their counterparts at large institutional operators. You're not just feeding leads into a corporate funnel. You own the traffic, the follow-up cadence, the file prep, and often the relationship well past move-in. Waypoint Management Services is hiring for exactly that kind of position at their Daytona Beach community.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Most of your time will split between working inbound inquiries and keeping your pipeline warm. That means phone calls, emails, tours, and the follow-up touches that actually convert a maybe into a signed lease. You'll handle the full leasing cycle: qualifying applicants, preparing lease documents, calculating prorations, and getting files ready for manager approval. Keeping the leasing office and model units tour-ready is part of the job too. Nobody closes a lease in a messy office.

Beyond the desk work, you'll contribute to outreach and marketing efforts to generate referrals and new leads, which is where bilingual (English/Spanish) ability gives a real edge in this market. Renewals and waitlist management also fall within your scope, so occupancy is a shared responsibility, not just a number the manager watches.

Yardi and CRM familiarity will help you hit the ground running. Fair Housing knowledge isn't optional in practice, even when listed as "ideal." Weekend rotation is part of the schedule.

What Waypoint Is Offering

  • Monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, plus a leaser-of-the-month monetary reward
  • Competitive base wage
  • Employee housing discount program
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage subsidized and effective on day one
  • 401k with company match
  • 120 hours PTO in year one, increasing with tenure, plus two floating days
  • Employee referral program, commuter benefits, and professional development training

Who Tends to Succeed Here

Two years of leasing, sales, or hospitality experience is the baseline. What actually separates strong candidates at this level isn't just closing rate. It's follow-up discipline. Prospects in a competitive market like Daytona Beach have options, and the consultants who convert consistently are the ones who treat their pipeline like a real list, not a wishlist. If you've worked in hospitality and understand urgency and guest experience, that translates well here.

This role is also a legitimate entry point into property management leadership. Leasing consultants who demonstrate solid NOI awareness, low delinquency habits from the front end (screening applicants properly), and genuine retention instincts tend to move into assistant manager roles within a couple of years. The skills you build here, specifically lease administration, traffic conversion, and resident relations, carry into virtually every other role in multifamily operations.

High school diploma required. Valid driver's license required. Equal opportunity employer.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Supervisor - 187
job.description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

An Assistant Maintenance Supervisor position lives at the intersection of hands-on technical work and team coordination. At Villages 3Eighty, a Berkshire Residential Investments community, you're not just completing work orders. You're helping run the maintenance operation. The skills that get used hardest here are make-ready coordination, quality inspection, scheduling support, and the ability to coach technicians without slowing the whole team down.

Make-readies are where a lot of the pressure shows up. Turns need to move on time, punch lists need to be tight, and units sitting offline hurt occupancy. Your eye for detail during unit inspections directly affects how fast the property can lease. That's a real number on a real report, and strong candidates understand that connection instinctively.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're supporting the Maintenance Supervisor and Property Manager across a range of operational tasks. That includes coordinating make-ready repairs and services, helping technicians meet deadlines, and making sure tour routes and models are always showing-ready. You'll help schedule daily activities, monitor work for both quality and quantity, and enforce safety standards consistently.

Inventory control and shop organization fall into your scope as well. Keeping supplies stocked and equipment maintained sounds routine until something breaks down mid-turn. You'll also track major repair needs and flag required expenditures to the Maintenance Supervisor and Property Manager before any money moves. That financial discipline matters at a company that owns and manages its own assets.

  • One year of hands-on maintenance experience across core skill areas
  • Comfort with technology, including property management software and related applications
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • Ability to meet physical requirements and take direction well

What Makes Berkshire Different for This Role

Berkshire owns and manages its own portfolio, which means decisions move faster and accountability runs closer to the ground than it does at a typical third-party management shop. As an assistant supervisor here, you're not waiting on a management company layer to approve a direction. That ownership structure gives the maintenance team more operational clarity and, frankly, more responsibility.

What separates a strong candidate from an average one in this specific role is the ability to coach without creating bottlenecks. Technicians need guidance, but the work still has to move. The best assistant supervisors at communities like this one can spot a struggling tech, step in to help, and keep the schedule intact. That's a harder skill than it sounds, and it's exactly what this role demands.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and competitive insurance benefits. If you're looking to grow from a senior tech or lead role into full supervisory responsibility, this is a realistic path to get there.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

At Wyndchase Aspen Grove, the Leasing Consultant role is squarely about converting traffic into signed leases. Berkshire holds consultants to a 20% closing ratio minimum, which means you're not just greeting prospects and handing out floor plans. You're tracking your own numbers, understanding where leads fall off, and adjusting your pitch accordingly. Every tour route and model unit is your responsibility to present in top condition. If something's off on the punch-out or the showcase looks tired, that's on you to flag and fix before the next showing.

Day to day, you're the first and most consistent human touchpoint for both prospects and current residents. That means professional written and verbal communication, a leasing office that feels welcoming rather than transactional, and enough market awareness to speak credibly about why Wyndchase competes well against comparable properties in the area. You'll feed ideas up to the Property Manager on marketing and resident satisfaction, so there's real input expected here, not just task execution.

Berkshire owns and manages its own assets, which means the performance metrics at the property level matter directly to the company's investment returns. Occupancy, traffic conversion, and delinquency aren't abstract corporate KPIs at a company like this. They show up in real decisions about staffing, concessions, and capital allocation. You're closer to that picture than most leasing roles at third-party management shops.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience, ideally in a role where closing or converting was part of how your performance was measured
  • Comfort adapting to leasing software and other property tech platforms
  • Strong written communication skills, including professional resident correspondence
  • A genuine interest in people and enough energy to sustain that through a full Saturday of tours
  • Attention to detail on administrative tasks, lease files, and follow-up documentation

Where This Role Can Go

Leasing Consultant is a natural entry point into property management. Consultants who hit their closing ratios consistently, build strong resident relationships, and show operational awareness tend to move into Assistant Manager roles, where the focus shifts toward collections, delinquency management, and T-12 reporting. At a vertically integrated company like Berkshire, strong performers have a clearer path upward than at fee management firms where turnover at the site level is higher and advancement depends more on timing than track record. The skills you build here, reading traffic patterns, managing prospect follow-up, and understanding what drives a lease decision, transfer directly into every senior leasing and management role in the industry.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Bozzuto manages properties across the Mid-Atlantic and beyond, and their reputation sits firmly in the upper tier of multifamily operators. This Assistant Property Manager role is based in Alexandria, VA, which means you're working in a competitive, high-demand rental market where resident expectations run high and occupancy pressure is real. The position pays between $63,000 and $66,000 annually, plus bonus eligibility.

The day-to-day splits between leasing and operations. You'll conduct tours, work to convert traffic into signed leases, and actively manage delinquency by collecting rent, posting receipts, and staying on top of accounts receivable. When the property manager is out, you run the site. That means coaching the team, keeping the community presentation sharp inside and out, and handling resident issues without waiting for someone above you to weigh in.

Weekend availability is part of the role. Expect one to two weekends per month on-site, with two weekdays off in exchange. That's standard for leasing-focused positions, and it reflects when prospective residents actually show up to tour.

Bozzuto also expects you to build a presence on social media. Creating content for platforms like Instagram and Facebook is part of how they market their communities, so comfort with that side of things matters.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just leasing ability. It's the combination of financial literacy and people skills. Someone who can read a delinquency report and act on it in the morning, then deliver a genuinely warm, personalized tour in the afternoon is exactly who thrives in this seat. The APM role at a company like Bozzuto is also a clear path toward a General Manager or Property Manager position, so candidates who treat it as a development role tend to move up faster than those who treat it as a leasing job with extra duties.

What You'll Need

  • A four-year degree or equivalent experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years working in one of those industries
  • Familiarity with rent collection, budgets, and accounts receivable
  • Experience with Yardi or comparable property management software
  • Comfort creating and posting content on social media platforms
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • A professional appearance and sales instincts

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Saturday afternoon, undecided between two communities. The way you run that tour, and what happens in the follow-up, determines whether they sign. That's a regular moment in this role.

Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Property Manager for their community in Hopkinton, MA. The salary range is $60,000 to $65,000, with bonus eligibility on top of base pay.

What the Job Actually Involves

This position splits its time across leasing, financial oversight, and team leadership. On any given week, you're conducting tours and working to convert traffic into signed leases, tracking delinquency and following up on collections, and coaching the people around you. When the Property Manager is out, you run the property. That's not a footnote. It means you need to be ready to make calls, handle escalations, and keep operations moving without waiting for direction.

Weekend availability is required, roughly one to two weekends per month, with corresponding weekday time off. That's the nature of leasing: prospects look for apartments when they're not at work.

You'll also manage the community's social media presence on platforms like Facebook and Instagram, creating content that reflects the brand. Interior and exterior presentation matters here. Bozzuto holds their communities to a high visual standard, and part of your job is making sure that standard holds.

What You Need to Bring

  • A four-year degree or equivalent hands-on experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years in one of those industries
  • Comfort working with P&L, budgets, and revenue data
  • Experience with Yardi or comparable property management software
  • Strong written and verbal communication
  • A real sales instinct, not just the ability to talk through a floor plan

What separates strong candidates here isn't just leasing experience. It's the combination of financial literacy and people skills. An APM who can read a delinquency report and then turn around and coach a leasing consultant on objection handling is hard to find. That's exactly who Bozzuto is looking for.

Bozzuto offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. For candidates thinking about career trajectory, the APM role at a well-run, third-party management company like Bozzuto is a direct path toward a Property Manager seat, and the exposure to P&L here is exactly what makes that next step credible.

job.title: Community Relations Manager-Cortland ChampionsGate
job.description:
Skills at the Center of This Role

This position sits at the intersection of sales execution and resident experience, and it demands fluency in both. The Community Relations Manager at Cortland ChampionsGate in Davenport, FL uses consultative selling skills daily: uncovering what a prospective resident actually needs, presenting the community as a solution, and closing leases with confidence rather than pressure. You'll also draw on CRM discipline, pipeline management, and conversion tracking to make sure no lead goes cold and no follow-up slips through the cracks. If you've built a track record in high-velocity, short-cycle sales environments, whether that's multifamily, hospitality, luxury retail, or premium automotive, you already speak this language.

Beyond the sales function, this role requires genuine operational competence. You'll support the Community Manager on daily compliance, inspect vacant units and make-ready apartments, walk move-ins and move-outs, monitor curb appeal, and manage vendor relationships. That's not a secondary responsibility. It's the other half of the job, and candidates who treat it as such will stand out.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

A typical day here doesn't fit neatly into one category. You might start with a community walkthrough, checking a punch list on a make-ready unit before a scheduled move-in, then shift into leasing mode to follow up with prospects in your pipeline and conduct a tour for a new inquiry. Afternoons might involve coordinating with a vendor on a pending project, updating CRM records, and reviewing occupancy and traffic data with the team. Resident events, social media engagement, and handling escalated concerns from current residents round out the picture.

  • Leasing and pipeline management: follow-up cadence, conversion tracking, and closing
  • Community inspections: vacant units, model homes, make-readies, and move-in/move-out walkthroughs
  • Vendor coordination and relationship management
  • Resident experience programming: events, personalized service, and retention-focused engagement
  • Social media and marketing program management
  • Compliance support: Fair Housing guidelines, OSHA protocols, and company policy adherence

What This Role Builds, and What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

For someone early in a property management career, this role accelerates development in ways that matter long-term. You'll build a working understanding of NOI-level thinking, because you're not just leasing apartments, you're helping protect occupancy and revenue targets. You'll develop the operational vocabulary and inspection habits that Community Managers rely on, which positions you well for a CM role if that's the direction you want to go.

What separates strong candidates from average ones here is the combination of sales discipline and genuine service orientation. Cortland's brand promise centers on premium resident experience, so candidates who can close a lease and still remember that a real person is moving into that home will thrive. The ChampionsGate location serves a market with active lifestyle appeal, so connecting residents to that sense of place, not just the apartment itself, is a real part of the pitch. Two or more years of demonstrated, measurable sales success is required. A bachelor's degree is preferred but not required if your results speak clearly.

Cortland is a vertically integrated operator with in-house design, construction, and management, which means the support infrastructure behind this role is deeper than what you'd find at a third-party management company. That context shapes how the team here works and what resources you can actually draw on.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Lincoln Property Company manages commercial real estate at a scale few firms match, with a portfolio exceeding 680 million square feet across office, industrial, retail, and mixed-use assets. This Assistant Property Manager position in Arlington, VA puts you inside that operation at the property level, working directly alongside experienced Property Managers to keep assets performing and clients informed.

The work itself covers a wide band of commercial property management fundamentals. You'll process vendor invoices against management agreement terms, help prepare monthly reports and budget packages, and assist with CAM reconciliations and operating expense recovery charges. Lease administration runs through this role too: lease setup, lease changes, coordination with accounting, and keeping everything accurate across company and client systems. On the operations side, you'll coordinate tenant move-ins and move-outs, walk spaces, keep vacant suites tour-ready, and respond to tenant needs with a sense of urgency. Vendor procurement, contract documents, purchase orders, bidding support, and regular property inspections round out the day-to-day.

What this role requires is different from what it builds, and that distinction matters if you're thinking about whether this is the right next step. Coming in, you need solid communication skills, comfort with financial concepts like percentages and markups, and the organizational discipline to manage multiple moving pieces without dropping details. Intermediate proficiency in Microsoft Office is a real baseline expectation, not a formality. One to two years of related experience helps, especially any exposure to commercial office, retail, or industrial properties.

What the role builds is harder to list but easier to recognize: the ability to read a property's financial picture through aging reports and collections data, the judgment to flag a vendor invoice that doesn't match contract terms, and the instinct to anticipate what a client needs before they ask. Those are skills that translate directly into a Property Manager seat, which is the natural next step for someone who performs well here.

One honest note about commercial property management at this level: the job is genuinely in-person and sometimes irregular. After-hours responses, weekend availability, and emergency situations are part of the contract with this kind of work. That's not a warning so much as a reality check. The candidates who thrive here are the ones who treat those moments as part of the craft rather than interruptions to it.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree preferred; 1 to 2 years of relevant experience, or a comparable combination of education and experience
  • Commercial property experience (office, retail, or industrial) strongly preferred
  • Intermediate Microsoft Office skills required
  • Ability to calculate financial figures and interpret lease and financial documents
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills across tenant, vendor, and client audiences
  • Organizational discipline and an analytical mindset
  • Willingness to work after hours and respond to emergencies as needed
  • 100% in-office role; no remote or hybrid option

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor in Training - Addison at Wyndham
job.description:
Most apartment communities separate their maintenance leadership from hands-on work. Weinstein Properties takes a different approach: they develop supervisors from within the work itself, which is why this role exists. The Maintenance Supervisor in Training position at Addison at Wyndham in Glen Allen puts you on the floor with a working supervisor and a full team, building toward a leadership seat rather than being dropped into one unprepared.

What This Role Actually Looks Like Day to Day

You'll spend your time split between doing and directing. Some mornings that means diagnosing an HVAC issue in a resident's unit; others it means coordinating vendor scheduling or reviewing the work order queue to make sure turns are moving on time. The hands-on expectation is genuine here. This isn't a desk role with occasional walkthroughs. You'll work alongside the team on repairs across HVAC, electrical, plumbing, appliances, carpentry, drywall, pool maintenance, and exterior structural work. You'll also share on-call rotation with other team members, so nights and weekends will come up. That's worth knowing going in.

The training component means you'll shadow and work under an experienced supervisor while gradually taking on more coordination responsibilities. Weinstein owns and manages all of its properties in-house rather than operating under third-party management, which tends to create more consistent standards and clearer internal career paths. Flexibility to transfer to another community as you advance is part of the arrangement.

Compensation starts at $26 per hour depending on experience, with a $150 weekly on-call bonus regardless of call volume, an additional holiday on-call bonus, a quarterly performance bonus with up to $1,110 potential, and a $1,500 sign-on bonus (details discussed during the interview). Benefits include rent discount, health, dental and vision, 401k, PTO, paid holidays, and birthday time off.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • At least 4 years of trade experience with hands-on work in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general building maintenance
  • At least 1 year in a lead, assistant supervisor, or supervisory maintenance role at an apartment community
  • EPA/CFC Refrigerant certification (Type I and II, or Universal) is required before starting
  • Comfortable using software to manage work orders, schedule turns, order supplies, and communicate with the team
  • Valid driver's license, personal transportation, and your own tools
  • DMV check and background check required

What separates strong candidates here isn't just technical range. It's the combination of trade competence with genuine comfort talking to residents. Maintenance supervisors at the community level are often the face of the property when something goes wrong. Residents remember how a repair interaction felt, not just whether it got done. If you can fix the problem and leave the resident feeling heard, you'll thrive in this kind of role. If you've been a strong tech who's ready to grow into leading others, this training structure is a real on-ramp, not just a title.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - EPA Certified
job.description:
Weinstein Properties manages its communities in-house, which changes the day-to-day experience for maintenance staff in ways that matter. There's no third-party management layer between you and the decisions that affect your property. Standards are consistent, leadership is accessible, and when something needs to get done, the answer doesn't get lost in a chain of approvals. For a skilled technician who's tired of the disconnect that comes with fee management setups, that structure makes a real difference.

The opening at Bexley at Anderson Mill in the Cedar Park area is a full-time maintenance technician role built around someone with at least three years of apartment maintenance experience and a current EPA certification (Type II or Universal). The work spans the full range of residential maintenance: completing work orders in occupied units, supporting turns and make-readies, and handling HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry repairs. You'll also help maintain the community's grounds, amenities, and pool areas alongside the rest of the maintenance team.

The compensation starts at $22 per hour and moves up based on experience. On-call participation comes with a flat $150 weekly guarantee regardless of call volume, plus an additional $150 for holiday on-call shifts. Quarterly bonuses reach up to $980 tied to property and team performance. Benefits include rent discount, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, an Employee Assistance Program, and a referral program. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8 to 5, with rotating emergency on-call coverage shared across the team.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just the EPA cert or the HVAC hours. It's the combination of technical range and resident-facing composure. Technicians who thrive in apartment maintenance understand that a work order is also a service interaction. The residents living in those units are your customers, and how you communicate while you're diagnosing a problem matters as much as how quickly you fix it. If you've developed that balance over your career, it tends to show up clearly during a walkthrough or a reference call.

From a career development standpoint, a role like this one builds the foundation for a lead technician or maintenance supervisor path. The skills that compound most over time: HVAC diagnostic depth, vendor coordination during turns, and the ability to prioritize a work order queue without letting anything age. Technicians who move into supervisory roles usually got there because they ran their properties like the performance of the asset was their responsibility, not just their manager's.

What You'll Need

  • Minimum three years of apartment or residential maintenance experience
  • EPA Certification, Type II or Universal
  • Hands-on HVAC troubleshooting and repair experience
  • Comfort with work order systems and basic computer and mobile device use
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs and work outdoors year-round in Central Texas conditions
  • Reliable transportation and ability to pass a background check

job.title: Maintenance Technician- Scottsdale Horizon Apartments
job.description:
Multi-trade competency is the core skill set here. Not just the ability to fix things, but the ability to triage, prioritize, and close out work orders without constant hand-holding. At Scottsdale Horizon Apartments, MG Properties is looking for a Maintenance Technician who brings real hands-on experience across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and appliance repair. Two years minimum on a property of 200 units or larger is the baseline they're working from. That's not an arbitrary number. At that scale, you've seen enough volume to know how to work a board efficiently and keep turns from dragging.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

Grounds and common area upkeep, service request completion, painting, and make-ready work are all part of the rotation. So is on-call coverage, which means you'll take emergency calls on your assigned nights and weekends. That's just the nature of residential maintenance. Anyone who's done it knows the on-call rotation is where you earn the trust of your team and your residents pretty quickly. Customer service isn't a soft skill here, it's operational. How you show up at a resident's door when their A/C goes out at 10 PM on a July evening in Scottsdale matters as much as whether you can fix it.

Speaking of Scottsdale in July: HVAC is not optional knowledge at this property. Arizona summers are unforgiving, and HVAC calls will dominate your board from late spring through early fall. If your A/C experience is thin, this role will expose that fast.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

  • Genuine multi-trade experience, not familiarity with one or two disciplines and a learning attitude about the rest
  • Comfort managing a full work order board without losing track of priorities
  • The ability to communicate clearly with residents under pressure
  • Reliable transportation to get to the property and respond to on-call situations
  • Team orientation. Maintenance at a community this size is a team sport.

Working for MG Properties

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. That kind of track record in a regional operator usually means standardized processes, real support infrastructure, and a company that isn't figuring out property management as it goes. The compensation package includes monthly bonuses, profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, full medical, dental, and vision, and rental discounts. PTO, paid holidays, personal days, and sick time are also part of the package.

If you've got the trade skills and the temperament for residential maintenance work, this is a solid place to put them to use.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Where Sales, Relationship-Building, and Campus Life Overlap

Student housing leasing runs on a different rhythm than conventional multifamily. Prospects are often first-time renters, their parents are frequently part of the conversation, and the leasing cycle compresses hard around academic calendars. At Redpoint Tempe, a Scion Group community serving the Arizona State University market, the Experience Team Member role sits at the center of all of it. This is a position built around interpersonal skill, and it calls on that skill constantly.

You'll conduct community and amenity tours, handle prospect follow-up, and execute sales and engagement initiatives set by the management team. Beyond the leasing floor, the role pulls in light marketing work: contributing ideas for local outreach, helping manage social media presence, and assisting with resident events. Property administration is part of the mix too. Package retrieval, office organization, maintenance request coordination, and after-hours lockout coverage all fall within scope. The range is real, and candidates who prefer narrow, task-specific work tend to find student housing ETM roles uncomfortable.

The Skills This Role Develops and Demands

Strong candidates bring communication skills that adapt quickly. You might be walking a high-energy sophomore through a floor plan, then shifting to a detailed phone call with a concerned parent, then following up with a prospect who raised objections during a tour earlier in the week. The ability to read a situation and adjust tone without losing momentum is the core competency here.

Reliability matters more than most postings acknowledge. Student housing turns are concentrated and intense. When the summer turn hits at a property like this, everyone is needed and tardiness or inconsistency creates real downstream problems for the operations team. Scion specifically requires availability during turn periods, summer, and holidays. That's not boilerplate. It reflects how student housing actually works.

  • Customer-facing communication with a diverse population of residents, prospects, and guarantors
  • Sales and objection handling at the leasing level
  • Social media and community engagement support
  • Package management, office maintenance, and general administrative support
  • After-hours on-call rotation for lockout assistance
  • Maintenance request tracking and follow-up coordination

What Makes This Role at Scion Worth Noting

Scion Group operates at scale in the student housing sector, which means the systems, training, and operational standards here are more developed than what you'd find at a smaller independent operator. For someone early in a property management career, that structure matters. The skills you build in a student housing ETM role, specifically high-volume prospect communication, creative marketing execution, and turn-cycle operations, transfer directly to conventional multifamily leasing roles and set a strong foundation for moving into assistant manager or leasing manager positions over time.

Tempe's rental market around ASU is genuinely competitive, with a steady supply of purpose-built student communities. That means leasing here isn't passive. Traffic needs to be converted with intention, and the feedback you provide to management about sales barriers and objections has real operational value. Candidates who treat that feedback loop seriously tend to stand out.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday afternoon and you're on the phone with a resident whose rent payment posted to the wrong ledger, while a prospect walks through the door for a scheduled tour. You wrap the call with a clear resolution, hand the prospect off smoothly, and get back to a delinquency follow-up list before the day closes. That's the rhythm of this role at Evolve Waterford in Leland, NC.

The Role at Evolve Waterford

Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the 50 largest multifamily management companies in the country and deeply rooted in the Southeast, is hiring an Assistant Community Manager for this Leland property. The position sits at the intersection of leasing, financial administration, and team leadership. You'll work alongside the Community Manager to keep occupancy strong, delinquency in check, and residents genuinely satisfied.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, respond to leads, guide prospects through applications, and work renewals to protect retention. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which at a property like this means showcasing resident events and keeping the community feel visible online. On the financial side, the job involves rent collection, payment posting, ledger audits, delinquency calls, and supporting eviction coordination when necessary. These aren't background tasks. They're a core part of what this role requires you to do well.

When the Community Manager is out, you run the office. That means maintaining team momentum, setting daily priorities, and fielding whatever comes through the door without letting things slide.

What This Role Requires

  • High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • At least six months in an assistant community manager capacity preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP designation is a plus

Candidates who stand out in this role tend to be comfortable reading financial reports and acting on what they find, not just passing numbers up the chain. Delinquency management specifically rewards people who are organized, consistent, and direct without being combative. If you've worked at a property where rent collection was treated as a weekly discipline rather than a month-end scramble, that experience translates directly here.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off to maintain a 40-hour week. Some evening and weekend availability may come up for resident events.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance. Hawthorne also offers a structured Career Path Program for employees working toward a Community Manager role.

job.title: Leasing Consultant Sales Intern (Nantucket Cove)
job.description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work

Leasing is a sales role with a customer service wrapper, and this internship at Nantucket Cove makes that clear from day one. The skills you'll use most heavily are consultative selling, active listening, and persuasive communication. Every tour is a structured conversation: you're qualifying a prospect's needs, matching them to the right floor plan, and making the case for why this community fits their life. If you've worked retail, hospitality, or food service, you already know how to read people quickly and adjust your approach. That instinct transfers directly here.

You'll also work inside property management software to track leads and follow-ups, which means attention to detail and data discipline matter from the start. Inaccurate records create gaps in follow-up, and gaps in follow-up cost leases. That's a lesson experienced leasing professionals learn early, and you'll learn it here.

What You'll Do at Nantucket Cove

BAM Companies operates within a private equity real estate portfolio, so there's real business context behind the work. You'll be on the front line of occupancy, greeting prospects, running tours, and walking people through community amenities and available units. You'll support local marketing efforts and contribute to social media content designed to drive traffic to the property. On the administrative side, you'll keep lead records current and accurate, which feeds directly into the leasing team's ability to follow up effectively.

Resident relations are part of the role too. You'll assist with move-ins and move-outs and support community events, which means you're managing the experience of current residents while simultaneously selling to future ones. You'll also conduct competitor market surveys, which gives you exposure to how properties are priced and positioned relative to the local Champaign market. That kind of analysis is how leasing teams inform concessions strategy and occupancy goals.

Coordination with maintenance is part of the job as well. Making sure units are make-ready and meet BAM's standards before a showing isn't glamorous, but it's fundamental. A unit that isn't properly turned before a tour can lose a lease no matter how good the pitch is.

Skills This Role Builds

This is where the internship earns its value. Strong candidates will leave with a practical understanding of the leasing lifecycle, from first contact through move-in. They'll have used real property management software, run live market analysis, and contributed to a marketing strategy. Those are transferable skills that open doors to full-time leasing consultant roles, assistant manager positions, and eventually property management roles as a career path.

What separates interns who get the most from this experience: they treat every tour as a real sales conversation, not a task to complete. They follow up on leads without being reminded. They ask questions about NOI and occupancy when they have a chance. The candidates who do that tend to get noticed.

  • Currently pursuing a degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Real Estate, or a related field
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office; able to learn property management software quickly
  • Organized, detail-oriented, and accurate with data entry
  • Flexible availability to meet property scheduling needs
  • Prior customer-facing experience preferred (retail, hospitality, or similar)
  • Interest in real estate investment and property management is a genuine plus

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
It's a Saturday afternoon, traffic is picking up, and you've got two prospects waiting in the leasing office while a current resident stops by with a maintenance question. That's a normal hour at a busy lease-up. If you can hold all of that together and still close, this role is probably a fit.

The Position at Reveal Hackensack

Berkshire Residential Investments is hiring a Leasing Consultant at Reveal Hackensack, their property in northern New Jersey. Berkshire is an owner-operator, not a third-party management shop, which means decisions move faster and there's more direct accountability at the site level. The leasing consultant here carries real responsibility for converting traffic into signed leases and keeping the resident experience intact once they move in.

The day-to-day covers what you'd expect: touring prospects, maintaining model and tour route presentation, tracking local market conditions, and staying on top of resident communications. Berkshire holds their leasing staff to a closing ratio of at least 20%, which is a reasonable benchmark and a clear signal that this isn't a purely administrative role. You're expected to sell.

Beyond the floor traffic, you'll contribute ideas to the property manager on marketing direction and resident satisfaction. That kind of input is taken seriously here. The office culture leans toward high energy and genuine hospitality, so if you're someone who goes flat after a long stretch of prospect calls, it's worth being honest with yourself about that.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of customer service experience that translates well to leasing, sales, or hospitality
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including professional resident correspondence
  • Comfort with technology and the ability to adapt as platforms change
  • Attention to detail on administrative tasks, from application processing to follow-up tracking
  • Genuine ease with people across a wide range of personalities and situations

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, personal development plans, a 25% rent discount, and a solid benefits package. Those details are worth noting because the rent discount in a market like Hackensack carries real dollar value.

One honest observation from fifteen years of watching leasing teams: the consultants who advance quickly are the ones who treat the CRM like a tool rather than a chore and who actually read the T-3 occupancy and traffic reports. Understanding why closing ratios dip in a given week, and being able to speak to it, is what separates a good leasing consultant from someone who's ready to move into an assistant manager role. Berkshire promotes from within, and this position is a legitimate starting point for that path.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - 186
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This position draws on a broad technical base. You'll work across plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and general building systems on any given day. The work isn't specialized in one trade. It's generalist maintenance done consistently well, which means your ability to diagnose quickly and execute without a lot of hand-holding matters more than depth in any single area.

Resident interaction is part of the job too. You're not just fixing things in empty units. You're communicating with people who live there, which means your customer service instincts get used as often as your tools.

What You'll Handle Day to Day

Walton Lofts is a Berkshire-owned and managed property, so standards get set in-house rather than filtered through a third-party management layer. That means accountability is direct and expectations are consistent.

  • Complete service requests across all trade categories: plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry
  • Support unit turns and make-readies, including punch list completion
  • Maintain curb appeal through regular inspections and follow-through
  • Manage shop organization, equipment upkeep, and inventory control
  • Enforce safety protocols and maintain key security procedures
  • Back up the management team in upholding property and company standards

You'll need at least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential or commercial setting. Computer proficiency is required for work order systems and documentation.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Technicians who do well in this kind of role stay ahead of the work order queue instead of just reacting to it. They notice things on property walks before residents call them in. They treat make-readies with the same attention they'd give an occupied unit repair. Berkshire operates its own portfolio, so the care you put into the physical asset has a direct connection to how the property performs. That context tends to matter to people who take their craft seriously.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, and personal development plans. They're explicit about building careers, not just filling positions.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
A resident submits a work order at 7 a.m. for a heating issue. By the time the leasing office opens, it's already resolved and closed out. That's the standard this role operates at.

Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Manager for their Mountlake Terrace, WA community. The position sits between hands-on technician work and team leadership, which makes it a genuinely useful career step. You're still diagnosing HVAC systems, troubleshooting plumbing, and handling appliance repairs yourself, but you're also modeling the work ethic and attention to detail that shapes how the rest of the maintenance team performs.

What the Role Covers

Day-to-day responsibilities run across the full maintenance spectrum. Service tickets need timely follow-up and thorough completion. The make-ready and turn process requires coordination and precision so units get back into leasable condition without delay. Preventative maintenance programs keep the asset performing well over time rather than lurching from one emergency to the next. You'll also handle grounds upkeep, safety compliance, snow removal, and the general cleanliness standards that affect how both residents and prospective renters experience the property. Weekend availability and participation in an on-call emergency rotation are part of the role. The salary range is $62,400 to $66,560, with additional bonus opportunities.

What You Bring

  • Five or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and appliance repair
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems such as boilers, chillers, split systems, or central plant equipment is a plus
  • Understanding of OSHA standards, risk management, and MSDS protocols
  • Supervisory or leadership experience, even informal mentoring, is preferred
  • Comfort with technology platforms and the Microsoft Office suite
  • Physical capability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb ladders, and work in variable outdoor conditions

What separates a strong candidate here from a capable technician who's ready to move on: the ability to hold a standard without micromanaging. Bozzuto properties carry a clear brand expectation around resident experience, and the maintenance team is central to delivering it. An assistant manager who can communicate crisply with residents, close work orders completely, and train up junior staff compounds value fast. That combination, trade depth plus people competency, is what opens the door to a full Maintenance Manager role, and from there, Regional Facilities Director tracks become realistic at larger operators.

Bozzuto offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement for ongoing development.

job.title: Bilingual Leasing Hub Associate - Sandy Springs, GA
job.description:
Centralized leasing hubs exist because scattered, community-by-community lead handling bleeds traffic and kills conversion. Cortland built this model to consolidate inbound volume, respond faster, and push qualified appointments to their onsite teams at scale. This role sits at the top of that funnel, and the throughput is real: you're working 40 to 50 leads per day across multiple communities.

This is not a traditional leasing consultant position. There's no model unit tour, no lease signing at your desk. The job is phone, email, and text, working RealPage leads and converting cold inquiries into booked appointments for Cortland properties across their portfolio. Think of it as inside sales for a top-10 multifamily operator.

What This Role Actually Requires

The volume is the first thing to internalize. Forty to fifty leads daily means you're building a rhythm fast. Slow typists, people who lose energy on repetitive outbound, or candidates who need face-to-face interaction to close won't last long here. What works is someone who treats each lead like a fresh conversion opportunity, stays organized across a high-contact queue, and communicates clearly in writing as often as by voice.

Bilingual fluency is listed as a qualification, and in the Sandy Springs and broader Atlanta metro market, that typically means English and Spanish. Spanish-speaking prospective residents are a meaningful share of the renter pool in this corridor, and the ability to build rapport in a prospect's preferred language directly affects appointment conversion rates. If that's your edge, it matters here more than in most leasing roles.

OneSite proficiency is required. L2L (Lead to Lease) experience is preferred. If you've worked in RealPage's ecosystem before, the learning curve on this platform is short.

Qualifications Worth Noting

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience, with a preference for sales backgrounds
  • Bilingual fluency (English required; second language a strong differentiator)
  • Strong written and verbal communication across multiple channels simultaneously
  • Solid computer and typing skills, given the volume of text and email outreach
  • Working knowledge of OneSite; L2L experience is a plus

What separates strong candidates here is not charm alone. It's the ability to manage lead cadence without dropping threads, adjust your pitch based on a prospect's stated needs and budget, and hand off warm appointments to onsite teams with enough context that the tour actually converts. You're not closing the lease. You're closing the visit, and that's a specific skill.

Cortland is a vertically integrated firm founded in 2005, now operating as one of the largest multifamily owners in the country. The hub model reflects how operators at their scale are rethinking leasing infrastructure: centralize the top-of-funnel work, free up onsite teams to focus on the in-person experience, and use data to track conversion at every stage. For someone building a career in multifamily, that kind of exposure to portfolio-level leasing operations, metrics, and systems is genuinely useful and not common in entry-level roles.

job.title: Property Administrator
job.description:
Commercial property administration runs on details. Purchase orders that don't get coded correctly throw off your NOI reporting. Delinquency letters that go out late push aged receivables into the 60-day column. Vendor COIs that lapse put the property at risk. This role at Lincoln Property Company in Savannah keeps all of that moving, and it demands someone who treats administrative accuracy as a genuine discipline, not a background task.

The Skills This Role Uses Every Day

Real estate accounting fluency sits at the center of this position. You'll apply tenant rents, reconcile open credits, organize and code invoices in Workspace, and compile tenant billings and miscellaneous charges. If you've worked through a monthly accounting cycle before, including A/P, A/R, and lease charge structures in a commercial context, you already understand the rhythm. MRI, Workspace, and Yardi experience will let you move faster from day one. Beyond the numbers, you'll need strong vendor coordination skills: monitoring contractor compliance, tracking certificates of insurance, and helping prepare and administer service agreements. These aren't one-time tasks. They recur every month, every quarter, every lease cycle.

Communication ties everything together. You're fielding calls from tenants, routing messages to the right people, and keeping the property management team informed with aged delinquency reports and purchase order status updates. Clarity and professionalism in every interaction matters because this role touches both the tenant-facing side and the owner-reporting side of the operation.

Responsibilities in Practice

  • Manage the full purchase order workflow: issuance, tracking, and matching POs to invoices as they process for payment
  • Run monthly reports and flag unresolved purchase orders before they create bottlenecks
  • Assist the Chief Engineer with the electrical analysis worksheet as utility invoices arrive (relevant if the property uses RUBS or direct billing structures)
  • Maintain tenant files, filing systems, and the property staff directory
  • Coordinate tenant events, including seasonal programming and community initiatives
  • Provide aged delinquency reports to the management team and send late letters on schedule
  • Support accounts payable and accounts receivable functions and assist with reporting

This is a 100% in-office position in Savannah working standard business hours. No remote or hybrid option.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Lincoln manages more than 680 million square feet of commercial space across institutional clients. At the property level, that scale means the administrative systems and reporting standards are real and enforced. Candidates who thrive in this environment already respect the monthly accounting close. They know that an uncoded invoice or a missed delinquency report doesn't just create internal noise. It affects what an owner sees on their statement. The strongest applicants will bring at least two years of commercial property management experience, genuine comfort with Yardi or MRI, and the kind of organized independence that doesn't need daily direction to stay on top of recurring deadlines. An associate's or bachelor's degree is preferred alongside the high school minimum.

If you've been in a commercial PM admin role and want to deepen your accounting and operations exposure within a well-structured platform, this position gives you direct access to the full property finance cycle.

job.title: Operations Specialist
job.description:
Asset Living runs a large third-party management portfolio across multifamily, single-family rentals, student housing, build-to-rent, and affordable housing. This Operations Specialist role sits at the corporate level, supporting senior managers who oversee that portfolio. The position can be based in Atlanta, Charlotte, or Jacksonville.

Day to day, the work splits across a few different lanes. You'll pull and review financial data on properties, including historical income and expense detail, and help prepare weekly, monthly, and quarterly reporting packages. You'll gather rent comps and market trend data from internal tools and third-party sources. You'll also handle client-facing communication, helping stakeholders understand how specific assets are performing. On top of that, there's a real administrative component: coordinating travel, fielding resident calls that come in at the corporate level, and supporting internal projects from start to finish.

The analytical side of this role is real. You're not just formatting reports. You're reviewing T-12 data, identifying trends, and presenting information in a way that helps senior leadership make decisions. Strong Excel skills matter here, and familiarity with property management platforms like MRI or One-Site will help you move faster. A background in finance, real estate, or economics is a plus, but the emphasis is on how you think and how you handle competing deadlines.

What separates a strong candidate from an average one in a role like this is the combination of financial literacy and organizational discipline. Plenty of people can run a spreadsheet. Fewer can manage a full reporting cycle across a large portfolio, stay on top of multiple projects simultaneously, and communicate clearly with both internal teams and external clients. If you've supported a regional or area manager in property management before, you already know how fast priorities shift. That experience translates directly here.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, ideally in finance, real estate, or economics
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel and PowerPoint
  • Experience with MRI, One-Site, or similar property management software is a plus
  • Solid analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines without losing accuracy or attention to detail
  • Comfortable with approximately 10% travel for property visits or internal meetings

This is a corporate support role with real exposure to portfolio-level operations across multiple asset classes. For someone early in their property management career, the visibility here into financials, client relationships, and cross-functional projects builds a foundation that can move toward asset management, regional operations, or portfolio analysis over time.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Bexley Village at Concord Mills
job.description:
Leading Maintenance at Scale

A 624-unit community with a nine-person maintenance team is a real operation. At this size, the Maintenance Supervisor role isn't just a technical job with a title attached. It's a coordination role, a quality control role, and a customer service role, all wrapped into one. Weinstein Properties has owned and operated apartment communities for over 70 years, and that kind of tenure tends to produce clear systems and genuine promotion paths for people who perform.

Bexley Village at Concord Mills sits in the Concord submarket northeast of Charlotte, a corridor that's seen consistent residential demand tied to employment and retail growth around Concord Mills. Keeping a 624-unit garden-style community performing well in that market means occupancy and NOI both depend, in part, on how fast and how cleanly your team executes turns and handles service requests.

What the Role Actually Requires

This is a hands-on supervisory position. Weinstein is specific about that. You'll work alongside your team, not just direct them. The technical baseline is real: HVAC diagnosis and repair, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, appliances, pool maintenance, and exterior structural work. EPA/CFC Universal or Type I and II certification is required before you start, not something you'll earn on the job here.

On the supervisory side, you'll coordinate daily workflows, manage vendor scheduling, oversee make-ready turns, and handle work order assignment through business software. With nine people reporting to you, your ability to triage competing priorities across a large property will matter as much as your trade skills. You'll also share on-call rotation with your teammates, and Weinstein pays a bonus for those weeks.

  • Minimum 4 years of trade experience across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and related disciplines
  • At least 1 year in a lead, assistant supervisor, or supervisor role in apartment maintenance
  • EPA/CFC certification (Type I and II or Universal) required
  • Computer proficiency for work orders, supply ordering, and communication
  • Valid driver's license, personal transportation, and your own tools

What This Role Builds

Strong candidates already know their trades cold. What separates the best applicants is the ability to run a team without micromanaging it. At 624 units, you can't be at every work order. You need to trust your team, set quality standards, and inspect results.
