Property management and resident services don't always operate in sync at every organization, but MidPen's model puts them in close contact by design. Understanding where one team's work ends and the other's begins makes you more effective in both directions.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Affordable housing compliance is its own discipline. Candidates who've worked at market-rate properties will find some of the regulatory layers unfamiliar. Experience with RealPage, income certifications, or any HUD or tax credit program gives you a head start. That said, strong administrative instincts and genuine comfort with detail can carry someone who's willing to learn the regulatory side quickly.

  • High school diploma or GED with at least one year of residential property management, customer service, or administrative experience
  • Proficiency in MS Office; RealPage experience is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Bilingual in English and Mandarin (required)
  • Organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable working independently
  • Alignment with MidPen's mission around affordable, dignified housing

Pay runs from $21.15 to $23.80 per hour based on experience. MidPen carries a full benefits package including health, dental, vision, 403(b) retirement, paid parental leave, and an education reimbursement program, among others.

For someone who wants a career path in property management, the ACM role at an affordable housing nonprofit builds a compliance foundation that transfers directly into Community Manager roles, regional positions, or even compliance specialist tracks. The regulatory knowledge you build here is genuinely hard to find and consistently in demand across the sector.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is a skill set, not just a job title. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, the Leasing Consultant role is built around three disciplines that experienced multifamily professionals recognize immediately: consultative sales, relationship management, and community representation. If you've developed any of these skills in retail, hospitality, or apartment leasing, this role gives you a place to use all three at once.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

The core of this position is converting prospect traffic into signed leases. That means you'll draw on active listening to understand what a prospect actually needs, not just what they say they're looking for. Tours aren't walkthroughs; they're guided conversations. You'll field inquiries by phone, email, and web, and your ability to follow up consistently and persuasively is what separates a full apartment from a partially occupied one.

You'll also handle the administrative side of leasing accurately: applications, verification paperwork, and move-in documentation. Attention to detail here protects the community's compliance record and sets new residents up for a smooth start. Occupancy and renewal goals are real benchmarks you'll contribute to, and monthly leasing and renewal commissions mean your results show up directly in your paycheck.

Skills This Role Builds

Hawthorne offers a defined career path program, and this role is a common entry point into assistant community manager responsibilities. The skills you develop here, including objection handling, market comp awareness, resident communication, and event coordination, transfer directly into operations-level roles. Many property management professionals who move into management trace their foundation back to time spent on the leasing floor.

You'll also build familiarity with local market positioning. Savannah's rental market has seen sustained demand driven by population growth, a strong tourism and hospitality economy, and continued interest from out-of-state renters. Knowing how to position your community against competitors in that context is a practical skill that carries into any leasing or management role you take on later.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

  • Coachability: Hawthorne has a defined service culture they call Live It. Candidates who learn it and apply it consistently outperform those who rely on instinct alone.
  • Follow-through: Most lost leases aren't lost on the tour. They're lost in the follow-up. Disciplined lead management is a real differentiator.
  • Comfort with a sales schedule: The office runs Monday through Friday with Saturday hours, and resident events may occasionally extend your week. That's standard in leasing, but worth knowing upfront.
  • Communication range: You'll need to be equally effective in person, over the phone, and in writing. One weak channel limits your conversion rate.

A high school diploma or GED is the minimum education requirement. One year of customer service or sales experience is preferred, and a valid driver's license is required. A CALP accreditation is a plus if you already have it, but it's not expected at entry. Hawthorne provides learning and development support to help you grow from where you are now.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II
job.description:
It's 7:45 AM on a Tuesday and a resident just submitted a work order for a tripped breaker and a running toilet. By 9:00, you've knocked out both, logged them, and you're already pulling a punch list on a vacant unit that needs to be make-ready before Friday's move-in. That's the rhythm of this role at Hawthorne Residential Partners' Oak Island community, Hawthorne at Pine Forest.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

As a Maintenance Technician II, you'll carry your own work order queue and handle repairs independently. That means diagnosing HVAC issues, plumbing repairs, appliance fixes, and general unit maintenance without needing a supervisor walking you through every step. Make-ready turns are a core part of the job. When a resident vacates, you're restoring that unit to Hawthorne's standards so it's ready for the next resident on time. That work directly connects to occupancy, and occupancy drives everything.

Day-to-day responsibilities also include preventative maintenance on schedule, building and common area upkeep, grounds cleanliness, and pool maintenance. You'll keep the shop organized well enough that anyone can do a quick inventory scan without digging through boxes. On-call emergency rotation is part of the deal, which is honest work but worth knowing upfront before you apply.

What Hawthorne Is Looking for

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Two years of apartment maintenance experience (preferred)
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA/HVAC certification (required)
  • CPO certification is a plus

The technical baseline matters, but so does reliability. A technician who shows up, closes work orders clean, and treats residents with genuine professionalism will outperform someone with more credentials but spotty follow-through. Hawthorne tracks resident satisfaction, and your work feeds directly into those scores.

Strong candidates at this level already know the difference between a warranty repair and a deferred maintenance item, and they don't wait to be told which is which. If you've worked at a garden-style or coastal property before, you'll recognize the grind of keeping exterior common areas and pool equipment in shape through a humid Carolina summer. That experience translates here.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus a monthly renewal bonus, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses. Benefits include free dental, medical and vision coverage, 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance. Hawthorne also offers a formal career path program with a clear progression from Technician II to Technician III, plus education reimbursement for maintenance-related training.

Standard schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you at the center of everything happening at Dover Hills Apartments. On any given day, you're fielding phone inquiries from prospects, walking tours, processing applications, and following up with a new resident to make sure their move-in went smoothly. The job blends sales, customer service, and administrative work in roughly equal measure, and no two days look the same.

You'll handle the full leasing cycle: from that first phone call or walk-in through application processing, move-in paperwork, and renewal conversations. You'll also inspect vacant units and common areas to make sure they're showing well, assist with local outreach and marketing efforts, and help plan resident events. The role reports to the property manager, who reviews and approves the paperwork you process.

One honest note: leasing work requires you to be "on" with people consistently, even on slow traffic days or when a difficult prospect walks through the door. If you find genuine energy in turning a skeptical prospect into a signed lease, this role will suit you well.

What You Bring

  • At least one year in a customer-facing sales or service role; six or more months of on-site leasing experience is preferred
  • High school diploma or equivalent required; some college coursework is a plus
  • Comfort with MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ideally some exposure to Yardi
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations, or a genuine willingness to learn them quickly
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly with lease documents and application paperwork
  • A communication style that works equally well in person, on the phone, and in writing

Context Worth Knowing

Paragon Properties is a Michigan-based company with a clear focus on long-term resident relationships and team development. They offer a structured training program, an employee recognition program, a leasing move-in bonus, and a rent discount alongside a full benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer contribution, and company-paid life and disability insurance. Starting pay is $18.50/hour, negotiable based on experience.

What separates strong candidates in this specific role isn't just sales energy. It's the ability to stay organized through a lease-up push while still delivering a personal, attentive experience to every prospect. Leasing consultants who track their own follow-up diligently, know their unit inventory cold, and treat every renewal conversation with the same care as a new lease tend to advance into assistant manager and property manager roles faster than those who focus purely on closing new traffic.

Kalamazoo has a steady rental market supported by Western Michigan University and a growing healthcare and manufacturing base, which means consistent prospect traffic across seasons. Dover Hills is a garden-style community, which typically means a mix of resident profiles and a pace that rewards relationship-building over high-volume churn tactics.

Pre-employment background check, drug screening, and physical are required before your start date.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

Maintenance technician work at a residential community is about breadth. On any given day you might be diagnosing a tripped breaker, pulling a faucet cartridge, patching drywall before a turn, and checking pool chemistry before noon. The technician who thrives here isn't a specialist in one trade. They're competent across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, and basic carpentry, and they move between those disciplines without losing momentum. Customer service matters too. Residents notice how you show up just as much as whether you fixed the problem.

Dover Hills Apartments is a Paragon Properties community in Kalamazoo. The role is a standard full-time, 40-hour-per-week position with on-call rotation included. That means after-hours calls will happen, including weekends and holidays. Paragon does pay an on-call bonus for that, which is worth noting since many operators don't structure it that way.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Make-readies will be part of your regular rhythm. Preparing units for occupancy means working through a punch list that typically includes painting, basic drywall repair, and rough carpentry alongside the mechanical checks. You'll also handle resident service requests, which at a community this size means volume and variety. Troubleshooting HVAC equipment, evaluating appliance failures, and maintaining pool and spa equipment all fall within scope.

Curb appeal and property condition reporting are part of the job too. You're expected to flag potential liabilities and propose improvements when you spot them. That kind of proactive eye is something the better technicians in this industry develop over time, and it's genuinely valued in this role.

  • 1 or more years of hands-on maintenance experience, technical school, or vocational training
  • HVAC Type II or Universal certification strongly preferred
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, and general carpentry
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • High school diploma required; trade school or college-level coursework strongly preferred
  • Ability to work outdoors across all seasons
  • Pre-employment background check, drug screen, and physical required

What's Distinctive About This Opportunity

Paragon offers a pay range up to $26 per hour depending on experience and certifications, which is competitive for the Kalamazoo market. The benefits package includes paid time off, nine company holidays, a 401(k) with employer contribution, and medical, dental, and vision coverage with a short enrollment wait. There's also a rent discount, company-paid life and disability insurance, and a tool kit provided after your first 30 days. A uniform program and quarterly team bonus round it out.

One thing worth mentioning for candidates thinking about trajectory: technicians who build out their HVAC credentials and get comfortable with turn management often move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles within a few years. Paragon has a stated training and certification program, which means the path is at least structured rather than informal. If you're already certified and have a few years behind you, this is a straightforward opportunity to land somewhere stable with a benefits package that holds up. If you're earlier in your career, the certification support is a real asset.

job.title: Floating Leasing Specialist
job.description:
This role runs on two core skills: adaptability and closing. You're not anchored to one property. You move where Hillpointe needs you, which means you have to get up to speed fast, read a new community's traffic patterns quickly, and start converting prospects without a warm-up period.

What This Role Actually Involves

Hillpointe is a Sun Belt workforce housing developer with a fully integrated model. They control everything from land acquisition through construction and asset management. That means their communities are purpose-built and consistently positioned, which helps when you're floating between sites. You're not learning a totally different product every time you move.

Day-to-day, you're covering leasing offices during lease-ups, team transitions, and high-traffic periods. You conduct tours, qualify prospects, follow up by phone, text, and email, and keep tour paths and model units presentation-ready. You'll also work weekends. That's not a footnote here. It's a regular part of the schedule.

Temporary or permanent relocation is on the table depending on where business needs land. Free rent at an assigned Hillpointe community is part of the compensation structure, subject to their internal policy.

Skills This Position Relies On

  • Leasing, sales, hospitality, or customer service background. The product changes by property; your ability to build rapport quickly doesn't.
  • Strong follow-up discipline. Leads go cold fast. Consistent outreach through multiple channels is what separates average leasing performance from strong occupancy numbers.
  • Comfort with ambiguity. You won't always have a full week to learn a new community before you're on the floor doing tours.
  • Valid driver's license and willingness to travel frequently between properties in the portfolio.
  • High school diploma or equivalent. Fair housing compliance is required and non-negotiable.

What Makes Strong Candidates Stand Out

The biggest differentiator in a floating role isn't leasing knowledge. It's how fast you can integrate. Someone who walks into a new site, reads the community's selling points, absorbs the current traffic situation, and starts producing without needing two weeks of hand-holding is the person this role is built for. Hospitality backgrounds transfer well here because that instinct to make someone feel welcome immediately is exactly what a lease-up or peak-traffic period demands.

Hillpointe's workforce housing focus also means your prospects are often practical buyers. They want to know what they're getting for the rent. Connecting features to real lifestyle value, not just reciting amenities, is a skill worth sharpening before you walk in the door.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the operational center of a residential apartment community in Centennial. Day to day, you're handling rent collection, processing payments, and managing delinquency. That means tracking late accounts, preparing notices, and following the legal timeline carefully. You're also maintaining resident files, coordinating with vendors, and supporting the leasing side of the business. When the Property Manager is out, the community runs through you.

Cottonwood Residential was an early mover on self-guided tours, which tells you something about how they approach operations. The leasing experience here isn't purely transactional. You'll be expected to think about how residents and prospects experience the property, not just process paperwork.

What You Bring

  • Background in leasing, sales, or customer service. The combination of people skills and process discipline matters here.
  • Comfort with basic accounting. You don't need to be a bookkeeper, but understanding charges, credits, and ledger entries is part of the daily rhythm.
  • Strong written and verbal communication. You're drafting formal notices and talking to residents in the same afternoon.
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing Laws. This isn't optional knowledge in a leasing environment.
  • Weekend availability. Residential communities don't pause on Saturdays.
  • Entrata Core experience is a plus. If you've worked in another property management software, the transition is manageable.

Where This Role Leads

The Assistant Property Manager title gets underestimated. In practice, it's where you build the full operational picture of a residential asset. Delinquency management, vendor coordination, resident retention, leasing support, and occasional community oversight all run through this position. People who do this job well tend to move into Property Manager roles with a real command of both the financial and human sides of a community. The accounting exposure here, even basic, compounds quickly once you're reading T-12 reports and working toward NOI goals at the manager level.

One thing worth knowing: the gap between a good APM and an average one usually comes down to follow-through on the administrative side. Resident files that stay current, delinquency that gets addressed early, vendor communication that doesn't fall through the cracks. The leasing part is visible. The backend discipline is what earns trust with a Property Manager and sets you up for the next step.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
It's 7:15 a.m. on a Monday and you've already got two HVAC calls from the weekend on-call log, a turn that needs to be punched by Wednesday, and a new tech who's still learning the ropes. That's a pretty average morning for a Maintenance Supervisor at The Orchards at Cherry Creek Park in Centennial, CO. Cottonwood Residential is looking for someone who doesn't flinch at that kind of start.

What This Role Actually Involves

You'll lead the maintenance team day to day, which means your job is equal parts hands-on technician and people manager. The make-ready process will sit squarely on your shoulders. Turns need to be tight, punch lists need to be thorough, and apartments need to be rent-ready on schedule so the leasing side can do its job. You'll also manage the full range of service tickets, HVAC troubleshooting, electrical, plumbing, and appliance repair, with the expectation that residents get timely follow-up, not just a closed ticket.

Beyond the unit-level work, you're responsible for grounds upkeep, building systems operating at peak efficiency, and keeping everything compliant with local codes and safety standards. You'll build and enforce monthly staffing schedules that guarantee 24/7 emergency coverage. That last part is real: this role carries on-call accountability, and you'll need to staff it accordingly.

Cottonwood also expects you to invest in your team. Hiring, developing, and running both on-the-job and classroom training for techs and community care associates is part of the position, not an afterthought.

What You'll Need to Bring

  • EPA certification Type II or Universal (required, non-negotiable)
  • Considerable hands-on HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • Valid driver's license
  • Demonstrated experience leading a maintenance team, not just working alongside one
  • Attention to detail on make-readies and a track record of hitting turn timelines
  • Comfort running an accident-free operation with a real understanding of safety codes

Cottonwood offers competitive pay with a bonus structure, full health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits available within the first 30 days, a 401k and HSA with company match, three weeks of PTO in your first year, and 10.5 paid holidays.

One thing worth noting for candidates coming from smaller operations: what separates strong supervisors in this role from average ones is usually the ability to coach without micromanaging. Your techs will handle a lot independently. Your job is to set the standard, check the work, and develop the people, not to be the one always holding the wrench. If you've been the best tech on a team and you're ready to grow into the leadership side of this trade, this is the kind of role that builds that foundation.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Cottonwood Residential operates The Orchards at Cherry Creek Park in Centennial, and they're looking for a maintenance technician who can handle the full range of day-to-day work that keeps a residential community running well. This isn't a light-duty posting. They need someone with real hands-on experience across plumbing, electrical, and carpentry, plus solid HVAC troubleshooting skills and an EPA Type II or Universal certification already in hand.

The Centennial submarket sits in one of the Denver metro's more competitive corridors, where resident expectations tend to run high. Communities here compete hard on condition and responsiveness, which means your work order turnaround and make-ready quality directly affect how the property performs. A technician who can knock out a tight punch list, handle a turn efficiently, and still respond professionally to a resident after hours is genuinely valuable here.

On-call coverage is part of the job. You'll rotate emergency response with the support of a Service Manager, so you're not fielding calls alone without backup, but you do need to be available and reliable when it's your rotation. That's an honest part of this role worth knowing going in.

A CPO certification isn't required but it's a real advantage if you have it. Valid driver's license is required. Physical demands are significant: lifting up to 50 lbs, working from ladders and scaffolding, and spending most of your shift on your feet or crouching in mechanical spaces.

What Cottonwood is looking for

  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • Considerable HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry repairs
  • Ability to work evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts
  • Valid driver's license
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English for work orders, safety procedures, and resident interaction
  • CPO certification (a plus, not a dealbreaker)

Cottonwood offers health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage with a quick eligibility window. You'd also get a 401k with company match, HSA match, three weeks of PTO in your first year, and 10.5 paid holidays. For maintenance professionals who've dealt with employers that treat benefits as an afterthought, that package is worth noting.

Technicians who grow in this type of role often move into lead tech or service manager positions within a few years, particularly at companies like Cottonwood that promote from within and manage multiple communities. If you're looking to build toward that track, the breadth of work here gives you the reps to get there.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
It's 7:15 a.m. and your team is already pulling work orders from overnight while you're walking the grounds, noting a gate sensor that's lagging and a pool chemical reading that needs adjusting before residents start their day. That's the rhythm of this role. Reactive and proactive, often in the same hour.

The Role at Waypoint

Waypoint Management Services is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor for a high-end luxury community in Miami, FL. This isn't a wrench-turning position with a title attached. You're running the full maintenance operation: budgets, vendors, make-ready timelines, preventive maintenance schedules, and a team that needs real leadership, not just direction.

Day-to-day, you'll own the make-ready process, coordinating with contractors to ensure units are genuinely move-in ready, not just checked off a list. You'll keep HVAC units on a preventive maintenance schedule, manage pool service and chemical readings, maintain the trash compactor, and make sure gated entrances and security equipment stay operational. Work orders get a 24-hour response, full stop. When service emergencies hit, you're the one building the corrective action plan and executing it.

The community manager is your primary partner. Strong communication between maintenance and leasing leadership is what keeps occupancy goals and service standards aligned. You'll need to hold that relationship well.

What You're Bringing

  • Prior supervisory experience leading both employees and outside vendors or contractors
  • EPA Section 608 certification (Types I and II), required at hire
  • CPO certification, or a commitment to earn it within 90 days
  • CAMT certification is preferred and signals a serious maintenance professional
  • Hands-on proficiency in plumbing, carpentry, general repairs, and HVAC troubleshooting
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards and a genuine commitment to safe operations
  • High school diploma or GED, plus at least two years of relevant maintenance experience
  • Bilingual in Spanish and English, strongly preferred given Miami's resident population
  • Willingness to carry an on-call schedule when the property needs it

Waypoint offers medical, dental, and vision coverage starting day one, a 401k with matching, an employee referral and recognition program, bonus opportunities, and an onsite housing discount for qualified employees.

One thing worth noting about this role specifically: the candidates who stand out aren't necessarily the most technically skilled. They're the ones who think about the property's physical condition the way an owner would. They catch the deferred maintenance item before it becomes a capex problem. They build a team that doesn't need to be micromanaged on turnovers because the standard is already understood. If that's how you operate, this is a role worth your attention.

From here, strong Maintenance Supervisors at luxury communities often move into Regional Maintenance Director roles or transition into facilities management at larger portfolios. The leadership and budget accountability you build in this seat transfers directly.

job.title: Part-Time Exterior Porter
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. on a Saturday. An event wrapped up the night before, and the first tenants and visitors are already moving through the lobby. Your job is to make sure they don't see a trace of what happened the evening before.

Comstock is hiring a part-time Exterior Porter for its ParkX operations in Herndon, VA. This role sits at the front line of the property experience. You're responsible for the condition of common areas across assigned sites: sidewalks, lobbies, restrooms, and public-facing spaces that tenants and guests interact with every day. That means pressure washing, window cleaning, trash removal, and routine janitorial tasks completed on schedule and to standard.

What the Work Actually Involves

You'll report to your assigned location in uniform before your shift starts, follow established cleaning checklists, and document anything that needs management attention. Safety compliance is part of the job, not an afterthought. That includes proper chemical handling, keeping storage areas organized and hazard-free, and flagging maintenance issues or damage when you spot them.

Event support is a real part of this role. Setup and breakdown for events or public gatherings will come up, and availability for weekends and after-hours during peak periods is expected. When a coworker is out, you may be called on to cover. The Senior Operations Manager, Janitorial, directs day-to-day priorities, and you'll attend team meetings that affect janitorial operations.

What Comstock Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record
  • Availability for weekend and after-hours work, especially around events
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and handle the physical demands of sustained outdoor and indoor work across variable conditions
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to self-direct with minimal supervision
  • Professional demeanor with tenants, visitors, and property staff
  • Comfort working independently and as part of a team

Benefits are available and include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, and life insurance, though specifics vary by role. Comstock also offers annual professional development funds, free parking, EV charging, and a parental leave program.

One honest note on what separates strong candidates here: it's not just physical ability. The people who do well in exterior porter roles long-term are the ones who communicate proactively. If a piece of equipment is showing wear, if a supply is running low, if something looks like it could become a bigger problem, saying something early matters more than most job descriptions let on. Property teams rely on porters as eyes on the ground, and that situational awareness compounds over time into trust and real opportunity within an organization.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a hands-on maintenance technician role at a Berkshire Residential community in Palm Valley. Your day moves fast and rarely follows a script. You're handling service requests across plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry, while also keeping an eye on curb appeal and making sure the property stays in shape between turns. You'll support the shop, manage inventory, and keep equipment and keys where they belong. Berkshire owns and manages its own assets, so there's no third-party buffer between the team and accountability. That matters in how this role actually functions day to day.

Curb appeal is real here. A well-maintained exterior signals to prospects and residents that the property is managed with care, and that starts with the tech who walks the grounds and notices what others miss. You're also a point of contact for residents, so your attitude on a work order visit carries weight. A quick, professional interaction goes a long way toward reducing delinquency headaches down the line by keeping residents satisfied and renewing.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across the core trades: appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building maintenance
  • Ability to communicate clearly in English, written and verbal
  • Comfort with computers and basic property management software for work order tracking
  • A general awareness of safety protocols and willingness to enforce them on site

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Berkshire operates its own portfolio rather than managing for outside owners, which typically means more consistent standards and less of the budget uncertainty that comes with fee management arrangements. The trade-off is that expectations are high and there's real ownership over outcomes. You're not just executing work orders. You're contributing to the physical condition of an asset that Berkshire has a direct stake in.

What separates a strong maintenance tech from an average one at a community like this isn't just technical skill. It's reliability, follow-through on punch list items, and the ability to read urgency correctly. A flooded unit and a dripping faucet are not the same emergency. Techs who triage well and communicate clearly with the office team make everyone's job easier and tend to move up. This kind of role can lead naturally into a lead tech or maintenance supervisor position as you build experience across more complex systems and start mentoring newer staff.

Berkshire does offer a 25% rent discount, three weeks of vacation, and personal development plans, which is worth noting because that package is above average for a maintenance-level role in this industry.

job.title: Sales & Resident Experience Consultant
job.description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

Leasing is a numbers game, and the best consultants know it. At Estancia Townhomes, you're expected to close at least 20% of your traffic. That means every tour, every follow-up call, every email thread has a measurable outcome attached to it. If you naturally track your own ratios and ask yourself why a prospect didn't convert, you already think the way this role demands.

The other skill that runs through everything here is communication. Not just being friendly, though that matters. It's the ability to shift your approach depending on who's in front of you, write a follow-up that actually gets a response, and handle a resident concern without letting it spiral. Berkshire calls themselves people-first, and at the leasing desk, that philosophy shows up in real time, every single day.

What You're Actually Doing Day to Day

Your mornings might start with walking your tour route and model units before the first appointment. Punch-list thinking applies here: scuffed baseboard, burned-out bulb, a door that sticks. These details read as signals to prospects about how the property is run, and a sharp leasing consultant treats the model like a product on a shelf.

From there, the day fills in around people. Prospective residents coming in or calling, current residents with questions or concerns, your property manager needing input on a marketing idea. You're also expected to stay current on what competing communities are doing with pricing and concessions, because local market awareness directly shapes how you position Estancia in a conversation.

  • Guide prospects through tours and apply genuine sales technique to move them toward a decision
  • Maintain a closing ratio of at least 20% on qualified traffic
  • Keep leasing office and tour routes professionally presented at all times
  • Handle resident communications with accuracy and a consistent, professional tone
  • Monitor local market conditions and contribute ideas that support occupancy and resident satisfaction
  • Bring two or more years of customer service or sales experience to the role

What Makes Someone Stand Out Here

Two candidates can both be warm and personable. What separates a good leasing consultant from a great one is follow-through. The prospect who toured on Saturday and hasn't responded to your email by Tuesday needs a second touch, a different angle, something that earns a reply. The candidates who thrive at Berkshire are the ones who treat their pipeline with the same attention a sales rep would, not just waiting for the next walk-in but actively working the ones they already have.

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means the leasing team operates with a level of accountability that third-party management setups sometimes dilute. You're not leasing for a client. You're leasing for the owner, which tends to sharpen the feedback loop between your performance and what actually matters to the business.

job.title: Overnight Concierge
job.description:
Bozzuto runs some of the most well-regarded residential communities on the East Coast, and the overnight concierge position at their Arlington property is a good example of why their buildings hold together the way they do. This is a Monday through Friday, 11PM to 7AM role. The building doesn't sleep, and neither does the standard of service.

The overnight shift carries its own rhythm. Foot traffic drops, but the moments that happen at 2AM or 6AM matter just as much as anything during peak leasing hours. You're the person a resident sees when they come home from a late flight. You're the one who notices a package was left in the wrong spot before the morning rush. You catch the things the day shift doesn't get to. That kind of quiet ownership is exactly what Bozzuto is looking for here.

The role itself covers a real range. You'll manage front desk operations, keep package rooms organized (holiday seasons bring serious volume), handle club room and freight elevator reservations, and build genuine relationships with residents over time. That last part isn't filler. Bozzuto places real weight on knowing residents by name, knowing their routines, and personalizing interactions in ways that build actual loyalty. Happy residents write reviews. They renew. That's the connection between this role and the property's long-term performance.

There's also a social media component. You'll help generate awareness and excitement for the community online and encourage satisfied residents to share their experiences publicly. If you've worked in hospitality or hotel operations, this will feel familiar. The front desk is the brand.

What makes a strong candidate here

The overnight shift self-selects for a certain kind of person. You need to be genuinely comfortable working independently for long stretches, staying sharp at 4AM, and making a tired resident feel welcome without it feeling performative. Two or more years in hospitality, retail, or hotel environments is the baseline. Strong written and verbal communication matters more on this shift than most, because you're often the only point of contact available. Comfort with software, apps, and building management tools is expected.

  • 2+ years in hospitality, hotel, travel, or retail service
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfortable with software, apps, and standard computer programs
  • Detail-oriented with a genuine instinct for anticipating resident needs
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds
  • Professional appearance and demeanor throughout the full shift

Compensation sits at approximately $23.08 to $23.56 per hour, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. Bozzuto is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

job.title: Front Door Waste Technician-Cortland Peachtree Battle
job.description:
Valet trash service has become a standard amenity at Class A multifamily communities, and keeping it running well depends entirely on the person doing the work. This role at Cortland's Peachtree Battle community puts you at the center of that operation, collecting resident waste on a nightly route and maintaining the cleanliness standards that directly affect resident satisfaction scores and renewal rates.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Each shift, you'll walk the property route, including stairwells, collecting resident waste bags left at doorsteps and transferring them into leak-proof carts for transport to onsite compactors or containers. Beyond the door-to-door collection, you're responsible for clearing dog waste stations, pool areas, mail kiosks, and other common spaces. You'll also handle spills and debris around compactor areas, monitor for prohibited waste items, and document your work through a mobile app, logging start and end times and capturing photos as required.

The physical side of this job is real. You're walking long distances, climbing stairs, lifting up to 50 lbs, and working outdoors regardless of weather. Strong odors come with the territory. If you've done waste services, custodial work, or any physically demanding outdoor role before, you already know what to expect.

You'll also interact with residents and staff regularly. That part matters more than people assume. A valet trash technician who communicates well and handles complaints professionally protects the community's reputation in ways that show up directly in resident satisfaction.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

Cortland is looking for candidates with at least one year of experience in waste services or a customer-facing role, working knowledge of EPA and OSHA safety standards, and a valid Class E driver's license. A high school diploma or equivalent is preferred. You'll need a personal smartphone (Android or iPhone) with a data plan for daily documentation.

  • At least one year in waste services or a customer-service-focused position
  • Familiarity with EPA and OSHA regulations related to waste handling
  • Ability to drive locally as needed
  • Physical capacity to climb stairs, walk extended routes, and lift 50 lbs
  • Bilingual ability is a plus but not required

What this role builds is worth noting. Technicians who perform well here develop a real understanding of how a multifamily property functions from the ground up. You learn the physical layout, the resident-facing service standards, and the reporting systems Cortland uses across its portfolio. That operational familiarity, combined with a track record of reliability, is exactly what grounds maintenance leads and property service coordinators are made of. Strong performers in roles like this one tend to move into broader facilities or maintenance support positions over time.

Cortland is a vertically integrated operator with in-house construction, design, and management, which means internal mobility is a real part of how the company grows its people. Showing up consistently, communicating well, and completing routes efficiently puts you in a position to be noticed.

job.title: Regional Vice President, Affordable Housing
job.description:
Asset Living has been in third-party fee management since 1986, and their affordable housing footprint is a serious operation. This isn't a title bump for someone who's managed a handful of tax credit sites. The Regional Vice President of Affordable Housing is a true senior leadership role, sitting above Regional Managers and carrying direct accountability for both operational performance and client retention across a multi-state portfolio.

The affordable housing side of this business carries compliance weight that conventional multifamily simply doesn't. LIHTC application processes, annual recertification timelines, Section 8 contract requirements, physical inspections with regulatory agencies , these aren't checkbox items here. They're central to the job. If you've spent your career in market-rate and you're thinking this is a lateral move with a different resident profile, it's worth reconsidering. The RVP owns the compliance culture across their region, and that starts with knowing the rules cold and making sure Regional Managers do too.

On any given week, this person is probably reviewing a budget variance with a Regional Manager in one city, joining a client call with an ownership group in another, and prepping for an agency inspection at a third property. The 25 to 50 percent travel estimate is real. This role is not desk-bound, and the clients Asset Living serves in affordable housing tend to have specific reporting expectations tied to regulatory funding sources. Keeping those relationships tight is part of the job description and part of what protects the portfolio.

What separates strong candidates from average ones at this level isn't just compliance knowledge. It's the ability to develop Regional Managers who are stretched thin and still hit their operational targets. The best RVPs we've seen in affordable housing are the ones who can walk a site, spot a file problem before an auditor does, then pivot to a board presentation the same afternoon without missing a beat.

What You'll Bring

  • Direct experience as a Regional Manager in affordable housing, specifically LIHTC and/or Section 8 portfolios
  • Comfort with regulatory agency relationships, file audits, and recertification compliance at scale
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and hold accountable a team of Regional Managers across multiple markets
  • Budgeting and financial reporting experience at the regional level
  • Strong client-facing presence, including business reviews and ownership group communication
  • Relevant certifications (HCCP, COS, TCS, CPM, CAPS) are meaningful here, not just nice-to-have
  • Bachelor's degree preferred, but real operational experience carries weight

Miami is the base, but the role is regional in scope. If you've built a career managing the intersection of regulatory compliance and operational performance in affordable housing and you're ready to do that at a larger scale under a nationally recognized third-party platform, this is a role worth looking at closely.

job.title: Maintenance Assistant Supervisor
job.description:
Weinstein Properties runs a vertically integrated operation: they own and manage everything in-house, which means the maintenance team isn't answering to a third-party owner who's never set foot on the property. That kind of structure changes the job. Decisions get made faster, there's real accountability at the property level, and technicians who perform well tend to grow within the company rather than get lost in a corporate shuffle.

This Maintenance Assistant Supervisor role covers properties in the South Charlotte and Concord areas. It's a working supervisory position, meaning you're not just reviewing work orders from a desk. You're in the field turning wrenches alongside your team, diagnosing HVAC issues, handling plumbing calls, running electrical repairs, and doing the full range of building maintenance work that keeps units occupied and residents satisfied. At the same time, you're helping coordinate the service team's schedule, assisting with vendor oversight, and making sure turns get completed on time and to standard.

The technical bar here is real. Weinstein requires EPA/CFC certification (Type I and II or Universal), hands-on HVAC repair experience, and a working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, pool maintenance, carpentry, drywall, and appliance repair. You'll also need to be comfortable with the software side: assigning and tracking work orders, scheduling, ordering supplies, and communicating through email. Four years of trade experience is the minimum, with at least one of those years spent in a lead, assistant supervisor, or supervisory capacity in apartment maintenance specifically.

On-call rotation is part of the role. That's worth saying plainly because it's a real commitment. The on-call bonus structure (a flat $150 per week regardless of call volume, plus extra for holidays) reflects that Weinstein takes it seriously as a working condition, not just a footnote.

What Separates Strong Candidates

The technicians who thrive in assistant supervisor roles like this one tend to be strong communicators as much as strong tradespeople. You're the link between residents who are frustrated and a team that's stretched. You'll interact with people who are upset about a broken AC in August, vendors who don't show on time, and a supervisor who needs accurate updates. The ability to stay calm, set realistic expectations, and follow through consistently matters as much as your HVAC certification.

  • Minimum 4 years of trade experience in apartment or residential maintenance
  • At least 1 year in a lead, assistant supervisor, or supervisory role in multifamily maintenance
  • EPA/CFC Refrigerant certification required (Type I and II or Universal)
  • Hands-on HVAC diagnostic and repair experience
  • Proficiency with work order software and basic computer tasks
  • Valid driver's license, personal transportation, and personal tools
  • Willingness to participate in on-call rotation
  • Background check and DMV review required

Starting pay is $25 per hour depending on experience, with quarterly performance bonuses, on-call pay, insurance, vacation and sick time, a rent discount, and a 401(k) with company match.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
It's 7:45 on a Monday morning and you're already walking the grounds before the office opens, mentally building your work order priority list before your team even clocks in. That's the job. If that sounds like your normal, keep reading.

The Role at Bexley Village at Concord Mills

Weinstein Properties is a family-owned operator with more than 70 years in the business and a portfolio of over 60 communities across the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic. They own and manage everything in-house, which matters more than people realize. There's no third-party management layer, no fee compression politics, and decisions get made by people who actually know the properties. That kind of structure tends to produce real stability for maintenance staff.

This Maintenance Supervisor position at their Concord, NC community is a working supervisor role. You're not just scheduling and delegating. You're turning wrenches alongside your team, diagnosing HVAC issues, handling electrical and plumbing repairs, managing pool maintenance, and working through the full range of make-ready punch list items between turns. You'll also coordinate vendor scheduling when outside work is needed and share on-call rotation with teammates (with a bonus paid when you're carrying the phone).

Keeping occupancy strong and rents maximized depends directly on how tight the service operation runs. That's on you. Quality control, inventory management, work order tracking through business software, and making sure the team follows proper maintenance practices. It's a full plate.

What Weinstein Is Looking For

  • Minimum 4 years of trade experience, with at least 1 year in an apartment maintenance lead, assistant supervisor, or supervisor role
  • EPA/CFC certification required (Type I and II, or Universal)
  • Solid hands-on knowledge across HVAC, electrical, plumbing, appliances, carpentry, drywall, and exterior repairs
  • Comfortable using software to manage work orders, schedule turns, and communicate with the team
  • Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and your own tools
  • Willingness to participate in on-call rotation

A background and DMV check will be conducted. A $3,000 sign-on bonus is available; details are discussed during the interview process.

One thing that separates strong candidates here: the ability to shift between technical work and team leadership without dropping either. Plenty of techs can fix things. Fewer can run a tight service team, keep delinquent work orders from stacking up, and still step in personally when a unit needs to turn fast. That combination is what this role actually requires.

Weinstein promotes from within and offers training for those who want to grow. For a Maintenance Supervisor with ambitions beyond the wrench, a clear path toward Service Director or regional facilities roles exists within an ownership group that's been doing this for seven decades.

job.title: Leasing Manager - 3300 Tamarac
job.description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

Leasing is sales. Anyone who tells you otherwise hasn't worked a busy Saturday with four prospects waiting and a phone that won't stop ringing. This Leasing Manager position at MG Properties' 3300 Tamarac community in Denver runs on a specific combination of skills: closing ability, file discipline, and the kind of steady customer service instinct that keeps renewals strong and delinquency low. If you're missing any one of those three, the role gets hard fast.

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. That's not a footnote. It means there are systems, processes, and a promote-from-within culture that actually functions because the company has had enough time to build it intentionally. This isn't a startup figuring things out.

What You're Actually Doing Day to Day

Your sales skills are on display from the moment a prospect walks in. You're qualifying applicants thoroughly, guiding them through the leasing process, and preparing and executing lease signings. That last part matters more than people think. A sloppy lease signing creates problems that follow a resident through their entire tenancy.

Your organizational discipline shows up in the file work. Rental data entry needs to be accurate, files need to be current, and monthly administrative tasks need to get done even when traffic is heavy and you're short-staffed. In our industry, the leasing office that lets paperwork slide is usually the same one with compliance headaches six months later.

Your customer service instincts carry the resident-facing side of the job. You're handling maintenance complaints, working toward timely rent collection, and generally being the human face of the community. You'll also assist in training and overseeing the leasing team, which means your judgment and habits become their habits. That's worth taking seriously.

Coordination with maintenance is part of the role too, specifically around move-ins. A smooth turn and make-ready process doesn't happen by accident. It happens because leasing and maintenance communicate early and clearly.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Two years of property management experience is preferred, and that baseline matters. But what actually separates a good candidate from a great one at this level is file accuracy under pressure. Anyone can be charming on a tour. The leasing managers who move up are the ones who keep the back-office work clean when the front office is chaotic.

  • Genuine sales instinct, not just friendliness
  • Comfort training and correcting junior leasing staff without making it awkward
  • Attention to detail on lease documents and applicant qualification
  • Professional communication with residents when situations get tense
  • Reliability on administrative follow-through, not just the high-visibility stuff

Compensation runs $25 to $27 per hour, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid holidays, sick time, and rental discounts. This position is expected to be filled in June 2026.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - North Pointe Apartments
job.description:
Apartment maintenance teams carry the day-to-day condition of a property. When service requests pile up, turns stall, or an HVAC unit fails on a hot weekend, the maintenance tech is the person who keeps everything from unraveling. MG Properties is filling that role at North Pointe Apartments in Vacaville, CA.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a full-trades position. You're handling plumbing, electrical, appliance repairs, painting, and general upkeep across a community. Grounds and common areas need regular attention. Service requests come in daily and you're expected to close them out. Apartment turns are part of the cycle too: punch list work, make-ready prep, getting units back online for occupancy.

On-call rotation is part of the job. Emergency calls happen after hours. That's the honest reality of apartment maintenance, and it matters that you go in knowing it.

MG Properties has been operating across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, acquiring, developing, and managing multifamily communities. This isn't a startup figuring out its systems. There are processes in place.

What You Need to Bring

  • At least 2 years of apartment maintenance experience, ideally on a property of 200 units or more
  • Working knowledge across trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and appliances
  • Reliable transportation (required, not optional)
  • Availability for on-call rotation
  • A customer service mindset. Residents notice how you communicate, not just how fast you fix things.

Pay runs $25 to $26 per hour depending on experience. The package includes monthly bonuses, company profit sharing, 401k with employer match, medical/dental/vision, PTO, paid holidays, and rental discounts.

What separates a strong candidate here isn't just technical range. It's the combination of trade skills and the ability to interact with residents professionally under pressure. Techs who treat every service request as a customer interaction, not just a task, tend to stand out on teams like this.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing leasing is its own category. The residents are younger, the parents are often part of the conversation, and the leasing calendar runs on an academic cycle that doesn't care about your holiday plans. The Experience Team Member role at The Scion Group's Village at Muller Park in Bloomington is built around all of that.

What This Role Actually Involves

The title says "leasing consultant" but the job is closer to a hybrid of sales, community ambassador, and front-desk operations. You'll tour prospects, field questions from future residents and their families, help push leasing initiatives, and support social media content. That's the visible part. The less glamorous side includes logging packages, keeping the office and amenity spaces presentable, following up on maintenance requests, and covering after-hours lockout calls on a rotating basis. Those after-hours duties are real, so if your schedule can't flex around an occasional evening call, this isn't the right fit.

Bloomington is a college town built around Indiana University, which means the leasing cycle here is intense and predictable in equal measure. Traffic spikes in fall and early spring. Turn season, when hundreds of residents move out and new ones move in within a compressed window, is the hardest stretch of the year. Scion expects this role to be present and functional during all of it, including summers and holidays when other people are off.

Who Does Well Here

Strong candidates in this kind of role aren't just friendly. They're organized under pressure, comfortable switching between a sales conversation and a package log in the same hour, and genuinely good at communicating with a wide range of people, from an anxious 18-year-old moving out of home for the first time to a parent calling with lease questions. If you need a rigid daily routine to feel productive, leasing in student housing will test you.

  • Customer-first mindset with real follow-through, not just warmth
  • Comfortable working daytime business hours plus an on-call rotation
  • Available during Turn, summer, and holidays
  • Strong written and verbal communication across platforms
  • Self-directed and reliable without needing constant supervision
  • Eligible to work in the U.S. (visa sponsorship is not available)

Where This Can Take You

ETM roles at student housing companies like Scion tend to be genuine on-ramps. People who perform here often move into assistant manager or leasing manager positions within a few years, with exposure to full-cycle leasing operations, marketing, and resident relations already on their resume. The skills you build, reading traffic patterns, handling objections, coordinating with maintenance, supporting Turn logistics, transfer cleanly into conventional multifamily roles too if you ever want to move in that direction. It's a real start, not just a stopgap.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager - $3,500 Sign-On Bonus
job.description:
It's 11 PM on a Tuesday and your phone rings. A boiler issue in one of the units. You're not surprised, and you're not rattled. You already know the system well enough to troubleshoot it before you even arrive on site. That's the kind of person Bozzuto is looking for in this role.

What This Job Actually Is

Bozzuto manages high-quality residential communities, and this Assistant Maintenance Manager position sits at the intersection of hands-on trades work and frontline leadership. The property is in Boston's 02115 zip code, which puts you in a dense, urban environment with the kind of complex mechanical infrastructure that goes with it. Think central plant, boilers, chillers, and split systems rather than simple package units. If you've only worked garden-style properties with straightforward HVAC setups, this one will stretch you.

Day to day, you're splitting your time between working the trades yourself and keeping the maintenance team moving. You'll resolve HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance issues. You'll own the turn process, making sure make-readies are completed thoroughly and on schedule so units get back online and leased. You'll run preventative maintenance programs that protect the building's long-term value, and you'll keep the grounds, common areas, and building systems operating cleanly and safely. Weekends are part of the schedule, and the on-call rotation is real.

Bozzuto places genuine weight on resident follow-through. Closing out a service ticket isn't just a paperwork task here. Residents notice when someone circles back to confirm the repair held, and that's the standard the team is held to.

What You Need to Bring

  • At least 5 years of experience in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of OSHA standards, risk management, and MSDS protocols
  • Demonstrated proficiency across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems (boilers, chillers, central plant) is a real plus
  • Supervisory or leadership experience, even informal team lead experience counts
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb ladders, and work in varying weather

The candidates who stand out here aren't just technically sharp. They're the ones who can walk a junior tech through a repair without taking over, who document their work cleanly, and who treat a resident's service request with the same urgency they'd want if it were their own home. That combination of trade competence and interpersonal steadiness is harder to find than either skill alone.

The salary range runs from $65,000 to $70,000, and the role comes with a $3,500 sign-on bonus. Bozzuto offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement. Additional bonus opportunities are also on the table.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
A prospective resident fills out an online form at 11pm. By the time they're checking email the next morning, you've already followed up with a personalized note about the community. That's the rhythm of this role.

What This Job Actually Involves

Bozzuto is hiring a Leasing Consultant at their Santa Clara, CA community. The core of the job is converting interest into signed leases. That means following up with every lead, conducting tours that feel personal rather than scripted, and staying consistent enough with the resident experience that people tell their friends.

You'll also manage social media presence for the community. Think Instagram and Facebook content that reflects the property's personality, not just stock photos and generic captions. This is a sales role with a marketing component built in.

The schedule runs three weekends per month, with two weekdays off in exchange. Weekends are when traffic peaks, so that's when the role earns its value.

Base salary runs $48,000 to $52,000 annually, with additional bonus opportunities on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

What Bozzuto Expects From You

  • Strong written and verbal communication. You're often the first human voice a prospect hears.
  • Comfort with social media platforms, specifically Facebook and Instagram, and an ability to create content that actually gets attention
  • A sales instinct. You can read what a prospect needs and adjust your approach accordingly.
  • Professional presentation. Bozzuto operates in a premium space; appearance and demeanor reflect the brand.
  • Competency with software, apps, and general tech tools used in leasing operations

What separates strong candidates here is follow-through. Average leasing consultants give a good tour. Strong ones follow up the same day, answer questions before the prospect thinks to ask them, and keep the relationship warm through the application process. Santa Clara's rental market is competitive, and prospects are often comparing several communities at once. The consultants who close are the ones who stay in the conversation longest.

This role is a common entry point into property management careers. Leasing consultants who perform well often move into Assistant Community Manager roles, which brings exposure to financials, delinquency, and operations. It's a practical foundation for anyone who wants to manage a property rather than just lease it.

job.title: Front Door Waste Technician-Cortland at the Village
job.description:
Cortland is one of the largest vertically integrated multifamily operators in the country, and they run their communities with a level of operational discipline that filters all the way down to the site level. This Front Door Waste Technician role at Cortland at the Village is a ground-level position in the most literal sense, and it's also one of the more resident-facing jobs on any property team.

The core of the work is valet trash service. Each shift, you'll walk assigned routes through the community, collecting waste bags left outside resident doors, loading them into leak-proof carts, and transferring everything to onsite compactors or containers. You're also keeping common areas clean: dog waste stations, pool decks, mail kiosks, parking lots, and compactor pads all fall within your scope. Routes include stairs, and the job requires consistent physical output, so this isn't a role where pace varies much from day to day.

Beyond the physical work, there's a reporting component that matters. You'll log start and end times, document your route with photos, and submit everything through a mobile app. Cortland tracks productivity at the community level, so completing your route efficiently and accurately isn't optional. If you spot improper waste or safety hazards, you're expected to flag them and take appropriate action, not just walk past.

Resident interaction is part of the job too. You're on the property during evening and early morning hours when residents are home, and how you carry yourself in those moments reflects on the community. Professionalism and consistent communication with both residents and site staff are genuine expectations here, not filler language.

What this role requires

  • High school diploma or equivalent (preferred)
  • At least one year in waste services or a customer-facing role
  • Working knowledge of EPA and OSHA safety standards related to waste handling
  • Physical ability to climb stairs, walk extended distances, and lift up to 50 lbs
  • Comfort working outdoors in all weather conditions, including exposure to strong odors
  • Valid Class E driver's license for local driving as needed
  • Personal smartphone (Android 2.2 or higher, or iPhone iOS 4.3 or higher) with an active data plan for route documentation
  • Bilingual ability is a plus

What separates strong candidates in this role isn't just physical capability. It's reliability and attention to detail. Valet trash services live and die on consistency. Residents notice immediately when a bag is skipped or a compactor area is left messy. If you show up on time, complete your route thoroughly, and communicate clearly when something is off, you'll stand out on any Cortland property. That kind of dependability also opens doors to broader porter and maintenance roles within the company over time.

job.title: Front Door Waste Technician-Cortland Duluth
job.description:
It's 8 p.m. on a Wednesday and you're working a valet trash route, moving from building to building, collecting bagged waste from resident doorsteps before it becomes anyone's problem. That's the core of this role. It's physical, it's consistent, and it matters more to resident satisfaction than most people expect.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Cortland is hiring a Front Door Waste Technician for their Duluth community. This is a valet trash position, which means you're running scheduled collection routes through the property, picking up resident waste bags from doorsteps, loading them into leak-proof carts and hampers, and transferring everything to onsite compactors or containers. You'll also keep common areas clean: pool decks, dog waste stations, mail kiosks, parking lots, and compactor pads all fall within your scope.

Beyond the physical collection work, you're expected to flag improper or prohibited waste, clean spills as you find them, and interact professionally with residents and staff throughout your shift. Documentation matters here. You'll log start and end times and submit photo-supported reports through a mobile app, so comfort with a smartphone is a real requirement, not an afterthought.

The role also requires a valid Class E driver's license, the ability to lift up to 50 lbs, climb stairs, and work outdoors in all weather. If strong odors are a dealbreaker, this one isn't the right fit. That's worth saying plainly.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent (preferred)
  • At least one year in waste services or a customer-facing role
  • Working knowledge of EPA and OSHA regulations around waste handling
  • Clear, professional communication with residents and on-site staff
  • Bilingual ability is a plus
  • Ability to follow written instructions and operate basic equipment
  • Personal smartphone (Android 2.2+ or iPhone iOS 4.3+) with an active data plan and email
  • Valid Class E driver's license

Cortland is a vertically integrated multifamily owner-operator, one of the larger ones in the country, which means their properties tend to run with more structure and more accountability than you'd find at a smaller management shop. Routes have productivity standards. Reporting is tracked. That's not a complaint, just context. If you do the job well and consistently, there's a real organization behind this role.

One thing worth noting for candidates coming from general labor or service backgrounds: valet trash on a Class A multifamily property is resident-facing work. You're the person residents see on their doorstep several nights a week. How you carry yourself on the route directly affects how the community feels to the people living there. The best candidates in this type of role treat it like a service job, not just a labor job.

job.title: Accounting Assistant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the intersection of property accounting and building administration, which means your day pulls in two directions at once. On the accounting side, you're coding and entering invoices in MRI or Yardi Voyager, posting tenant receipts, verifying monthly rents, distributing rent statements, and compiling the closing reports that keep the management team honest about where the numbers stand. New vendor setups, cash verifications, monthly reporting packages. It's detail work, and the margin for error is small.

On the administrative side, you're the connective tissue of the building office. You answer phones, manage lease and building files, maintain tenant and emergency contact lists, track certificates of insurance for both tenants and vendors (including renewal dates and coverage requirements), and handle amenity requests like fitness center memberships and bike room access. You'll also coordinate after-hours vendor access, which means confirming insurance is current and making sure building staff have everything they need before anyone shows up at an odd hour.

This is a fully in-office position in Boston. No hybrid schedule, no remote option. That's worth knowing up front.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma required; some accounting coursework or experience is a genuine advantage
  • Familiarity with MRI, Yardi Voyager, or comparable property management software is helpful, though not required
  • Solid Microsoft Office skills, particularly Word and Excel
  • Strong written and verbal communication. You'll be in contact with tenants, vendors, and internal staff regularly
  • Organized enough to track COI expirations, manage multiple file systems, and juggle accounting tasks without things slipping
  • Comfortable occasionally working beyond standard hours when the building or reporting cycle demands it

A Few Things Worth Knowing

The COI tracking piece deserves more attention than most postings give it. Keeping current certificates on file for every active vendor and tenant, and following up when coverage lapses or expires, is one of those tasks that feels administrative until something goes wrong. If you're meticulous about that kind of detail, you'll be genuinely useful here.

For someone early in a property management career, this type of role builds a practical foundation that transfers well. You'll touch accounts payable workflows, tenant billing, vendor management, and lease file administration all at once. Those are skills that show up on the job description for property accountant, assistant property manager, and building administrator roles alike. Lincoln Property Company operates across a large commercial portfolio, so internal mobility is a realistic consideration for someone who performs well and wants to grow.

Pay is $31 to $36 per hour. Lincoln Property Company is one of the larger private real estate operators in the country, with a portfolio that spans commercial, office, life science, and mixed-use assets.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
What This Role Demands From Day One

Regional management is fundamentally a coordination role. You're not turning units yourself or sitting at a leasing desk, but you're accountable for everything that happens at both. The skills this position draws on most heavily are financial analysis, personnel development, and the ability to hold multiple sites to a consistent standard without being physically present at any of them on a given day. If you're someone who can read a T-12, spot a delinquency trend before it compounds, and also have a direct conversation with a Community Manager who's struggling with team morale, this role is built for that range.

Asset Living is a third-party management firm, which shapes this role in a specific way. You're not managing assets on behalf of an internal owner. You're the face of the company to external ownership groups, which means your financial reporting, your property inspections, and your staff decisions all carry client relationship weight. That's a different kind of pressure than in-house management, and it's worth understanding before you step into it.

What You'll Actually Be Managing

The portfolio spans multifamily, single-family rentals, affordable housing, build-to-rent, and student housing, so the operational mix across your sites may not be uniform. That breadth is genuinely interesting if you've worked across asset classes, but it also means you can't rely on one playbook for every property.

  • Personnel: recruiting, training, coaching, and when necessary, terminating on-site staff. You'll approve timesheets, sign off on salary requests, and work closely with HR to document performance issues correctly.
  • Financial oversight: building and monitoring operating budgets, reviewing monthly income and expense variances, flagging capex needs, and ensuring ownership reports go out accurately and on time.
  • Leasing strategy: developing annual marketing plans, evaluating staff leasing effectiveness, and stepping in on resident satisfaction issues that escalate beyond the site level.
  • Administrative and maintenance accountability: regular property inspections, service request turnaround monitoring, vendor contract oversight, and emergency response coordination.

NOI improvement is a core expectation here. You'll be expected to identify where revenue is being left on the table and where expenses are running above budget, then recommend concrete adjustments, not just flag the variance.

What Separates Strong Candidates From Average Ones

The Regional Managers who thrive in third-party management tend to be people who can compartmentalize well. You might spend the morning reviewing a budget forecast for a Class B garden-style community and the afternoon walking a punch list at a build-to-rent site with a completely different ownership expectation. The ability to shift context without losing rigor is underrated in this role.

Strong candidates also know how to develop Community Managers rather than just manage around them. The on-site team is your primary execution layer. If you're consistently filling gaps yourself instead of building capability in the people below you, the role becomes unsustainable. The best Regional Managers are coaches first and operators second.

Asset Living holds IREM's Accredited Management Organization designation and has ranked in the NMHC top 50. That reputation matters to ownership groups when they're choosing a management partner, and it creates a real standard you'll be expected to uphold across your portfolio. This isn't a role where average performance stays quiet for long.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Olympus at The Woodlands
job.description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

Assistant Manager work is really two jobs running in parallel. You're keeping the financial side clean, collections current, and records accurate while also staying visible to residents and backing up your leasing team when traffic picks up.
