The skills this position uses hardest are financial accountability, resident communication, and operational follow-through. If any one of those three is weak, the property feels it quickly.

At Olympus at The Woodlands, you'll be the person who makes sure rent is collected and deposited before bank close each day, that move-out account statements go out promptly, and that the office files stay organized and confidential. On the delinquency side, you're not just running reports. You're actively managing the process and escalating appropriately when legal or liability issues surface. The Business Manager leans on you to hold things together during absences, so you need to be comfortable stepping into that decision-making seat without a lot of notice.

The leasing piece is real here, not just a checkbox. You'll jump in to show apartments and support resident retention, which means you need to read a prospect quickly and adjust your approach. Community events and the first weekend of each month require schedule flexibility, so if your availability is rigid, this probably isn't the right fit.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

A typical morning might start with pulling delinquency numbers, following up on outstanding balances, and checking whether make-ready units are actually ready for their move-in dates. Punch list items have a way of appearing at inconvenient times. By midday you could be handling a resident complaint that needs to be resolved before it becomes a formal issue, and by afternoon you're helping a leasing consultant close a prospect who came in without an appointment. Knowing the submarket matters here. The Woodlands is a competitive corridor, and staying current on new construction activity and nearby hiring trends gives you real context when you're talking to prospects about why your community makes sense for them.

RealPage and Onsite experience will make your first few weeks considerably less painful. Olympus uses these platforms for operations, so if you've worked in them before, you can focus on learning the property rather than learning the software at the same time.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

We've seen plenty of leasing consultants cross-train into assistant manager roles and struggle with the financial discipline side. The candidates who do well in this role tend to be the ones who are already comfortable with collections conversations, can read a T-12 without needing it explained, and don't treat the accounting functions as someone else's problem. Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained leasing consultant is required, and that background genuinely shows in how quickly someone gets productive here.

  • Onsite apartment community experience as an Assistant Manager or cross-trained Leasing Consultant
  • RealPage, Knock, or Onsite software experience (strongly preferred)
  • Comfort managing collections, deposits, and move-out dispositions
  • Ability to cover Business Manager responsibilities when needed
  • Schedule flexibility for the first weekend of each month and periodic resident events

Olympus has held a spot on the National Apartment Association's Top Employer list three years running, which tells you something about how they manage internal culture. Monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses are part of the compensation structure, along with a benefits package that includes an apartment rental allowance and a sabbatical program. Growth paths here are real. Assistant Manager is a well-worn stepping stone to Business Manager and eventually Regional roles for people who perform.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Olympus Creekside Park
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

The assistant manager position at Olympus Creekside Park in The Woodlands calls on a specific mix of financial discipline, interpersonal awareness, and operational follow-through. You're not purely a leasing consultant, and you're not yet a property manager. You sit in the middle, which means your day pulls you in multiple directions at once. The skill that separates people who thrive here from those who struggle is the ability to shift between a detailed, numbers-focused task and a face-to-face resident conversation without losing momentum on either one.

Financial accuracy is central to this work. Collecting rent, posting payments, reconciling receipts, and making sure every dollar is deposited before bank close each day requires consistency and a low tolerance for cutting corners. If you've worked with RealPage or Onsite before, you'll have a real head start here. If you've used Knock for lead tracking on top of that, even better.

What You'll Actually Be Doing Day to Day

Expect mornings that start with reviewing delinquency, flagging outstanding balances, and touching base with the property manager before the office opens to traffic. From there, the day can shift quickly. A prospective resident walks in and the leasing team is occupied. You step in, show a unit, and handle the conversation. A resident has a complaint about a neighbor. You address it directly and document it properly. A make-ready unit needs a final inspection before a move-in tomorrow. You walk it, catch what maintenance missed, and make sure the punch list gets closed out before the keys transfer.

When the property manager is out, you're running the site. That's not ceremonial. It means making real decisions about operations, escalating liability issues to the regional manager when appropriate, and keeping the team focused. The expectation is that you already understand how a community runs, which is why Olympus is looking for someone with onsite apartment experience, either as an assistant manager or a cross-trained leasing consultant.

The Woodlands is a competitive submarket. Knowing what's being built nearby, what concessions competitors are offering, and how hiring trends in the area affect renter demand is part of doing this job well. That market awareness feeds directly into retention conversations and renewal strategy.

Fit and Culture at Olympus Property

Olympus has been recognized as a top employer by the National Apartment Association three consecutive years running, 2023 through 2025. That kind of recognition doesn't happen by accident, and it also creates a real expectation: the culture they've built requires people who actually want to be part of it, not just people who list "team player" on a resume.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with some flexibility for after-hours resident events and the first weekend of each month. That's a reasonable ask for a community-facing role, but it's worth knowing upfront. Resident events aren't optional extras here. They're part of how this team maintains occupancy and builds the kind of retention that shows up in renewal numbers.

  • Onsite apartment experience required (assistant manager or cross-trained leasing)
  • RealPage, Onsite, or Knock experience strongly preferred
  • Comfortable stepping into the property manager role during absences
  • Detail-oriented with financial processes and resident file management
  • Available for occasional weekend and after-hours commitments

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, educational assistance, pet insurance, short and long-term disability, life insurance, paid time off, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses round out the compensation structure.

job.title: Business Manager - Olympus at The Woodlands
job.description:
Running a Luxury Asset in The Woodlands

The Woodlands is one of the stronger submarkets in the Houston metro, with a renter base that expects Class A finishes and service to match. Olympus at The Woodlands sits squarely in that competitive space, and the Business Manager role here is a full-ownership position. You're not just enforcing policy. You're running the asset.

Olympus Property uses the title "Business Manager" deliberately. This is a property manager role in scope, but the expectation is that you think like an operator. That means owning the financial performance of the property from top to bottom: reviewing monthly performance against budget, building annual business plans, and having informed conversations with your Regional Manager and Regional VP about where the numbers are headed and why. You'll manage rents, occupancy, and expenditures with enough fluency to spot variance before it becomes a problem.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

On any given week, you might be reviewing a vendor bid for a capital project in the morning, walking units with maintenance to confirm make-ready quality in the afternoon, and hosting a resident event that evening. The role is genuinely varied. You'll oversee both office and maintenance staff, which means your leadership skills get tested across two very different team cultures simultaneously.

Resident retention and renewal programs fall under your watch, as does leasing performance. You're responsible for marketing strategy and execution, not just approving what someone else builds. Regular property inspections, vendor contract negotiations, and compliance oversight are all part of the standard workload. Olympus uses RealPage, Knock, and OneSite, so familiarity with that stack will matter from day one.

  • Minimum two years of multifamily property manager experience required
  • Luxury Class A experience is strongly preferred
  • RealPage, Knock, and OneSite proficiency preferred
  • Full-time Monday through Friday with schedule flexibility for events and emergencies

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Plenty of property managers can handle occupancy and leasing traffic. The candidates who stand out at a company like Olympus are the ones who can read a T-12 with the same comfort they bring to a resident conversation. Class A residents in a master-planned community like The Woodlands have high expectations and they're not shy about voicing them. Operators who stay calm under that pressure, coach their teams well, and still hit NOI targets are the ones who build long careers here.

Olympus earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer designation three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025), which signals something real about how the company invests in its people. They offer career pathing support, leadership conferences, and educational assistance alongside the standard benefits package. For an experienced property manager ready to run a premium asset with genuine company backing, this is a serious opportunity.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Most leasing roles ask for experience first and teach culture second. Weinstein Properties built their hiring model the other way around. After more than 70 years as a family-owned company, they've learned that attitude and people skills outlast any amount of prior leasing knowledge. This Leasing Consultant opening in Cedar Park reflects that philosophy directly.

The position splits time between two communities: Bexley Lakeline and Bexley at Whitestone. You're not bouncing between unrelated properties as an afterthought. You're embedded in two communities that share a market and a management team, which means you'll build familiarity with both resident bases, both maintenance crews, and both leasing pipelines simultaneously. That dual-site setup is worth understanding before you apply. It adds variety, but it also means you need to stay organized and transition smoothly between two distinct environments on any given day.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your day starts with traffic. Prospects walk in, call in, or reach out online, and your job is to convert that interest into a signed lease by giving people a genuine sense of what living there feels like. That means walking units, answering real questions honestly, and following up consistently. You're also the person current residents interact with when they have a concern, a question about their lease, or just need someone to acknowledge them. The administrative side is real too: applications, move-in paperwork, and keeping the leasing office running correctly.

The schedule runs weekdays 9 to 6, Saturdays 9 to 5 on a rotational basis, and Sundays are closed. Starting pay is $20 per hour with quarterly bonuses, and rates increase with experience. Occasional weekend events or weather-related situations may pull you outside standard hours. That's worth knowing upfront rather than being surprised by it later.

Who Fits This Role

  • Strong communicators who listen as well as they talk, both in person and in writing
  • People who genuinely enjoy helping others solve problems, including the messy ones
  • Organized, goal-oriented individuals who don't need someone standing over them to stay on task
  • Team players who pitch in outside their lane without making it a point of contention
  • Candidates who can hold a positive attitude through a chaotic afternoon without it feeling forced

Prior leasing experience is not required. Weinstein invests in a hands-on training program designed to bring motivated people up to speed. That said, candidates who stand out typically bring some background in sales, hospitality, retail, or any role where reading people and managing competing needs was part of the job. The skills transfer directly.

It's also worth noting where this role leads. Many of Weinstein's current site managers and regional staff started in leasing. If you perform well here, you're not stuck. The company operates over 60 communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia, which means there's genuine room to grow into assistant management, property management, or even corporate roles over time. Leasing is often the best entry point into property management precisely because it teaches you how a community generates revenue, handles residents, and maintains occupancy. All of that context becomes the foundation for every role above it.

Weinstein Properties is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Dockside Apartments
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a front-line leasing role at Dockside Apartments in Kent, WA. You're the first face prospective residents see, which means your energy and follow-through directly affect occupancy. The job covers the full leasing cycle: greeting and qualifying prospects, preparing and executing leases, coordinating move-ins with the maintenance team, and keeping rental files tight and current in the property management system. You'll also handle the day-to-day resident interactions that come with the territory, rent collection questions, maintenance follow-ups, the occasional complaint that needs a calm and professional hand.

The administrative side is real. Monthly reporting, organized paperwork, accurate data entry. It's not glamorous, but it's what keeps a property running cleanly. If you're someone who treats a punch list walkthrough and a lease signing with the same attention to detail, you'll fit in here.

One honest note: leasing roles require consistency on the days traffic is slow just as much as the days it's busy. The consultants who advance are the ones who treat a quiet Tuesday the same as a Saturday with five tours on the books.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of property management experience (preferred, not required)
  • Genuine sales ability backed by solid customer service instincts
  • Professional communication, written and verbal
  • Comfort working in a team environment where you're not the only moving part
  • Accuracy and organization when managing lease files and entering data

The Bigger Picture

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. They're a company that promotes from within, which in our industry means something specific: leasing consultant roles routinely feed into assistant manager and manager positions when the person shows they can handle both the sales side and the operational side. If you're thinking about a career path in property management rather than just a job, that context matters.

Compensation runs $21.50 to $24.00 per hour depending on experience, with monthly and quarterly bonuses and a company profit-sharing program. The benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer match, paid holidays, sick time, and rental discounts. Kent sits in the south King County submarket, which has seen steady multifamily demand from the industrial and logistics employment base in the area. It's a working-class renter market that rewards consultants who can connect with a broad range of applicants and communicate clearly without a lot of pretense.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Single-family rental at scale creates a specific maintenance challenge: your properties aren't clustered in one building or complex. They're scattered across a metro area, each with its own condition, history, and quirks. Roofstock operates in exactly that model, and this Maintenance Technician role in Tampa is built around someone who can work independently across multiple sites without a supervisor down the hall.

What This Role Actually Involves

Your days will vary. One morning you might be completing a make-ready punch list on a vacant home before a new resident moves in. That afternoon could take you to a different property to audit work a vendor completed, checking quality against what was actually invoiced. You'll handle HVAC, plumbing, and electrical repairs, conduct move-in and move-out inspections, and manage your work orders through a mobile app rather than paper tickets. The ability to navigate your own schedule, prioritize stops, and document clearly matters as much as your technical skills.

The schedule here is worth noting. Full-time hours, no on-call rotation, no weekends. A company vehicle and gas card are provided, which removes the wear-and-tear concern that comes with field roles. Pay runs $25 to $30 per hour depending on experience and licensure.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

The role requires HVAC Type II Certification at minimum, with Universal Certification preferred. You'll need a valid driver's license, solid troubleshooting instincts, and comfort using mobile tools for dispatching, documentation, and communication. Working independently isn't optional here. It's the entire structure of the job.

What you'll develop is equally valuable. Technicians who work across scattered single-family portfolios get exposure to a wider range of property conditions than most apartment maintenance roles offer. You'll sharpen your ability to assess a property fast, identify deferred maintenance, and produce inspection documentation that holds up during onboarding audits. That skill set transfers directly into field supervisor, regional maintenance, or property operations roles as your career progresses.

  • HVAC Type II Certification required; Universal Certification preferred
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record
  • Comfortable with mobile apps for work orders and field communication
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs, climb, and work in varying conditions
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship

Strong candidates in this type of role tend to be people who treat vendor QA seriously, not just as a checkbox. Catching sloppy work before a resident moves in protects the property, protects the company's reputation, and builds trust with ownership. That attention to detail is what separates a good field tech from a great one.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
It's move-out weekend at Varsity House Gainesville. You're walking units with a vendor, flagging punch list items in Turnable, and fielding a call about a disputed damage charge, all before noon. That's a normal Tuesday in student housing, and it's exactly the kind of environment this role is built for.

What This Role Actually Involves

The Scion Group runs one of the more operationally sophisticated student housing platforms in the country, and the Assistant Community Manager (titled internally as Assistant General Manager) at Varsity House is a genuine second-in-command. You're not shadowing. You're running the building when the General Manager is out, and you're a daily partner in everything from staff development to financial reporting when they're in.

The responsibilities here span a wider range than most assistant-level roles in conventional multifamily. On any given week, you might be coaching a leasing team member through a difficult resident interaction, auditing accounts receivable in Entrata, reviewing KPIs on leasing velocity and concessions, and physically helping move furniture during the annual turn. Student housing turns are a different animal. The volume is compressed, the stakes are high, and everyone, including management, gets hands-on.

Specific duties include:

  • Supporting the GM with hiring, training, and staff scheduling, including after-hours on-call coordination
  • Managing resident accounts, utility billing, and accounts receivable with regular auditing
  • Keeping delinquency below 2% through consistent enforcement of late fee and collections policies
  • Conducting property inspections and coordinating work orders with vendors and facilities staff
  • Assisting with the full annual turnover process, including move-out inspections, damage assessments, and final billing
  • Monitoring resident feedback across Google, Yelp, and internal survey platforms, then acting on it
  • Using KPI data to inform decisions on market rates, concessions, and leasing strategy alongside the Customer and Sales Experience Manager

What Qualifies You and Where This Can Lead

You need at least one year of on-site experience in property management or residential communities, and comfort with Entrata is a real plus given how deeply it's used here. Strong written communication matters more than people often expect in this role. Resident notices, review responses, and damage dispute correspondence all reflect on the property's reputation.

The tool stack at Scion is worth noting: Entrata, Turnable, Qualtrics, Lattice, ClickUp, and Greenhouse. Candidates who pick up systems quickly and think in terms of process will feel at home here. Those who prefer loose, unstructured environments probably won't.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in a role like this is the ability to hold both the detail-level work (a resident's billing dispute, a punch list item, a late fee exception) and the bigger picture (occupancy trends, team morale, turn readiness) at the same time. Neither one gets dropped.

Career-wise, this is one of the cleaner paths to a General Manager seat in student housing. The exposure here covers operations, people management, financial performance, and facilities, which means the skills you build aren't siloed. They transfer directly to a GM role at a larger community, a regional support position, or even a corporate ops track if that's the direction you want to go. Student housing experience also translates well to conventional multifamily, especially on the lease-up side, where the high-velocity leasing cycles are comparable.

This is a salaried, exempt position based on-site at Varsity House in Gainesville. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental leave, and learning reimbursement. Work authorization in the U.S. is required. Visa sponsorship is not available.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager - Student Housing
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits right in the middle of everything at Alight Fayetteville. You're the General Manager's right hand on daily operations, which means one morning you're reviewing delinquency reports and chasing down late fees, and the next afternoon you're walking units with a vendor during a make-ready inspection. Student housing runs on a calendar that doesn't slow down, and neither does this position.

A big part of the job is financial oversight: keeping accounts receivable clean, reconciling month-end reports, and holding delinquency below 2% by the time the books close each month. You'll also manage resident accounts and utility billing, post damage charges from quarterly inspections, and process move-out refunds or dispute responses. It's detailed, repetitive work that has real consequences if it slips.

Then there's turn. Student housing runs on a lease-up cycle tied to the academic year, and the annual turnover process here is a full team effort. You'll use Turnable to track progress on the electronic turn board, walk units with vendors, assess damage charges at move-out, and yes, physically help move furniture and clean units when volume demands it. If you've only ever managed turn from behind a desk, that expectation is worth knowing upfront.

You'll also support leasing and customer experience goals alongside the Customer and Sales Experience Manager, keeping an eye on KPIs like leasing velocity, concessions, and gain to lease. When resident concerns escalate, they land with you. You'll respond to Google and Yelp reviews through Entrata and develop action plans based on patterns you're seeing in resident feedback.

What You Bring

  • At least 1 year of experience in property management or residential community operations
  • Comfort working in Entrata or a comparable property management system
  • Strong written communication skills (resident notices, review responses, and internal reporting all require clarity)
  • The ability to handle confidential resident and financial information without cutting corners
  • Willingness to work non-traditional hours during peak leasing periods and take on-call shifts
  • Experience with or quick adaptability to platforms like ClickUp, Qualtrics, Greenhouse, or Lattice is a plus

Context Worth Having

Student housing has its own rhythm that differs from conventional multifamily. Residents are often first-time renters, parents are frequently involved in leasing decisions, and the entire community turns over on a compressed summer timeline rather than on rolling lease expirations. That creates concentrated stress points, especially during move-in and move-out weeks, that you won't find at a typical garden-style property. The upside is that the operational complexity accelerates your learning. Assistant Community Managers who handle student housing well tend to be well-prepared for General Manager roles because they've already dealt with high-volume turns, active parent communication, and tight financial reporting cycles.

The Scion Group uses a fairly deep tech stack for a property-level role. Familiarity with Entrata is the most important piece, but being comfortable jumping between project management tools, experience platforms, and applicant tracking systems will make the day-to-day less friction-heavy. This position is based on-site at Alight Fayetteville and requires U.S. work authorization. Visa sponsorship is not available.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
It's 9:15 on a Tuesday morning. You've already posted two payments, left a delinquency follow-up message for a resident three days past due, and you're pulling up the day's traffic log before the Community Manager has finished her first cup of coffee. That's the pace of this role at Vestavia Reserve, and for the right person, it's genuinely energizing.

The Role at Vestavia Reserve

Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the top 50 multifamily operators in the country and a company with deep roots in the Southeast, is hiring an Assistant Community Manager for this Vestavia Hills, Alabama community. The position sits at the intersection of leasing performance and financial oversight. You're not just supporting the Community Manager. You're running point on delinquency, ledger accuracy, rent collection, and renewals while simultaneously keeping occupancy moving through tours, lead follow-up, and lease execution.

On the leasing side, you'll guide prospects from first inquiry through signed lease, manage social media content to keep the community visible and engaged, and help maintain the kind of curb appeal and office presentation that converts traffic into residents. On the financial side, you'll monitor delinquency weekly, make follow-up calls, coordinate eviction procedures when necessary, and assist with reporting for regional leadership. When the Community Manager is out, you hold the operation together.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • At least six months of prior assistant community manager experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP certification is a plus

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off to keep the week at 40 hours. Occasional evenings or weekends may come up for resident events.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

What separates strong candidates in this role from average ones is comfort with the financial side. Leasing skills are common. The ability to read a ledger, catch a misapplied payment, and manage a delinquency list without letting it snowball is rarer. If you've got both, this role is a clear step toward a Community Manager seat, and Hawthorne's internal Career Path Program is built to get you there.

job.title: Floating Leasing Specialist
job.description:
You walk into a leasing office you've never worked in before, learn the floor plans by mid-morning, and close your first lease before lunch. That's the rhythm of this role. Hillpointe is looking for a Floating Leasing Specialist to move across their portfolio of workforce housing communities in the Sun Belt, stepping in wherever leasing momentum needs a boost.

What This Role Actually Involves

Hillpointe builds and manages market-rate workforce housing, and they're one of the more active developers in that space right now. As a floating specialist, you won't be anchored to one address. You'll rotate across communities based on where the need is greatest: a lease-up pushing to stabilize, a high-traffic period overwhelming a small on-site team, or a brand-new community launch that needs experienced leasing coverage from day one.

Day to day, you're greeting prospects, conducting property tours, and tailoring your pitch to what each person actually needs in a home. You'll follow up by phone, text, and email, keep tour paths and model units looking sharp, and make sure every interaction reflects well on the community. You're also expected to maintain professionalism across very different site environments, since each property will have its own team culture, floor plan mix, and traffic patterns.

One real benefit worth noting: Hillpointe provides free rent at an assigned community, subject to their policy and position requirements.

What Hillpointe Is Looking For

  • Genuine comfort with frequent travel and the flexibility to relocate temporarily or permanently when the business needs it
  • Availability to work weekends, evenings, and holidays as leasing activity demands
  • Prior experience in leasing, sales, hospitality, or customer-facing roles (preferred, not required)
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to connect with a wide range of people quickly
  • A valid driver's license and the ability to move through all areas of a property, including stairs and outdoor spaces
  • High school diploma or equivalent

The candidates who stand out in floating roles aren't just good at leasing. They're fast adapters. Walking into a new office and being productive within hours, without needing hand-holding on the basics, is what separates someone who thrives here from someone who struggles. If you've worked multiple properties or covered for other sites before, that experience translates directly.

This kind of role also builds a strong foundation for moving into a permanent leasing consultant position, a lead leasing role, or eventually an Assistant Manager track. Floating specialists who perform well across a portfolio tend to get noticed faster than those working a single stable asset, simply because more people in the organization see their work.

job.title: Floating Leasing Specialist
job.description:
Hillpointe builds and operates workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and they've grown fast enough that their leasing teams sometimes need reinforcement before a community can catch its breath. That's where this role comes in. The Floating Leasing Specialist exists to plug gaps: lease-ups, high-traffic periods, team transitions, new community launches. You're not planted at one property. You go where the pipeline needs you.

The day-to-day is straightforward enough. You're greeting prospects, running tours, tailoring your pitch to what actually matters to each person, and following up consistently across phone, text, and email. You're keeping the tour path and model units presentable. You're answering questions and moving leads through the funnel. What makes this role different from a standard leasing consultant position is the constant context-switching. You might be supporting a lease-up in one community for three weeks, then shift to cover a vacancy on an established property the next month. Every assignment has its own team culture, its own traffic patterns, its own quirks.

One thing worth being honest about: this role requires genuine flexibility, not the kind people claim on a resume. Hillpointe can ask you to relocate temporarily or permanently based on operational need. If that sounds like a disruption, this probably isn't the right fit. If it sounds like an interesting way to build a broad base of experience across a growing portfolio, that's a better sign. On the upside, free rent at an assigned Hillpointe community is part of the package, which is a meaningful benefit in this market.

From a career standpoint, floating roles like this one tend to accelerate development in ways that staying at a single property doesn't. You'll see how different communities handle traffic, concessions, and occupancy goals. You'll get exposure to lease-ups, which is some of the most useful experience in multifamily. Leasing consultants who come out of floating or multi-site roles often move into assistant manager or leasing manager positions faster than their peers, simply because they've seen more situations and adapted to more teams.

What Hillpointe is looking for

  • Prior experience in leasing, sales, hospitality, or customer-facing roles (preferred, not required)
  • Comfort working across different properties and teams without a long ramp-up period
  • Availability to work weekends and adjust your schedule around leasing activity
  • Valid driver's license and willingness to travel between communities in the portfolio
  • Strong interpersonal communication skills across diverse groups of people
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Ability to physically tour indoor and outdoor areas, including stairs, in varying weather

Fair housing compliance is non-negotiable, as it is everywhere in our industry. Hillpointe is a fully integrated developer, meaning they control everything from land acquisition through asset management. That's relevant context for you: this isn't a third-party management shop. The communities you'd support are owned and operated in-house, which generally means a more cohesive operational culture across the portfolio.

job.title: Floating Leasing Specialist
job.description:
What This Role Actually Is

Floating leasing roles are underused and underappreciated in our industry. When they're done well, they're one of the most effective tools a growing portfolio has. Hillpointe, a Sun Belt workforce housing developer with a fully integrated model from land acquisition through asset management, is hiring a Floating Leasing Specialist based out of Pensacola to move across their communities as demand dictates. That means lease-ups, coverage gaps, high-traffic periods, and new community launches. You're the closer they send in when it matters.

This is not a role for someone who wants to put down roots at one property and settle into a routine. It's for someone who picks up a new floor plan, learns a new community's comp set, and is giving tours confidently by day two.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

The core of this job is leasing. Tours, follow-up calls, texts, emails, and making sure the tour path looks sharp before the next prospect walks in. You'll cover communities during team transitions and step in during peak traffic periods when the on-site team needs reinforcement. The specific responsibilities include:

  • Traveling to Hillpointe communities across the portfolio as assigned
  • Conducting property tours and tailoring your pitch to each prospect's actual needs
  • Managing follow-up communication through phone, text, and email
  • Keeping leasing office areas, model units, and amenity spaces tour-ready
  • Gathering prospect information and maintaining accurate records
  • Supporting community launches and high-volume leasing periods

Hillpointe also provides free rent at an assigned community, which is worth factoring in when you're thinking about total compensation. That benefit is subject to their internal policy and position requirements.

Who Tends to Succeed in This Role

We've seen floating specialists burn out fast when they underestimate the adaptability this kind of position demands. Walking into a new property every few weeks, building rapport quickly with on-site teams you don't know, and staying sharp on fair housing compliance regardless of which community you're working at, that's the actual job. It's more mentally demanding than a standard leasing consultant role, even if the core tasks look similar on paper.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just sales ability. It's the combination of interpersonal range (you can talk to anyone), genuine comfort with ambiguity, and the discipline to represent a brand consistently across different environments. Hillpointe builds and manages workforce housing at scale, which means your prospects are working people with real budgets. The ability to communicate value clearly and honestly matters more than a polished script.

Prior leasing experience is preferred but not required. Backgrounds in hospitality and customer-facing sales translate well. You'll need a valid driver's license, flexibility to work weekends, and a genuine willingness to relocate temporarily or permanently if the business needs it.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a hands-on maintenance technician role at Lake St. James, a Cottonwood Residential community in Conyers, GA. Your days will involve a mix of work orders and reactive repairs across plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry. You'll be troubleshooting HVAC systems regularly, so comfort with diagnostics matters more than just swapping parts. Between work orders you'll be walking the property, checking on units, and keeping things running. The job is physical. You're on your feet, on ladders, and occasionally in crawl spaces.

On-call rotation is part of this role. After-hours emergencies happen, and you'll be expected to respond. Cottonwood supports their technicians through the Service Manager during those calls, but the expectation is real and worth knowing going in. If that kind of responsibility suits you, this role is a solid fit.

What You Bring

  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • Considerable hands-on HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • Working knowledge of plumbing and basic electrical repairs
  • Valid driver's license
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work in physically demanding conditions including stairs, ladders, scaffolding, and tight spaces
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts
  • CPO certification is a plus but not required
  • Strong enough English communication skills to process work orders, read safety manuals, and talk through issues with residents

The Role in Context

Cottonwood Residential was an early mover on Self-Guided Tours, which tells you something about how they approach operations. They're not a company standing still. For a maintenance technician, that means you're working within a management culture that takes resident experience seriously, not just at leasing but through the life of the tenancy. A well-run maintenance operation is a direct driver of renewal rates and reputation, and companies like Cottonwood know it.

Benefits kick in quickly here, within the first 30 days, and the PTO package for a first-year employee (120 hours plus 10.5 paid holidays) is genuinely competitive for a field-level maintenance role. The 401k and HSA company match adds real value over time.

If you're the kind of technician who takes ownership of a property rather than just closing tickets, this is a role worth your attention.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Birgo manages apartment communities across several Pittsburgh-area neighborhoods, including North Versailles, East McKeesport, Wilmerding, and Edgewood. This Maintenance Technician role sits at the center of daily operations across those properties, and the work touches residents directly. That matters here. Birgo describes itself as mission-driven, and the maintenance team is a real part of that, not just a support function.

What You'll Actually Do

A typical week mixes turn work, common area orders, and preventative maintenance. Make-readies are a core part of the rhythm: painting, drywall patching, plumbing repairs, replacing fixtures, and getting units ready for incoming residents. Common area calls tend to be the unglamorous but important stuff: unclogging drains, swapping p-traps, fixing lighting. You'll also handle electrical, carpentry, and HVAC repairs as they come up.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., with a rotating on-call shift for after-hours needs. On-call is real. Residents don't schedule emergencies, and you should go into this role knowing that some nights and weekends will come up on rotation. It's part of the job, and it's manageable, but it's worth being clear-eyed about before you apply.

You'll be moving between multiple properties, so a valid driver's license and your own insured vehicle are required. Mileage reimbursement is included.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience with tools and general repairs across trades (plumbing, electrical, drywall, painting, carpentry, HVAC)
  • Physical ability to lift and carry 50 pounds, work in confined spaces, and safely use ladders and power tools
  • Valid driver's license and a personal, reliable, insured vehicle
  • Eligibility to work in the United States
  • Comfort with technology and a willingness to learn systems and processes on the job
  • The kind of reliability that means residents and teammates can count on you

Birgo isn't looking for someone who needs every task spelled out. They use the phrase "servant hearted" in their values, which is a real signal about culture fit. Strong candidates here tend to be self-starters who take quality seriously on a punch list without needing someone to check every item. If you've done make-readies before and you take pride in a clean, well-finished turn, that background will show immediately.

Context Worth Knowing

Working across multiple Class B and C garden-style communities in the Pittsburgh suburbs means variety in building age, condition, and resident needs. Older housing stock in these neighborhoods often has its own quirks: aging plumbing, mixed electrical systems, deferred repairs that require real problem-solving rather than just part swaps. Technicians who build strong diagnostic instincts in environments like this often move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles as a natural next step. The professional development reimbursement Birgo offers suggests they're open to supporting that kind of growth.

Pay is $23 per hour, paid weekly. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance with employer contributions, PTO, paid holidays, sick time, a 401(k) match, and discounted rent at Birgo properties.

job.title: Senior Associate - Asset Management (Real Estate)
job.description:
Birgo Capital has grown fast. Since 2020 the firm has tripled in size, now managing over $300 million in assets across a 3,500-unit multifamily portfolio spread across four states. That kind of growth creates real complexity, and this Senior Associate role sits directly at the center of it.

The core job is translation. Acquisitions underwrites a deal with assumptions about rent growth, occupancy, expense ratios, and capex recovery. Your job is to take those assumptions and make sure operations actually delivers on them. When a property drifts from its business plan, you're the one who catches it early, understands why, and builds the case for corrective action. That means owning the annual budget cycle, running monthly re-forecasts, and stress-testing fund-level cash flow models well enough to give leadership a clear, honest read on IRR and DSCR performance. The portfolio includes 60-plus vintage assets, so you'll rarely be working with new construction assumptions. These are older buildings with real maintenance profiles, and the numbers reflect that.

Property management performance is another major lever here. Birgo runs a vertically integrated model, so the PM team is internal, but that doesn't mean alignment is automatic. You'll build genuine working relationships with site-level and regional staff, helping them read variance reports, understand market comps, and make smarter decisions on net effective rent and expense control. This isn't a top-down dynamic. The role rewards people who can earn trust through competence and consistency, not title.

On the capital side, you'll manage lender relationships, monitor covenant compliance, and prepare reporting packages for refinances and dispositions. With a portfolio this size and vintage, there's almost always something in the capital stack that needs attention.

Birgo is also building out AI-assisted tracking tools for occupancy, net effective rent, and capex ROI. You'll be expected to use them and help refine them, not just consume outputs.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • 3 to 5 years of direct asset management experience in multifamily, with real exposure to budgeting, re-forecasting, and variance analysis
  • Financial modeling skills sharp enough to stress-test a fund-level cash flow model, not just read one
  • Comfort working with offshore analysts: setting clear expectations, reviewing REO schedules, and maintaining output quality without micromanaging
  • Familiarity with AppFolio or comparable property management software
  • Based in or willing to relocate near Pittsburgh, Buffalo, Cleveland, or Morgantown, with roughly 25% travel for site visits

One honest note on what separates good candidates from great ones in a role like this: the ability to hold property managers accountable without damaging the relationship. Asset management at a vertically integrated firm lives or dies on that dynamic. If you default to being either the enforcer or the pushover, performance suffers. The people who do well here tend to be analytically sharp and genuinely curious about operations, not just the spreadsheet behind it.

The comp structure includes disposition fees and profit-sharing, which means your upside is tied directly to how the assets perform. That alignment is intentional. Birgo is expanding its Midwest footprint, so there's real room to grow with the platform as the portfolio scales.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
It's 7:15 a.m. A resident submits an emergency work order: no hot water. You're the first one on site, diagnosing the water heater before most of your neighbors have had their coffee. That's the rhythm of this role.

The Work

Comstock is hiring a Maintenance Technician for a midrise apartment community in Rockville, MD. This is a hands-on, full-spectrum maintenance position. You'll handle HVAP, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, and general carpentry. Make-readies are part of the routine: turning units between residents, completing punch lists, and getting apartments move-in ready on schedule.

Day to day, you'll respond to resident work orders, perform preventive maintenance on unit-level and building-level equipment, and keep up with exterior grounds work including light landscaping and common area upkeep. You'll also carry a share of the on-call rotation, which means being available after hours and on weekends and able to reach the property within 45 minutes for emergencies. That's a real commitment, and it's worth knowing going in.

Resident interaction is a genuine part of this job. The community targets a Class A service standard, so how you communicate with residents when you enter their unit, explain a repair, or follow up on an open issue matters as much as the technical fix itself.

What You'll Need

  • At least one year of experience as a maintenance technician
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems
  • CFC Universal Certification (preferred)
  • Class A property experience (preferred)
  • Familiarity with Yardi and building automation systems (both a plus)
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Outlook
  • Valid driver's license with no major violations
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and work in variable conditions indoors and outdoors
  • High school diploma or GED (equivalent experience considered)

The pay range for this position in Maryland is $25 to $28 per hour, with bonus potential. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, and life insurance. Comstock also offers annual professional development funds and advancement opportunities across their growing portfolio.

One thing that separates strong candidates here: technicians who treat the on-call rotation as part of the job, not an inconvenience, tend to build the most trust with both management and residents. Reliability at 10 p.m. carries more weight than any certification on a resume.

job.title: Maintenance Technician ($1500 Sign-On Bonus)
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Maintenance work at a luxury apartment community is a different animal than Class B or C operations. Residents expect fast turnarounds, polished communication, and zero visible evidence that anything was ever broken. The technical skills here are real: HVAC diagnosis, plumbing repairs, electrical troubleshooting, appliance work, carpentry, and painting. But what separates a strong tech from an average one at a property like this is the ability to walk into a resident's home, fix the problem correctly the first time, and leave the space cleaner than you found it. Soft skills aren't optional at this level.

CFC Universal Certification is preferred, and HVAC knowledge is required. If you've worked Class A assets before, you already understand the standard. If you haven't, be honest with yourself about the adjustment. The pace is real, the expectations are high, and residents notice details.

What You're Actually Doing Day to Day

Your day starts with a work order queue. Some are straightforward: a leaking faucet, a cabinet door off its hinge, a slow drain. Others require more diagnosis. Preventative maintenance runs alongside reactive work, so you're not just putting out fires. You're also turning units for new move-ins, which means completing punch lists efficiently so make-readies stay on schedule and occupancy doesn't slip.

  • Complete interior and exterior repairs across plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and appliances
  • Perform preventative maintenance on unit-level and building-level equipment
  • Execute make-readies to prep units for incoming residents
  • Handle grounds work including pickup, sweeping, and light landscaping
  • Participate in an on-call emergency rotation with a 45-minute response window
  • Work with building automation systems and Yardi (experience with both is a plus)

The on-call rotation is worth acknowledging directly. After-hours calls happen. You need reliable transportation and the ability to reach the property within 45 minutes. That's a real commitment, and this role is upfront about it.

What Makes This Worth Your Attention at Comstock

Comstock operates an expanding portfolio, which matters for career trajectory. A tech who performs well at the property level has a clear path toward lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles as the portfolio grows. There's also annual professional development funding, which is genuinely useful if you're working toward certifications or want to sharpen skills in building automation or HVAC systems.

The $1,500 sign-on bonus reflects real market demand for qualified technicians in the Northern Virginia corridor. Ashburn in particular is a competitive submarket with significant multifamily density, so experienced techs have options. Comstock is competing for that talent with a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401K match, and life insurance, alongside the sign-on incentive.

One year of maintenance technician experience is the baseline. A current driver's license without major violations is required. If you bring the technical range and the resident-facing professionalism this type of community demands, the role is structured to reward both.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Bozzuto runs a tight operation, and this role sits right in the middle of it. The Assistant Maintenance Manager at their Seattle property works alongside the Maintenance Manager to keep the building performing at a high level, residents taken care of, and the asset protected. It's a hands-on position. You're not just supervising; you're in the work.

Day to day, that means closing out service tickets with real follow-through, not just marking them done. It means owning the turn process so units are make-ready on schedule and new residents aren't waiting. It means running preventative maintenance programs before things break, not after. HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair: you need to be competent across all of it. Exposure to complex mechanical systems like boilers, chillers, or central plant setups is a plus at a building like this.

You'll also be part of the on-call rotation. That's the honest reality of this role. Emergencies don't wait for business hours, and Bozzuto expects its maintenance leadership to respond when it counts.

What the role requires

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of OSHA, MSDS, and risk management practices
  • Hands-on proficiency with HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Supervisory experience or a clear ability to lead and motivate a small team
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office use
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in varying weather conditions
  • Availability for emergency on-call and weekend coverage

What separates a strong candidate here from an average one is the combination of technical range and leadership instinct. Plenty of maintenance techs are skilled with tools. Fewer can also run a punch list review with a junior tech, communicate clearly with a frustrated resident, and still close out three work orders before noon. That dual capability is what Bozzuto is hiring for at the assistant manager level.

The pay range runs from $30 to $31.50 per hour, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

If you know buildings well enough to anticipate problems before they become complaints, and you're ready to take on a leadership track in property maintenance, this is a role worth looking at seriously.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
What This Role Actually Involves

Bozzuto manages properties with a reputation for quality that demands real accountability from the maintenance side. At a Santa Monica community, that means you're not just fixing things. You're the person residents trust to follow through, and the person the maintenance team looks to for direction. This Assistant Maintenance Manager role sits between hands-on trade work and team leadership, and that balance is genuinely demanding.

Your day pulls you in a few directions at once. You might start the morning reviewing open service tickets and walking a freshly completed turn with a punch list in hand, then pivot to troubleshooting an HVAC issue on a hot afternoon while checking in on a technician who's handling a plumbing call. Santa Monica's coastal climate is generally forgiving, but complex mechanical systems in mid-rise or larger residential buildings don't care about the weather. You'll need real fluency with central plant equipment, split systems, and boilers, not just residential-grade familiarity.

What You'll Be Responsible For

  • Leading the make-ready process: coordinating turns so units are prepped, inspected, and ready to lease on schedule
  • Resolving HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and appliance issues, either personally or through your team
  • Running preventative maintenance programs that protect the asset's long-term value
  • Holding the team accountable to Bozzuto's standards for cleanliness, safety, and appearance
  • Following applicable building codes, OSHA requirements, and safety protocols across all work
  • Participating in the on-call emergency rotation, including weekends

That last point deserves honest mention. After-hours calls are part of this job. If you're coming from a commercial facilities background where emergencies were rare, residential management operates differently. Resident needs don't follow business hours, and a senior maintenance leader who's reachable and composed under pressure makes a real difference in how residents experience the community.

Who Fits Well Here

Bozzuto looks for people who treat asset preservation as a professional value, not just a job requirement. The phrase they use internally, "know it like you built it," reflects a mindset they genuinely expect. You should be the kind of person who notices a water intrusion issue before it becomes a work order, or spots a fire door that isn't latching properly during a routine walk.

Strong candidates will have five or more years in the trades or residential facilities, an EPA or HVAC certification, and some supervisory experience. Exposure to complex mechanical systems is a real differentiator here. Basic carpentry, drywall, and paint skills round out the technical picture. Just as important is how you communicate: with residents who are frustrated, with vendors who need direction, and with a maintenance team that takes cues from how you carry yourself.

The salary range for this position is $71,000 to $76,000, with additional bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement for those who want to keep building their skills. For someone with the right background, this role is a natural step toward a Maintenance Manager position with full-site responsibility.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning and you're fielding a call about a late rent payment while a prospect waits at the leasing desk and your property manager is out for the day. That's not a worst-case scenario at this job. That's just Tuesday.

What This Role Actually Involves

Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Property Manager for their community in Salem, OR. This is a real number-two role, meaning you're not just supporting the property manager, you're running things when they're not there. That responsibility shows up in the day-to-day in ways the job title doesn't fully capture.

A big part of your week will be split between two things that don't always feel related: financial performance and people. On the financial side, you'll own rent collection, manage delinquency, and stay close to budget and P&L activity. On the people side, you'll conduct tours, work to convert traffic into signed leases, and make sure every resident interaction reflects well on the community. You'll also coach and mentor the team around you, which means your influence extends beyond your own tasks.

The role includes one to two weekends per month, with two weekdays off in exchange. Prospects shop on weekends. That's the reality, and this schedule is built around it.

Keeping the property's interior and exterior in solid shape is part of the job too. You're not doing maintenance work, but you're accountable for the community's presentation and for making sure the team carries the brand well.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • A four-year degree or equivalent work experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years in one of those industries
  • Familiarity with revenue, P&L, and budget management
  • Comfort with Yardi or similar property management software
  • Active use of social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook, with the ability to create content that actually engages people
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • A genuine sales instinct, not just the willingness to sell

The salary range for this position is $52,000 to $54,080, with additional bonus opportunities. Bozzuto also offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

What separates strong candidates in this role from average ones is usually composure under competing demands. Leasing skills matter. Financial literacy matters. But the APMs who grow into property manager roles tend to be the ones who can hold the operation together on a complicated day without waiting to be told what to do. If you've got that instinct, this is a solid place to develop it further.

job.title: Bilingual Screening & Applications Specialist - Sandy Springs, GA
job.description:
Where Attention to Detail Meets High-Volume Leasing Operations

This role lives at the intersection of compliance, communication, and speed. Cortland's centralized Contact Center processes applications across a large national portfolio, which means the person in this seat isn't just answering phones. They're moving prospective residents from submitted application to approved file to move-in, often managing dozens of open files at once. If you've ever worked a lease-up push where traffic spikes and every day counts, you understand the operational weight that sits inside an applications queue.

The bilingual requirement here is real. Spanish-speaking applicants need a point of contact who can walk them through documentation requests, explain adverse action steps, and de-escalate concerns without anything getting lost in translation. That skill alone separates this role from a standard leasing support position.

What This Role Actually Demands

The core of the job is application review and file management. You'll collect and verify income documentation, ID, and rental history, then move files through Cortland's approval workflow while staying inside Fair Housing guardrails. That compliance piece isn't optional. One misstep on screening criteria can create fair housing liability at scale, so accuracy under volume pressure is the defining skill.

Beyond the file work, you're the primary contact for applicants reaching out by phone, email, and chat simultaneously. That means your ability to triage, prioritize, and give clear status updates without letting files stall is what keeps conversion rates healthy. Platforms like OneSite, RealPage, and Funnel are part of the daily workflow, and comfort moving between CRM tools and property management software matters as much as any soft skill listed here.

  • 2 or more years in a high-volume customer service or contact center environment, with multifamily experience strongly preferred
  • Bilingual fluency in English and Spanish
  • Hands-on experience with RealPage, OneSite, or Funnel
  • Solid working knowledge of Microsoft Office, especially Outlook and Excel
  • Demonstrated ability to handle confidential applicant information with discretion
  • Availability for weekends and extended hours when volume demands it
  • High school diploma or equivalent required

The Cortland Context

Cortland operates as a vertically integrated firm, meaning design, construction, and property management all run in-house. That structure gives the Contact Center team a direct line into how communities are positioned and what resident expectations look like at each asset. For someone building a career in multifamily operations, a centralized applications role at a top-10 owner and operator gives you exposure to portfolio-level leasing processes that most on-site roles don't offer. The skills you build here, specifically compliance documentation, CRM management, and high-volume applicant communication, transfer cleanly into leasing management, operations coordinator, and compliance-focused roles down the road.

The Sandy Springs office puts you inside Cortland's Atlanta headquarters footprint, close to the operational core of the company rather than isolated on a single property. That proximity to leadership and process development is worth noting for anyone who wants to grow beyond a single asset.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

This position runs on a specific combination of financial literacy, tenant communication, and operational follow-through. If you're comfortable reading aging reports, catching billing discrepancies, and tracking CAM reconciliations without someone holding your hand, you're already thinking in the right direction. Lincoln Property Company is looking for an Assistant Property Manager to support day-to-day operations across commercial, industrial, or retail assets in Denver.

The financial piece here is real work. You'll review vendor invoices against management agreement terms, help prepare monthly reporting packages for institutional clients, and assist with collecting data for CAM reconciliations and operating expense recovery charges. That means you need to understand how recovery structures translate into tenant billings, and you need to catch errors before they compound. Lincoln manages over 680 million square feet of commercial space nationally, so the reporting standards are serious and client expectations are high.

What You're Actually Doing Day to Day

A typical day might start with reviewing an aging report, flagging a tenant balance that's slipped past 30 days, and coordinating with the Property Manager on next steps. From there, you might walk a vacant suite to confirm it's tour-ready, process a purchase order for a vendor delivering HVAC services, and field a tenant request about a common area issue before noon. The role spans lease administration, vendor coordination, property inspections, and emergency preparedness. None of it is glamorous in isolation, but together it forms the operational backbone of how a well-run commercial asset performs.

You'll also assist with bidding activities, coordinate tenant move-ins and move-outs, and help draft client communications. This is a 100% in-office position, and you will travel between assigned properties as needed.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • 1 to 2 years of experience with commercial office, retail, or industrial properties (preferred)
  • Intermediate proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel for financial calculations and reporting
  • Comfort with lease administration systems and the ability to learn client-specific platforms
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills across a range of audiences, from tenants to institutional clients
  • A bachelor's degree (BA/BS) is preferred, though equivalent experience is considered
  • Availability for after-hours, weekend, and emergency response situations when the property needs it

What actually separates strong candidates here is the combination of financial attention to detail and genuine follow-through on tenant issues. Lots of people can handle one or the other. The ones who move up at a firm like Lincoln are the ones who close the loop without being asked, whether that's confirming a vendor completed the work or making sure a reconciliation discrepancy got resolved before the monthly report goes out. This role is a clear path toward a Property Manager position on commercial assets, which carries significantly more client-facing responsibility and P&L ownership.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - The Slate
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a full-time, Monday through Friday role supporting the service team at The Slate, an Olympus Property community in Savannah, GA. Your day runs roughly 9 to 6, though emergencies don't keep a schedule, and you'll need to be available when something urgent comes up after hours. Most of your time is split between completing resident work orders and staying ahead of problems before they become bigger ones.

On any given day, that means cycling through HVAC filter changes and coil cleanings, troubleshooting a refrigerator that stopped cooling, handling a running toilet or a leaking fixture, swapping out an electrical switch, or rekeying a unit after a turn. You'll track everything through the property's maintenance software and coordinate daily priorities with the Lead Maintenance Technician. Grounds upkeep and pool maintenance are also part of the mix, so this isn't a role where you stay strictly indoors.

Savannah's coastal humidity is genuinely hard on HVAC systems and building exteriors. Technicians who understand how salt air and persistent moisture affect equipment, caulking, and HVAC performance tend to stay ahead of the preventative side of the job more naturally than those coming from drier climates. That context matters here.

What You Bring

  • At least 2 years of hands-on maintenance experience in a commercial, residential, or apartment setting
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems. An EPA 608 certification is a strong plus and may be required
  • Comfort with plumbing repairs ranging from fixture replacements to minor installation work
  • Basic electrical troubleshooting: switches, outlets, fixtures
  • Appliance repair experience across standard kitchen and laundry units
  • Ability to operate hand tools and power tools confidently and safely
  • Willingness to be on call for emergency maintenance as needed

Why This Role Is Worth a Look

Olympus Property has earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer designation three consecutive years (2023, 2024, and 2025), which isn't something most management companies can say. The benefits package here is genuinely broad: medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, short and long-term disability, life insurance, paid time off, and an apartment rental allowance. There's also a sabbatical program and structured career pathing, which matters if you're thinking beyond your current title.

For a technician who wants to grow, this kind of platform can lead somewhere. Technicians who build strong HVAC and plumbing skills while developing a track record with a quality operator often move into Lead Technician or Service Manager roles within a few years. Olympus's stated commitment to internal growth and team culture suggests that path is available here, not just on paper.

If you take the work seriously, communicate well with your team, and can manage a steady volume of work orders without cutting corners on the make-ready side, this is a solid place to build your maintenance career.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Groundskeeping at a well-run apartment community is more physical and observational than most people expect. The core skills here aren't complicated, but they matter every single day: attention to detail at ground level, the discipline to work independently without someone checking on you, and the physical stamina to keep moving through an Austin summer. If you're someone who notices the cigarette butt others walk past, or the overgrown edge nobody trimmed, you'll fit this work well.

Weinstein Properties has been family-owned for over 70 years, managing more than 60 communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. The Bexley 3Five community in South Austin is where this role lives. That family-ownership structure means decisions get made by people who actually care about how the property looks and feels, not just what the numbers say on a quarterly report. Curb appeal directly affects traffic and lease-up velocity, and the groundskeeper is the person most responsible for that first impression.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Expect repetition. That's not a warning, it's just the reality of this work. Litter pickup, pet waste stations, blowing walkways, pressure washing, weeding, light planting, and keeping common areas clean are daily and weekly rhythms. You'll also support the maintenance team on make-readies when needed, which could include light painting or housekeeping tasks inside units being turned. Operating a golf cart and trailer, using backpack blowers and power washers, and lifting up to 50 pounds regularly are all part of the physical profile here.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm. No on-call rotations, no weekend requirements built into the base schedule. That's a genuine quality-of-life detail worth noting for this type of role.

  • Daily litter and pet waste pickup throughout the community
  • Pressure washing, blowing, and maintaining exterior common areas
  • Weeding, planting, and general landscaping upkeep
  • Supporting maintenance on turns and make-readies as needed
  • Light painting and interior housekeeping tasks when required
  • Operating equipment including golf carts, trailers, and power tools

What Makes Someone Stand Out Here

The starting pay is $18 per hour with quarterly bonuses, plus a $1,000 stay-on bonus after 90 days in good standing. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, birthday time off, and a rent discount. That package is more complete than what many groundskeeper roles offer at this pay level.

What separates a strong candidate from an average one isn't experience with specific equipment. It's showing up consistently, completing the unglamorous tasks without being asked twice, and communicating well with the maintenance and leasing teams. Weinstein explicitly invests in promoting from within. Groundskeepers who demonstrate reliability and a willingness to learn have a real path into maintenance technician roles, which carry higher pay and broader responsibility across the property's mechanical and unit-level operations. If you're early in a maintenance career and want a structured way in, this is a legitimate starting point.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Alternative Schedule
job.description:
Leasing is one of the few entry points into property management where the ceiling is genuinely high. Traffic converts to signed leases, leases build occupancy, and occupancy drives NOI. The people who understand that connection early tend to move fast. This role at Weinstein Properties in Cumming, GA is a real starting point for that trajectory.

Weinstein is a family-owned operator with more than 70 years in the business and over 60 communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. That kind of longevity in a consolidating industry means something. They're not a REIT optimizing for quarterly earnings. They run their properties hands-on, and they've built a reputation for training people from scratch rather than just hiring experience. The Bexley Westshore community in Cumming is where this particular role sits.

The Schedule and What It Actually Means

This is an alternative schedule position, which is worth understanding before you apply. You'll work five days a week including Saturdays, with Sundays and one weekday off. Weekday hours run 9am to 6pm; Saturdays are 9am to 5pm. Weinstein pays an extra $80 per pay period specifically for this schedule commitment. Saturday availability is genuinely valuable in leasing because that's when most prospective residents tour. If you can work Saturdays consistently, you're covering the highest-traffic window of the week.

Pay starts at $20 per hour and increases with experience, plus quarterly bonuses. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, vacation and sick time, birthday time off, a rent discount, and an Employee Assistance Program.

What You're Actually Building Here

No leasing experience is required. Weinstein is explicit about this, and it's not just recruiting language. They're looking for communication skills, a customer-first approach, and the ability to stay organized when priorities shift. The role covers a real range: guiding prospects through tours and applications, handling resident concerns, supporting property appearance, and managing administrative work. Nobody does just one thing.

  • Strong verbal and written communication, comfortable with both in-person and digital interactions
  • A genuine interest in helping people find a home, not just closing a deal
  • Comfort with a physical, on-your-feet role that includes walking the property and inspecting units
  • Ability to stay organized and composed when the day doesn't go as planned
  • Team orientation over individual credit

What separates strong candidates here isn't polish or a resume full of property management titles. It's consistency. Showing up with the same energy on a slow Tuesday as on a busy Saturday open house, following through on administrative tasks that don't feel glamorous, and building resident relationships that reduce turnover before it starts. Those habits, built early in a leasing role, translate directly into assistant manager and property manager positions down the road. Many of Weinstein's current leaders came up through leasing. That's not a marketing line; it's how the company is structured.

If you're coming from retail, hospitality, customer service, or any role where you've managed people and competing priorities at the same time, the skill set is closer than you think.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - EPA Certified
job.description:
It's 7:45 on a Tuesday morning. You're reviewing the work order queue before the office opens, spotting a reported HVAC issue in a second-floor unit and two plumbing tickets from the night before. By noon, you've cleared three work orders, checked in with a resident about a return visit, and knocked out a punch list item on a recently turned unit. That's the rhythm of this role.

The Work Itself
