Berkshire is offering a sign-on bonus eligible after 90 days, unlimited vacation for salaried employees, a 25% rent discount, and personal development plans. The company positions itself as culture-forward, and the posting reflects that tone throughout. If you've spent years at a shop where the culture pitch felt hollow, this is a place where that claim at least comes with specific benefits attached.

Strong candidates here won't just manage the property. They'll make their team better, read the financials like they matter, and treat resident relationships as a genuine competitive advantage. Average candidates manage tasks. The best ones build communities that retain residents and attract new ones without heavy concessions.

job.title: Assistant General Manager
job.description:
Most leasing teams succeed or struggle based on who's running the floor when the General Manager isn't there. That's the real weight of an Assistant General Manager role, and it's why Bozzuto takes the hire seriously. This isn't a stepping stone for someone waiting around for a promotion. It's a position that demands genuine leadership, sales instincts, and the ability to hold a team accountable with patience rather than pressure.

Based in Stamford, CT, this role sits inside one of the more active rental markets in the Northeast. Stamford draws a mix of commuters, young professionals, and corporate relocations, which means your prospect pool is varied. Residents have real expectations. They compare your community to other Class A options in the area, and they'll notice quickly if the experience doesn't match the price point. That context matters when you're conducting tours, handling service concerns, or coaching a leasing consultant through a tough follow-up conversation.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're moving between leasing, operations, and people management. You'll conduct personalized community tours that convert, not just inform. You'll manage delinquency, post rent receipts, and keep an eye on occupancy numbers. When the GM is out, you step into that decision-making seat without waiting to be told. The team looks to you, and you need to already know what you're doing when that moment comes.

Weekends are part of the schedule. Prospective residents shop on Saturdays and Sundays, so you'll work one to two weekends per month with corresponding weekdays off. That's not a small thing, and it's worth naming directly. If weekend availability is a real conflict, this role will create friction fast.

  • 2+ years in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • Familiarity with rent collection, delinquency management, and basic budget concepts
  • Experience with Yardi or comparable property management software preferred
  • Comfort creating and posting content across social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Real estate license required or must be obtained within 90 days of hire where applicable
  • Four-year degree or equivalent hands-on experience

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The candidates who thrive in this role aren't just organized. They read people well. Bozzuto's brand is built on the resident experience, which means your instincts for conversation, empathy, and follow-through carry as much weight as your leasing numbers. Someone who can close a lease but leaves residents feeling processed rather than heard won't last long here.

This role also tends to lead somewhere. AGMs at well-run companies like Bozzuto who demonstrate consistent financial performance and team development often move into General Manager seats within a few years. The exposure you get here, including budget accountability, delinquency management, and team oversight, builds a resume that translates directly into site leadership.

Compensation for this position ranges from $67,362 to $70,000, with additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a full property management role at a Bozzuto community in Abingdon, MD. You're running the operation: occupancy, NOI, team performance, client reporting, and resident experience. All of it lands on your desk. You'll own the financial performance of the property, which means you're reading your T-12, watching your T-3, managing delinquency, and presenting accurate operational and financial reports to clients on a consistent schedule. Bozzuto is a fee management company with a strong client-service orientation, so that client relationship piece isn't a footnote. It's core to this role.

On the leasing and marketing side, you're not just monitoring traffic numbers. You're partnering with the consumer marketing team to execute strategy, staying sharp on competitive intel, and making sure your concessions and pricing decisions are grounded in what the local market is actually doing. You'll also work one weekend per month, which is standard for a role where prospective residents are most active on Saturdays and Sundays.

The team leadership component here is real. Bozzuto puts genuine weight on coaching and developing the people under you. Rolling up your sleeves when the situation calls for it isn't optional, it's expected. If a make-ready needs hands on it or the leasing office is slammed, you're in it.

What You Bring

  • A four-year degree or equivalent experience that demonstrates you've earned it the hard way
  • Five or more years in property management, hospitality, or retail, with a track record that shows you can lead people and manage a P&L
  • Real budget experience. You know what variance analysis looks like and you're not intimidated by it
  • Proficiency with Yardi or a comparable platform
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, specifically the kind that work with both residents and clients
  • A professional presence that matches a Bozzuto community's positioning

Context Worth Knowing

Bozzuto operates across the mid-Atlantic and Northeast, and their properties tend to skew Class A with a service culture that's closer to hospitality than traditional multifamily. That's not a bad thing, but it does mean expectations around resident experience and community presentation are high. If you've come up in a high-volume lease-up environment or a more transactional operation, the adjustment is real. The upside is that Bozzuto invests in its people at a level you don't see at every management company, and the brand carries weight if you're thinking about where this role takes your career.

Strong candidates for this type of role typically separate themselves not on the leasing or financial side, but on team retention and client communication. Those two things are where average property managers lose the job and strong ones build a reputation. Worth keeping in mind when you're putting your application together.

job.title: Groundskeeper - Cortland at Fredericksburg - San Antonio, TX
job.description:
What This Job Actually Looks Like Day to Day

The Groundskeeper role at Cortland at Fredericksburg in San Antonio is physical, outdoor-heavy work. Most of your shift starts before residents notice anything is wrong, which is exactly the point. You're walking the property, picking up litter, cleaning common areas inside and out, and making sure the grounds look sharp before the first person heads out to their car in the morning. San Antonio summers are brutal, and you'll be working through them.

Beyond the daily trash and debris rounds, you'll handle seasonal deep-cleaning tasks, flag safety hazards to the maintenance team, and occasionally pitch in on resident events or community functions. You're not a maintenance tech, but you're close enough to the operation that your eyes matter. Spotting a broken light, a drainage issue, or a safety concern before it becomes a work order or a liability is part of the value you bring.

The maintenance team may pull you in to support service requests when volume gets heavy. That's not overstepping the role. It's how well-run communities actually function.

What You Bring

  • Prior groundskeeping, landscaping, custodial, or general labor experience is preferred, but not a hard requirement if you're reliable and willing to learn
  • Physical stamina for lifting, bending, and working outdoors in variable weather conditions
  • Attention to detail that goes beyond "good enough." You notice when something looks off
  • Punctuality and the ability to work independently without someone checking on you every hour
  • Basic familiarity with cleaning tools and safe material handling, or a genuine willingness to get up to speed quickly
  • Clear, respectful communication with residents and teammates when issues come up

A Realistic Lens on This Role

Curb appeal is not a small thing in multifamily. A well-kept exterior directly affects how prospective residents feel when they walk a property during a tour. It affects renewal decisions more than most people admit. The Groundskeeper is one of the first and most consistent impressions a community makes, which means this work carries real weight even if it doesn't always get recognized as such.

What separates strong candidates from average ones here isn't experience. It's consistency. Showing up every day, covering the full property, and not letting the small stuff slide, even on a 100-degree Tuesday in August, is what actually moves the needle. Cortland operates as a top-10 multifamily owner and operator nationally, and their properties are expected to reflect that. The standard is real, and this role is part of holding it.

job.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant - Cortland at Fredericksburg - San Antonio, TX
job.description:
Leasing is one of those roles where the job title undersells the actual work. At a community like Cortland at Fredericksburg, the leasing consultant isn't just processing applications. They're the first and most important impression a prospective resident gets, and they're directly responsible for occupancy, revenue, and the lived experience of the people who choose to call that community home.

What This Role Actually Requires

Cortland is looking for someone who treats leasing like a sales craft, not a hospitality gig. That distinction matters. You'll be managing a pipeline: following up on leads, tracking conversion rates, keeping your CRM current, and hitting KPIs that leadership will hold you to. The consultative side of the work means you're not reciting floor plan prices. You're listening for what a prospect actually needs, then matching that to a solution and closing with confidence.

You'll also own the resident experience side of things. That includes planning community events, managing the social media presence for your property, and handling objections without losing composure. Turning a hesitant prospect into a signed lease is a skill. So is keeping current residents engaged enough to renew instead of shop around.

  • At least 6 months of sales, customer-facing, or performance-driven experience (leasing experience is not required, but a track record of meeting goals is)
  • Comfort being measured: traffic, conversion, and occupancy numbers will reflect your work directly
  • CRM fluency, or the willingness to get there fast
  • Polished communication and personal presentation that fits a premium brand standard
  • Coachable. Cortland has a defined sales methodology, and the expectation is that you implement feedback quickly, not eventually

What This Role Builds

Leasing consultant is one of the most direct paths into property management leadership in the multifamily industry, and companies like Cortland tend to promote from within when they find someone who produces. The skills you develop here, specifically pipeline management, objection handling, and resident relationship-building, transfer cleanly into an Assistant Manager role where you'd add financial responsibilities like delinquency tracking and lease administration. From there, the path to Community Manager becomes much shorter.

One honest note: this role lives and dies on follow-up discipline. The difference between a strong leasing consultant and an average one usually isn't charisma. It's the person who sends the follow-up text two hours after a tour, logs it in the CRM, and calls again on day three. Cortland operates with metrics visibility, which means your conversion numbers are visible to your manager. That accountability is motivating for the right person and uncomfortable for the wrong one.

If you're someone who genuinely enjoys the close, takes pride in a well-managed pipeline, and wants to build a career in multifamily with a company that has real infrastructure behind it, this role at Cortland's Fredericksburg community in San Antonio is worth a serious look.

job.title: Property Manager in Training
job.description:
Most property management companies hire experienced managers and hand them a set of keys. Weinstein Properties does something different. This training role exists specifically to bring in sharp people from adjacent fields, customer service, hospitality, retail, sales, and develop them into site leaders with real operational ownership. It's a deliberate pipeline, not a gap-filler.

This position is based at Kings Crossing, a Weinstein-managed community in the Henrico/West End corridor of Richmond. You'll train alongside an existing manager, learning the day-to-day rhythm of the property before eventually stepping into your own site. The timeline for that transition varies, so if you need a guaranteed promotion date, this probably isn't the right fit. If you're comfortable building skills first and earning that step forward, there's a clear path here.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your days will split between leasing activity and operational support. You'll handle internet leads and phone inquiries, schedule tours, walk prospects through the community, and process applications through to signed leases. On the resident side, you're the person helping someone understand their renewal options, process a notice to vacate, add a pet to their lease, or get clarity on their account balance. That part of the job requires patience and consistency. Not every interaction is easy.

You'll also work closely with maintenance. That means walking make-ready apartments to confirm punch list items are complete, following up on open work orders, and keeping an eye on the overall condition of the property. Rent posting, delinquency follow-up, move-out processing, and security deposit dispositions round out the administrative side. And because this is a leadership track, you'll be expected to help coach the team and contribute to community events, not just execute tasks assigned to you.

  • Prior management or team leadership experience is required (1 to 3 years)
  • Property management background is a plus but not a dealbreaker
  • Strong administrative skills and comfort managing competing priorities
  • Clear, confident communication with residents, prospects, and team members
  • Self-directed work style. You won't be micromanaged, but you will be expected to stay busy
  • Schedule includes weekday and rotating Saturday coverage (Sundays off)

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Weinstein has been family-owned for over 70 years and manages more than 60 communities across five states. That scale means real career mobility, but the culture still runs on a hands-on, people-first approach. The candidates who thrive in this program aren't just organized and friendly. They take genuine ownership of their property's condition, their team's performance, and the resident experience. They notice things. They follow through without being reminded. They treat the property like it's theirs.

If your background is in hotel front desk management, retail leadership, or a high-volume customer service environment, the translation to property management is more direct than you might think. Leasing is sales. Resident relations is hospitality. The operational side adds a layer, but the core skills carry over well. This role pays starting at $25 per hour with quarterly bonuses and a sign-on bonus discussed at the interview stage.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is one of the few roles in property management where you can enter with a customer service background and, within a year or two, be running the front office of a multifamily community. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, that path is built into the job description rather than left to chance. The company's internal career progression puts the Leasing Consultant role directly below Assistant Community Manager, and their Learning and Development program exists specifically to close that gap.

The position is based at Hawthorne at Hixson, a community in Hixson, TN, where you'd be the first voice prospects hear and the first face they see. Your days will center on touring apartments, converting leads to signed leases, and keeping the resident experience warm after move-in. That means following up on web and phone inquiries, completing leasing paperwork accurately, supporting renewal goals, and helping organize resident events that build a genuine sense of community. The office runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays from 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to keep you at 40 hours. Occasional evenings may come up around community events.

Compensation here is structured to reward performance. Beyond an hourly base, you're eligible for monthly leasing commissions and renewal bonuses, which means your income grows directly with your ability to close and retain residents. That commission structure is a good early lesson in how NOI thinking works at the property level, and it's the kind of context that makes the jump to a management role feel natural rather than abstract.

What the Role Asks Of You

  • At least one year in customer service, sales, or apartment leasing (preferred, not required)
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Valid driver's license
  • A CALP designation is a plus if you already have it
  • Comfort communicating across phone, email, and in-person conversations

What separates strong leasing consultants from average ones isn't usually the ability to give a tour. It's the follow-up. Most prospects visit two or three communities before deciding. The ones who choose Hawthorne do so because someone followed up with them thoughtfully, remembered a detail from the conversation, and answered their specific question rather than giving a scripted response. If that kind of relationship-building comes naturally to you, this role builds real, transferable skills in sales, resident retention, and community operations that carry value well beyond this particular job.

Hawthorne is one of the 50 largest multifamily operators in the country, with a concentration in the Southeast. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, and paid parental and adoption leave. Telehealth access and company-paid life insurance round out the package.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Most apartment communities don't fail because of bad leasing. They fail because the physical asset deteriorates faster than the team can respond. The Maintenance Supervisor role exists to prevent exactly that, sitting at the intersection of technical skill, team leadership, and resident experience.

Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor at Hawthorne at Bear Creek, a community in Asheville, NC. This isn't a wrench-turning role dressed up with a title. You're running a maintenance operation: scheduling your team, managing the budget, overseeing unit turns, coordinating vendors, and keeping a preventative maintenance program alive quarter after quarter.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On a typical day, you're walking the property before the office opens, triaging overnight service requests, and confirming your team has clear assignments before 8 AM. By mid-morning, you might be inspecting a vacant unit before it goes on the make-ready schedule, catching a punch list item that would've delayed move-in. By afternoon, you're following up with a vendor on a capital project or reviewing inventory to make sure supplies don't run short during a heavy turn cycle. On-call rotation is part of the deal, and Asheville's weather means after-hours calls aren't hypothetical.

The role requires at least three years of apartment maintenance or skilled trade experience, with HVAC, plumbing, or electrical work in the background. EPA certification is required. CPO certification is strongly preferred. Prior supervisory or lead technician experience matters here because you'll be mentoring techs, not just working alongside them.

Qualifications Worth Having

  • Minimum 3 years of apartment maintenance or skilled trade experience (HVAC, plumbing, or electrical)
  • Supervisory or lead technician experience, strongly preferred
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA certification (required)
  • CPO certification (highly preferred, may be required depending on state)
  • High school diploma or GED

Hawthorne offers a bonus structure that includes monthly renewal incentives, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses on top of hourly pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance. There's also an education reimbursement program and a formal career path program for employees who want to grow within the company.

Here's the career angle worth knowing: Maintenance Supervisors who build strong vendor relationships, keep turns tight, and develop their teams tend to move into Regional Maintenance Director roles or transition into facilities and capex-focused positions as companies scale their portfolios. The skills compound quickly. Managing a preventative maintenance program teaches asset thinking. Running a team teaches operational leadership. Both open doors well beyond any single property.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is usually vendor management and turn discipline. Anyone can fix things. The supervisors who advance are the ones who keep the make-ready schedule from slipping, catch problems before residents report them, and build a team that doesn't need to be micromanaged on routine work.

job.title: Limpiador de Oficinas (Mon-Fri, 6PM-10PM)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is an evening porter position covering common areas at a Comstock-managed office property in Reston, Virginia. The shift runs Monday through Friday, 6PM to 10PM, which means you're working after the building empties out. That's actually a real advantage: fewer interruptions, a clear checklist, and the satisfaction of leaving a space genuinely clean before the next workday starts.

Your daily work covers lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, and public spaces. You'll follow cleaning schedules and checklists assigned by the Senior Operations Manager, track supply inventory, and keep the janitorial closet organized and hazard-free. Pressure washing is part of the rotation. When events happen at the property, you'll help with setup and breakdown. If something looks broken, unsafe, or damaged, you document it and report it. Simple accountability, consistently applied.

At the end of each shift, you complete the required documentation and hand off properly to whoever follows you. That handoff discipline matters more than most people realize. A missed note about a wet floor or a low supply stock creates problems for the next shift and reflects on the whole team.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with no major violations
  • Ability to lift, push, or pull up to 50 pounds and stay on your feet for extended periods
  • Flexibility to occasionally work weekends or outside your regular hours during high-traffic events
  • Strong time management and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision
  • A professional, courteous manner with property staff, tenants, and visitors
  • Comfort working around cleaning chemicals and following safety protocols correctly

Context Worth Knowing

Comstock is a significant player in the Reston Town Center corridor, which has grown into one of Northern Virginia's denser mixed-use nodes. Office properties here serve a mix of tech, government contracting, and professional services tenants who have real expectations about building presentation. A porter who takes visible pride in clean lobbies and well-maintained exteriors directly supports how those tenants experience the property every single day.

Porter and groundskeeper roles at well-managed commercial and mixed-use properties are often a starting point for people who grow into facilities technician or building operations positions. If you're reliable, attentive, and show initiative, those paths are real. The skills you build here, chemical safety, equipment care, maintenance documentation, shift handoffs, transfer directly into maintenance technician work and beyond.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) matching, life insurance, free parking with EV charging, parental leave, and an annual professional development fund. For a part-time evening shift, that's a meaningful package.

job.title: Union Porter (Mon-Fri, 6PM-10PM)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is an evening shift porter role covering common areas at Comstock's ParkX properties in Reston. You're coming in at 6PM when the daytime team wraps up, which means you're often the person who sets the tone for how the property looks through the rest of the night. Lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, and public spaces need consistent attention. You'll run through daily cleaning checklists, handle pressure washing assignments, and keep janitorial storage areas organized and hazard-free.

Event support is part of the job. When the property hosts gatherings or public events, you help with setup and breakdown, and you respond to cleanliness issues as they come up rather than waiting for someone to escalate them. End-of-shift documentation matters here. You're responsible for a clean handoff, noting any maintenance issues, equipment damage, or safety concerns so nothing slips between shifts. Supply inventory, equipment upkeep, and compliance with cleaning standards all fall within your daily scope.

The Monday through Friday schedule is consistent, but flexibility for after-hours or weekend coverage during peak periods is expected. This is a union position, which means you'll have a defined set of responsibilities and protections that go with the role.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with no major violations
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and sustain physical work across a full shift, including standing, stooping, climbing stairs, and working in variable temperatures
  • Genuine comfort interacting with residents, guests, and property staff in a professional, courteous way
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to follow cleaning schedules and checklists accurately
  • Willingness to cover for coworkers and adjust to shifting priorities without needing close supervision
  • Reliable attendance and a solid understanding of why punctuality matters at shift start

Context Worth Knowing

Reston is a dense, mixed-use market where Comstock has built a significant footprint around transit-oriented development. The ParkX brand specifically manages parking and related property services across Comstock's portfolio, so this role sits within a team that touches multiple properties and interacts with a real cross-section of tenants and visitors each evening. The work is physical and repetitive by nature, but the evening timing and the union structure offer a degree of predictability that service roles don't always provide.

Strong candidates in this type of role tend to be the ones who treat a clean janitorial closet with the same care they give a lobby. The details no one sees directly affect the details everyone does. If you take ownership of your space and show up consistently, there's room to grow within Comstock's expanding portfolio.

job.title: Business Manager - Olympus at Memorial
job.description:
Olympus Property has earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer recognition three years running (2023, 2024, and 2025). That's not a marketing footnote. It reflects something real about how this company operates, and it matters for anyone evaluating where to take their career next.

The Business Manager role at Olympus at Memorial is, in plain terms, the property manager position. You're running the asset. That means owning the financial performance, the team, the resident experience, and the vendor relationships all at once. You'll work directly with Regional Leadership to set strategy, build annual business plans, and analyze monthly performance against budget projections. If you're the kind of person who reads a T-12 the way other people read a news feed, you'll be comfortable here.

Day to day, this role pulls you in a lot of directions. Morning might be a budget conversation with your Regional VP. Afternoon could be a property inspection, a vendor negotiation on a service contract, or coaching a leasing consultant through a difficult prospect interaction. The financial side and the people side don't take turns. They happen simultaneously, and the best candidates for this role don't just tolerate that reality. They're wired for it.

This is a Class A community, and Olympus has a preference for candidates who've managed at that level before. Luxury assets carry specific expectations around curb appeal, amenity presentation, and resident communication. The bar for "market-ready condition" is higher, and so is the resident's willingness to escalate when it isn't met. That's not a reason to be discouraged. It's just the honest context for what you're walking into.

The team you'll lead includes both office and maintenance staff. That cross-functional dynamic is worth thinking about. Strong candidates here don't just manage their leasing team and hand maintenance off to a supervisor. They understand enough about make-ready timelines and punch list quality to have real conversations with their maintenance lead, hold the standard, and back their team up when vendors push back on scope or pricing.

What You'll Need

  • At least two years of direct multifamily property management experience, with Class A or luxury background preferred
  • Familiarity with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite platforms (strongly preferred, not just a nice-to-have)
  • Comfort with financial reporting, budget forecasting, and performance analysis
  • Full-time availability Monday through Friday, with flexibility for resident events and after-hours situations when they arise
  • Experience supervising and developing both leasing and maintenance staff

The base pay range is $70,000 to $80,000 annually, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program, among others. Olympus also invests in leadership development through their Budget Camp and Leadership Conferences, which matters if you're thinking about where this role leads. Business Managers at companies like Olympus are a natural pipeline for Regional Manager positions, particularly for candidates who demonstrate strong financial acumen alongside team development skills.

If the culture-first language in property management job postings usually makes you skeptical, that's fair. But Olympus builds recognition programs, career pathing, and team events into the actual structure of the job, not just the recruiting copy. Whether that fits how you work is worth thinking through before you apply.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - The Preserve at Greenway Park
job.description:
Leasing Consultant roles at apartment communities are part sales, part customer service, part administrative grind. At The Preserve at Greenway Park in Casper, WY, you're the first face a prospective resident sees, and the last person who makes sure their move-in paperwork is actually ready before they show up with a moving truck.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Most of your time splits between working the leasing floor and managing what happens around it. You're greeting walk-ins, taking calls, and guiding prospects through unit tours while explaining floor plan differences, pricing, and availability. You're closing leases, yes, but you're also entering data, preparing lease files, and coordinating move-in logistics so nothing falls through the cracks on key day.

Beyond the sales cycle, you're helping existing residents when concerns come up, which means some days feel more like problem-solving than selling. You'll also spend time outside the property visiting local businesses and apartment locators to build referral relationships and drive traffic back to the community. Resident events are part of the job too, including some after-hours availability on a monthly basis. It's not constant, but it's real, and you should expect it.

The schedule includes both Saturday and Sunday availability. That's non-negotiable here, and worth knowing upfront rather than finding out later.

What Olympus Is Looking For

  • At least one year of apartment leasing experience, or comparable time in a customer-facing role in retail, hospitality, or restaurants where you were genuinely selling, not just assisting
  • Comfort with a sales conversation, including closing without being pushy about it
  • Organized enough to handle lease paperwork, move-in prep, and database entry without things slipping
  • A genuine interest in helping people find a place to live, not just filling units

Pay starts between $15 and $18 per hour depending on experience, and the role includes monthly leasing commissions and resident renewal bonuses, so your actual take-home has real upside tied to your performance. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program, among others.

Where This Role Can Take You

Olympus has been recognized by the National Apartment Association as a top employer three years running (2023, 2024, 2025), and they're transparent about career pathing being part of how they operate. Leasing Consultant is a well-worn entry point into property management. Strong performers here typically move into Senior Leasing, Assistant Manager, or eventually Property Manager roles, especially at a company that promotes from within. The skills you build here, closing leases, reading residents, managing traffic and follow-up, translate directly into the operational side of running a property.

If you want a role where showing up with energy and follow-through actually shows up in your paycheck, this one is structured to reward that.

job.title: Pool Attendant
job.description:
Seasonal, outdoor, and genuinely straightforward. Pool attendant roles at apartment communities like Bexley Westshore exist because residents expect a clean, safe, well-managed amenity experience on their days off, and that doesn't happen without someone present and paying attention.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You're the person on the pool deck during the hours it matters most: weekend afternoons and Friday evenings when resident traffic peaks. Your job is to make sure only authorized residents and their guests are using the pool, that the deck and bathrooms stay clean and trash-free, and that community rules get enforced calmly and consistently. You'll also help close down the area at the end of each shift.

Occasionally, you may walk through other amenity spaces like the gym or business center to do a quick spot check. Nothing complicated, but it does require someone who stays alert and doesn't need to be told twice to handle something they notice on their own.

The schedule is fixed and part-time: Friday evenings and Saturday and Sunday afternoons, totaling around 20 hours per week. The role runs through September or October, with some flexibility if your schedule changes before then. This is a seasonal position. It's not designed to become full-time, and Weinstein Properties is upfront about that.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • Reliable. Residents count on amenities being properly staffed, and showing up consistently matters more than almost anything else here.
  • Comfortable working independently without a supervisor nearby at all times
  • Able to enforce rules with residents in a firm but non-confrontational way
  • Physically comfortable being outdoors for extended periods in warm weather
  • CPR or First Aid certified (a plus, not a requirement; this is not a lifeguard position)
  • Has reliable transportation to get to the property on time every shift

Pay runs $15 to $17 per hour. A background check is part of the process.

One Thing Worth Knowing

Enforcing pool rules is the part of this job that trips people up. Most residents are fine. Some aren't happy when told their guest count is over the limit or that the pool is closing. If you're the kind of person who can hold a boundary without making it a confrontation, you'll do well here. That skill, handling low-stakes but uncomfortable resident interactions, is something that transfers directly if you ever want to move into a leasing or assistant manager role at a residential community down the road.

Weinstein Properties manages a number of communities across the Southeast, so if you perform well and show genuine reliability, there's context for future opportunities within the company even if this specific role is seasonal.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Dylan Point Loma
job.description:
It's a Saturday afternoon, and a couple walks in without an appointment, having driven past Dylan Point Loma twice before finally stopping. You've got ten minutes to turn that curiosity into a signed lease. That's the job.

What This Role Actually Involves

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. Dylan Point Loma in San Diego is one of those communities, and this Leasing Consultant position sits at the front line of keeping occupancy where it needs to be. You're the first impression, the tour guide, the application processor, and the move-in coordinator, all at once.

Day to day, you're greeting and qualifying prospective residents, walking them through units, and converting traffic into signed leases. You'll prepare and execute lease agreements, maintain accurate rental files, and enter data into the property management system with enough precision that nothing falls through the cracks at month-end. You'll also coordinate with the maintenance team to make sure new residents move into a clean, punch-list-complete unit. When current residents come to you with complaints or maintenance concerns, you handle them professionally and follow through.

Saturdays are required. Point Loma sees weekend traffic, and that's when leasing decisions often get made.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of property management or leasing experience (preferred, not required if your sales background is strong)
  • Genuine sales ability and customer service instincts, not just a friendly personality
  • Comfort with leasing software and accurate data entry
  • Professional communication, written and verbal
  • Availability to work Saturdays consistently
  • Willingness to work within a team that expects follow-through, not just front-desk charm

Compensation runs $21 to $22 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonuses tied to performance. MG Properties also offers company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid holidays, sick time, and rental discounts for employees.

One thing worth knowing about MG Properties specifically: they promote from within at a rate that's notable for a company their size. A Leasing Consultant who hits occupancy targets, keeps delinquency low, and handles resident relations well is exactly the profile that moves into an Assistant Manager seat. The administrative work you do here, organizing files, processing applications, closing leases cleanly, builds the operational foundation that makes that next step a realistic one, not just a talking point in an interview.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Sterling Village Apartments
job.description:
Maintenance Technicians at apartment communities wear a lot of hats. On any given day, you're the person a resident trusts to fix what's broken, the teammate keeping the property presentable, and the on-call responder when something goes wrong at 10pm. At a property like Sterling Village Apartments in Vallejo, that range of responsibility is exactly what the job looks like.

What the Work Actually Involves

MG Properties is a well-established regional operator with over 30 years managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. They're looking for a Maintenance Technician who can handle the full scope of property upkeep, not just one or two trades. That means service requests across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and appliances, plus grounds and common area cleaning, painting, and apartment turns. Turns are worth calling out specifically: getting a unit make-ready between residents requires attention to detail, a solid punch list mindset, and the ability to move efficiently without cutting corners.

You'll also participate in an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That's a real commitment, and it's worth knowing going in. It's not every night, but when it's your week, it's your week.

  • Complete resident maintenance service requests across all major trades
  • Perform apartment turnovers and make-ready work
  • Handle appliance repairs, painting, and general upkeep
  • Maintain grounds, offices, and common areas
  • Participate in on-call emergency rotation

What MG Properties Is Looking For

Two or more years of hands-on apartment maintenance experience is preferred, ideally on a property of 200 units or larger. That scale matters because larger communities generate more concurrent work orders, and you need to be able to triage and prioritize without constant direction. Multi-trade competency is required, not optional. Customer service attitude is listed as a key qualifier, and they mean it. Residents interact with maintenance staff more directly than almost anyone else on a property team, and how you show up at someone's door sets the tone for how they feel about where they live.

Reliable transportation is required. You'll need to get yourself to the property and, depending on the on-call situation, potentially respond from home.

Compensation and Team Culture

The pay range is $25 to $26 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of base wages. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, paid holidays, paid sick time, and rental discounts. That last one is meaningful if you're local to the Vallejo area and looking to reduce your own housing costs.

MG Properties talks about employee development as a real priority, not just a line in a job description. For a technician with broad trade skills, that can translate into a path toward lead maintenance or even a maintenance supervisor role as the company continues to grow its Western U.S. portfolio. The skills you build managing turns, handling complex service requests, and working across trades are directly transferable to higher-level maintenance leadership positions. Companies like this tend to promote from within when they find people who show up consistently and communicate well with both residents and management.

If you've got solid hands-on experience, a calm approach to resident interactions, and you're comfortable being part of an on-call rotation, this is a role worth taking seriously.

job.title: Dual-Site Leasing & Marketing Manager
job.description:
Scion is one of the more established names in student housing, and this role sits at the intersection of leasing, marketing, and community operations across two Fort Collins properties. The title is Customer Experience Manager, but the job is really about driving occupancy and retention while keeping two communities running smoothly day to day.

You'll split your time between both sites, which means your organizational discipline matters as much as your sales instincts. Student housing has its own rhythm. Traffic surges during lease-up season, the annual turn is its own project within the job, and your residents are signing leases months before they move in. You need to understand that cycle and stay ahead of it.

On the leasing and marketing side, you're executing social media strategy across Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook, running on-campus events, doing weekly market surveys, and working toward revenue goals tracked through KPIs. You're not just reporting numbers. You're expected to read trends and adjust. On the operations side, you're inspecting curb appeal, coordinating work orders, keeping tabs on resident satisfaction, and helping plan and execute the annual turnover process alongside the General Manager and Facilities Supervisor. Student housing turns are high-volume and time-compressed. If you've done one, you know what that means.

This is also a people leadership role. You'll coach Experience Team Members, help with onboarding, and make sure the team stays Fair Housing compliant. You won't be managing the property solo. You're supporting the GM, but you're also expected to lead independently when needed.

What this role requires

  • At least two years in customer service, sales, or community management (student housing experience is a real advantage here)
  • Comfort working up to six days per week during peak seasons, including turn
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and ideally Entrata
  • Strong written and verbal communication across formats: in-person, social, email
  • Ability to manage competing priorities across two sites without dropping details
  • College degree preferred but not required with relevant experience

The base salary range is $45,000 to $55,000, with a discretionary annual bonus and a full benefits package including health, dental, vision, 401k matching, and paid parental leave. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

One thing worth knowing: candidates who perform well in student housing CXM roles tend to move into General Manager positions relatively quickly. The dual-site scope here gives you exposure that single-property roles don't, and Scion's size means there are paths forward if you perform. That's not a guarantee, but it's a real pattern in this sector.

job.title: Insurance Claims Administrator
job.description:
A vendor's certificate of insurance expired three weeks ago. Nobody caught it. Now there's a slip-and-fall claim at one of the properties, and suddenly everyone's looking for the file. That's the kind of situation this role exists to prevent, and to clean up when prevention fails.

What This Role Actually Covers

The Scion Group operates in the student housing space, and their Chicago corporate office is looking for an Insurance Claims Administrator to sit within the legal and compliance function. It's a broad seat. You're not just tracking claims, you're also helping draft and revise housing agreements and commercial contracts, supporting outside counsel on litigation matters, and keeping vendor insurance compliance from falling through the cracks.

Day to day, you'll coordinate the full lifecycle of insurance claims on behalf of the company and its managed properties, respond to property staff questions about legal and policy matters, and flag resident complaints or regulatory issues that need attorney attention. You'll also support entity and asset acquisition work by coordinating with inside and outside counsel. The role reports into the legal team, with direction coming from staff attorneys, the VP of Legal Affairs, and General Counsel.

This is a corporate headquarters position with standard business hours. No on-call, no weekends managing turns. That's a real differentiator from most property-side roles.

What They're Looking For

  • Associate's degree or paralegal certification preferred
  • At least one year in a legal, insurance, or administrative role (a plus, not a hard requirement)
  • Solid organizational skills and clear written communication
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office; familiarity with property management systems is a bonus
  • Eligibility to work in the U.S. (no visa sponsorship available)

The salary range is $50,000 to $65,000 base, plus a discretionary annual bonus. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental and maternal leave, and learning reimbursement.

What separates the candidates who thrive in this kind of role from those who struggle is usually not legal knowledge. It's the ability to track a dozen open items simultaneously without letting anything go quiet. Insurance claims have a way of aging badly when nobody's watching them. If you're the person who builds the spreadsheet before anyone asks you to, you'll fit right in.

For someone with paralegal ambitions or an interest in real estate law, this is a legitimate foot in the door at a company with a significant portfolio footprint in the student housing sector.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
A prospective resident stops by Saturday afternoon with her parents in tow, a stack of questions, and a move-in date that's six weeks out. You're the first real impression Cottages of Clemson makes on all three of them. How that conversation goes matters more than almost anything else happening that day.

What This Role Actually Covers

The Experience Team Member title is a deliberate one. Scion builds its student communities around the idea that leasing and customer experience aren't separate functions, and this role reflects that. You're doing tours and closing leads, yes. But you're also helping plan and execute resident engagement events, managing the social media presence for the community, fielding package pickups, and occasionally handling after-hours lockout calls when you're on rotation. The job is genuinely varied, and some days will pull you in four directions at once.

On the administrative side, you'll track maintenance requests and follow up to make sure they move forward, keep the office and common areas presentable, and stay current on community policies, floor plans, and local market knowledge so you can answer questions with confidence rather than guessing. You'll also pass feedback up to management when you're hearing the same objections or concerns from multiple prospects. That kind of ground-level insight is useful, and Scion actually wants it.

Student housing has its own rhythm. The leasing cycle is compressed, turn season is intense, and your resident population turns over in large waves. If you've worked in conventional multifamily, the pace here is different. If you're coming in fresh, expect the summer and turn periods to be genuinely demanding stretches that require full availability.

What Scion Is Looking For

  • Strong interpersonal skills with a wide range of people, including residents, parents, and university contacts
  • Comfort with an unpredictable daily schedule and a willingness to shift priorities quickly
  • Reliability. This is a team environment, and your coworkers depend on you showing up and following through
  • Availability during summers, holidays, and turn periods, which are non-negotiable busy seasons in student housing
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

What separates strong candidates here isn't a leasing background, it's genuine people instincts combined with the discipline to handle the administrative side without letting it slip. Plenty of personable candidates struggle with the follow-through. The ones who do well in student leasing tend to be organized enough to track details while staying warm and present in every conversation.

This role is based on-site at Cottages of Clemson in Central, South Carolina, with standard business hours plus an after-hours on-call rotation shared among the team.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing leasing runs on a cycle unlike any other asset class. You're not managing steady monthly traffic; you're building toward a single renewal and new lease deadline that determines whether the property hits occupancy before the academic year starts. At Alight Fullerton, that cycle is constant, and the Experience Team Member role sits right at the center of it.

Scion is one of the larger purpose-built student housing operators in the country, and this part-time position at their Fullerton property is a ground-level leasing and customer experience role. The title is Experience Team Member, but the work is real leasing work: tours, follow-up, sales conversations, handling objections, and feeding intel back to the management team about what's stalling conversions. You're also the face of the community on social platforms and at resident events, which matters in student housing where peer referrals and Instagram presence actually move traffic.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

On a typical shift, you might open the office, walk the clubhouse and amenity spaces to make sure they're presentable, and then run back-to-back tours with prospective residents or their parents. Package logging, maintenance request coordination, and leasing admin fill the gaps. There's an after-hours on-call rotation for lockouts, so flexibility isn't just a preference; it's a real requirement. The role ramps up hard during Turn, the period between leases when units flip for incoming residents, and availability during summers and holidays is expected.

  • Conduct property and amenity tours for prospective residents
  • Execute leasing and engagement initiatives set by the management team
  • Support social media content and community outreach
  • Log and retrieve resident packages
  • Coordinate maintenance request follow-up
  • Assist with office and common area upkeep
  • Participate in after-hours lockout rotation as needed

Who Tends to Do Well Here

Candidates who thrive in this role usually have one thing in common: they're genuinely comfortable talking to a wide range of people, from 18-year-old freshmen to skeptical parents co-signing a lease. Strong performers don't wait for traffic to come to them; they're proactive about local marketing ideas and notice when a sales objection keeps coming up, then flag it. Average candidates show up for tours and call it done. Strong ones treat every interaction as a data point.

This is a part-time role paying $17 to $19 per hour in California. It's a solid entry point into property management, and student housing experience specifically transfers well to conventional multifamily leasing roles down the road, particularly for anyone interested in eventually moving into an Assistant Manager or Leasing Manager position at a larger community.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Hawthorne Residential Partners operates around 50 communities across the Southeast, and Park Forest in Greensboro is one of those properties. The Assistant Community Manager role here is genuinely a two-track job: part leasing, part finance, part team leadership when the Community Manager is out. You're not just answering phones and giving tours. You're watching delinquency reports, posting payments, reviewing ledgers, and making sure the numbers tell an accurate story before they hit regional leadership.

Greensboro's rental market has stayed competitive, with steady renter demand driven in part by the university presence and a consistent in-migration of workforce renters. That context matters because occupancy and renewals aren't passive here. You'll need to actively convert traffic and retain residents through genuine relationship-building, not just lease incentives.

Day to day, this role moves fast. Mornings might involve delinquency follow-up calls and ledger audits. Afternoons shift toward tours, lease paperwork, and renewal conversations. Saturdays are working days, and the office runs Monday through Friday from 9 to 6, with Saturdays from 10 to 4. One weekday off rotates in to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Resident events can pull you in on evenings too, so flexibility isn't optional.

What separates a strong candidate here from an average one is comfort with the financial side of operations. A lot of people come into assistant manager roles with solid leasing instincts but shaky confidence on rent collection, eviction coordination, and reading a financial report with real understanding. If you can hold both skill sets at once, you'll move faster through Hawthorne's internal Career Path Program, which is a real pathway toward Community Manager, not just language in a job posting.

What Hawthorne is Looking For

  • Two years of property management experience, ideally with at least six months in an assistant manager seat
  • Demonstrated ability to handle delinquency management, payment posting, and ledger review
  • Comfort leading a small team when the Community Manager is unavailable
  • Strong conflict resolution skills, especially in resident-facing situations that require patience and follow-through
  • Valid driver's license; a CALP designation is a bonus but not required
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits cover medical, dental, vision, 401k with match, paid time off including your birthday, pet insurance, telehealth access, and paid parental and adoption leave. Life insurance is company-paid.

If you've been doing leasing work and want to grow into a role with real financial responsibility and a clear path toward community management, this position is structured to support that move.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the intersection of leasing, finance, and team operations. On any given day, you might open the office, pull a delinquency report, follow up on outstanding balances by phone, then shift immediately into conducting a tour for a prospect who walked in off the street. That range is real, and it's daily.

You'll support leasing activity end to end: responding to leads, walking prospects through available homes, and making sure lease applications and renewals are completed accurately and on time. Occupancy goals are shared goals here, and your leasing performance contributes directly to them. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which means you're thinking about resident engagement and community identity, not just transaction volume.

On the financial side, you're handling rent collection, payment posting, ledger reviews, and delinquency follow-up. When accounts go sideways, you're coordinating the eviction process alongside the Community Manager. This isn't background administrative work. You're expected to understand what the numbers mean and flag problems before they compound.

When the Community Manager is out, you run the operation. That means keeping the team on task, handling resident concerns with professionalism, and making judgment calls that keep things moving. The people who thrive here don't wait to be told what needs attention.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of property management experience, with six months in an assistant manager capacity preferred
  • Comfort reading and interpreting financial reports, including delinquency tracking and account ledgers
  • Leasing experience: you know how to convert a tour, not just conduct one
  • Strong conflict resolution instincts. Resident disputes happen. How you handle them matters.
  • A valid driver's license
  • CALP accreditation is a plus but not required

The Bigger Picture

Hawthorne Residential Partners is a top-50 multifamily management company with deep roots in the Southeast. Atlanta is a competitive multifamily market with consistent renter demand and a wide spectrum of properties across Class A and B assets. Knowing how to drive retention in that environment, not just traffic, is what separates strong assistant managers from ones who plateau.

Hawthorne has a formal Career Path Program that connects this role directly to a Community Manager seat. If you're someone who wants to run your own community within a defined timeline, this structure exists to make that happen. Total targeted compensation is $75,000 including hourly pay, monthly leasing and renewal commissions, and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid parental leave, and paid time off that includes your birthday.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday with Saturday hours required. One weekday off is built in to keep you at 40 hours. Resident events may occasionally pull you outside standard hours. That's the honest reality of community management, and it's worth knowing before you apply.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning and you're already fielding a call from a frustrated resident before the leasing office opens, reviewing a delinquency report, and mentally prepping your team for a busy midweek traffic push. That's the reality of this role. It's demanding, varied, and genuinely rewarding when your community is running the way it should.

Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the top 50 multifamily management companies in the country and a company with deep Southeast roots, is hiring a Community Manager for one of their Atlanta apartment communities. This is a full-scope operations role. You're responsible for financial performance, leasing results, resident satisfaction, team development, and the day-to-day health of the property. If you've worked your way up through leasing and assistant management and you're ready to own a community, this is worth a close look.

What You're Actually Responsible For

On the financial side, you'll manage the budget, oversee rent collection and deposit accounting, track delinquency, and report on community performance using Yardi. You'll work with ownership and regional leadership, so comfort reading financial reports and making decisions within budget constraints is genuinely necessary, not just a box on the job description.

Operationally, you'll drive leasing and renewal performance to hit occupancy goals, partner with maintenance on work orders and preventative care, manage vendor relationships, and conduct regular property inspections. You'll also handle escalated resident concerns, monitor online reputation, coordinate resident events, and manage social media content for the community.

Team leadership is central to this position. You'll hire, train, and coach both office and maintenance staff, run weekly team meetings, and build a culture of accountability and service. Hawthorne calls it their "Live It" culture, and they expect their Community Managers to model it daily.

What the Right Candidate Looks Like

  • At least two years of property management experience, including time as a Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager
  • Six months of direct Community Manager experience in multifamily, strongly preferred
  • Proficiency in Yardi and Knock preferred; Microsoft Office required
  • Valid driver's license required; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate license is a plus
  • Strong financial literacy, specifically the ability to read and act on reporting rather than just produce it
  • Genuine conflict resolution skills, the kind you've actually used with difficult residents, not just claimed on a resume

The work schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays 10 to 4, with one weekday off to maintain a 40-hour week. Some evenings and weekend availability may be needed for resident events.

Atlanta's multifamily market has seen meaningful rent moderation over the past year after a heavy wave of new supply, particularly in submarkets like Midtown, Buckhead, and the northern suburbs. That means Community Managers here are being asked to work harder on retention, get creative with renewals, and keep a close eye on concessions. A candidate who understands how to hold occupancy in a competitive environment without sacrificing NOI is exactly who thrives in this market right now.

Compensation targets $85,000 total, with monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses layered on top of base salary. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off including your birthday, pet insurance, and paid parental leave. Hawthorne also runs a formal career path program, and the Community Manager to Regional Manager track is one they actively support.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do at Brookefield

This role puts you at the front door, literally and figuratively. You're the first person a prospective resident meets, the voice that answers the phone, and the team member who follows up after a tour to keep a lead warm. Day to day, you're conducting personalized apartment tours, responding to inquiries across phone, email, and web platforms, processing lease applications and move-in paperwork, and helping push the community toward its occupancy and renewal goals.

It's not just transactional work. Hawthorne calls this role a Leasing and Live It Specialist, which signals something real about how they operate. You're expected to build genuine connections with residents, coordinate community events, and help maintain the kind of environment that makes people want to renew. That means you'll be checking in on common areas, supporting social media and local outreach efforts, and keeping tabs on what competitor properties in the Raleigh market are doing.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with Saturdays from 10 to 4. You'll get one weekday off to keep the week at 40 hours. Resident events and community needs can occasionally pull you outside those hours, so flexibility matters here.

What You Bring

  • A high school diploma or GED. That's the floor.
  • At least one year in customer service, sales, or apartment leasing is preferred, though not required if you can demonstrate the right instincts
  • A valid driver's license
  • Confidence communicating in person, by phone, and in writing
  • A natural ability to listen to what a prospect actually needs and match them to the right home, not just the next available unit
  • A CALP (Certified Apartment Leasing Professional) credential is a bonus, not a barrier to entry

Strong candidates in leasing roles tend to share one trait that's hard to teach: they're comfortable with the follow-up. Sending the second email, making the check-in call, staying engaged with a lead who went quiet. That persistence, when paired with genuine warmth, is what separates good leasing consultants from great ones.

Where This Role Fits

Hawthorne is a top-50 multifamily operator with deep roots in the Southeast, and Brookefield at 2400 Cluette Drive sits in a well-established Raleigh submarket with real competition for residents. Your market awareness matters here, not just your personality.

On the career side, Hawthorne runs a formal Career Path Program with the specific goal of moving Leasing Consultants into Assistant Community Manager roles. If you want to grow into operations, financial reporting, and team oversight, the path exists and the company invests in it. The leasing skills you build here, objection handling, resident communication, traffic conversion, transfer cleanly into every other role in property management.

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions, along with incentive programs tied to performance. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, and paid time off that includes your birthday.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is a skills game. The people who do it well aren't just friendly. They read a prospect quickly, adjust their pitch without being manipulative, handle a "I need to think about it" without desperation, and still find time to follow up on six other leads before lunch. That's the core of what Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring for at their Atlanta community.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Every day, you're using a short stack of skills repeatedly: active listening, objection handling, written communication, and basic sales discipline. Conducting personalized tours is less about memorizing floor plans and more about figuring out what matters to the person standing in front of you. Is it the commute? The closet space? The dog-friendliness? You ask, you listen, and you connect the dots out loud for them.

Beyond tours, you're processing leasing applications, completing move-in paperwork accurately, and tracking your own follow-up pipeline. The paperwork isn't glamorous, but a missed step during move-in creates problems that ripple into the resident's entire tenure. Precision matters here, not just personality.

You'll also help coordinate resident events and community engagement efforts. These aren't optional extras. They're how a property builds the kind of retention that keeps occupancy healthy without relying entirely on new traffic and concessions.

What Separates a Good Leasing Consultant from a Great One

The honest answer is follow-up discipline. Most prospects don't lease on the first visit. The consultants who convert at a high rate are the ones with a consistent, non-annoying system for staying in touch after a tour. They're also the ones who actually know the competing properties in the submarket, because a prospect asking "how does this compare to the place down the street?" deserves a real answer, not a deflection.

One more thing worth knowing: this schedule includes Saturdays, and resident events can occasionally push into evenings. That's the nature of leasing. If your weekends are completely off-limits, this role will create friction. If you're flexible and like the trade-off of a weekday off during the week, it tends to work well.

Building a Career Here

Hawthorne has a formal career path program, and the Leasing Consultant role is a recognized entry point into property management leadership. The natural next step is Assistant Community Manager, where the skills shift toward operations, financials, and team coordination. The leasing experience you build here, particularly around occupancy management and resident relations, translates directly into that next level.

  • High school diploma or GED required; one year of customer service or sales experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP certification is a plus but not required on day one
  • Total target compensation around $55,000, including hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions
  • Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid time off, pet insurance, and paid parental leave

Hawthorne is one of the larger Southeast-rooted multifamily operators in the country. If you want a company with enough structure to support your growth but enough regional identity to actually feel like something, that combination is harder to find than it sounds.

job.title: Leasing Consultant- Multi Site
job.description:
Multi-site leasing roles aren't for everyone. You're covering more than one community, which means your schedule shifts, your product knowledge has to be sharp across multiple floor plans and rent ranges, and your follow-up game has to be tighter than average. If that sounds like a grind, it probably is. If it sounds like a challenge worth taking on, keep reading.

Hawthorne Residential Partners is one of the larger Southeast-based operators in the country, consistently ranking among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally. This position is based at Retreat at Knoxville in the 37932 zip code, a growing corridor on the west side of the city that has seen consistent rental demand. The role itself is a leasing consultant position, but because it spans multiple sites, you're essentially running a tighter version of the full leasing cycle on repeat: handle traffic, tour prospects, convert leads, process paperwork, support renewals, and then do it again at the next property.

Day to day, you're the first person a prospective resident talks to, whether that's a walk-in, a phone call, or an email inquiry from an ILS. You're conducting tours, managing follow-up, and building enough rapport that someone chooses your community over the three others they toured that week. You'll also help coordinate resident events and keep an eye on what competitors are doing in the local market. It's a sales role with a service wrapper around it, and the best people in these seats understand that difference instinctively.

What actually separates strong candidates from average ones here isn't just personality. It's consistency. Anyone can have a great tour on a good day. The people who move up in leasing careers are the ones who follow up on the cold leads, who close on a Saturday afternoon when foot traffic has slowed, and who treat the 30th inquiry of the week with the same energy as the first. Hawthorne's own career path program recognizes this: leasing consultant to assistant community manager is a well-worn track in this industry, and operators like Hawthorne tend to promote from within when they see someone who can perform under volume.

What You'll Need

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least one year in customer service, sales, or apartment leasing (preferred, not required)
  • Valid driver's license (required given the multi-site nature of this role)
  • CALP certification is a plus if you have it
  • Comfortable working Saturdays and occasional evenings for resident events

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions, which is standard for the role. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k with match, paid time off, pet insurance, and paid parental leave options. The office runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays, 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to keep the schedule at 40 hours.

If you're early in your property management career and want to build leasing fundamentals fast, multi-site exposure does that more quickly than a single-property seat. You'll see different resident profiles, different pricing strategies, and more situations in a shorter period of time. That experience compounds.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Multi-Site
job.description:
Multi-site maintenance supervision is a different animal than running a single property. You're not just fixing things. You're managing schedules across communities, tracking vendor timelines on multiple make-readies simultaneously, keeping your team accountable when you're not physically on-site, and still finding time to put hands on equipment when the situation calls for it. Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring for exactly that kind of role in Atlanta.

The day-to-day here spans the full maintenance lifecycle. Unit turns need to be inspected and signed off before move-in, preventative maintenance programs need to run on a quarterly cadence, and capital improvement projects need bids sourced, schedules built, and execution managed. On any given week you might be walking a punch list on a vacant unit in the morning, meeting with a vendor about an ongoing capex project at noon, and coaching a technician through a proper HVAC repair in the afternoon. The variety is real, and so is the accountability.

Budget monitoring and inventory management fall under this role too. That means you need to understand what things cost, catch waste before it compounds, and make sure your team isn't sitting idle waiting on parts that should have been stocked. Grounds, amenities, and common areas also stay on your radar because curb appeal directly affects traffic and, ultimately, occupancy.

What separates a strong candidate here isn't just technical range, though you do need solid working knowledge across HVAC, plumbing, and electrical. It's the ability to keep multiple communities moving without letting any single one slip. Supervisors who thrive in multi-site roles tend to build tight vendor relationships early, because when a turn is sitting incomplete, a reliable contractor you can call on short notice is worth more than almost anything else.

On-call rotation is part of the job. After-hours emergencies happen, and Hawthorne expects you to respond. That's worth knowing going in.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least 3 years in apartment maintenance or a skilled trade (HVAC, plumbing, electrical)
  • Prior supervisory or lead tech experience strongly preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • EPA certification required
  • CPO certification highly preferred (required in some states)

Compensation includes hourly pay plus a monthly renewal bonus, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses. Hawthorne also offers a career path program with genuine development structure, education reimbursement for maintenance skills, and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid parental leave, and pet insurance, among other things.

If you've been running maintenance at a single property and want the complexity and career growth that comes with multi-site responsibility, this is a logical next step. Multi-site supervisors who build strong operational track records often move into regional or director-level maintenance roles, and Hawthorne's internal development program is structured to support that trajectory.

job.title: Regional Property Manager
job.description:
This role lives or dies on two skills: reading a financial statement fast and reading people even faster. The Regional Property Manager position at Hillpointe asks you to do both simultaneously, across a Sun Belt portfolio of workforce housing communities in and around Atlanta.

What This Role Actually Demands

Hillpointe isn't a third-party fee management shop. They develop, build, and operate their own product. That matters because when you're the Regional here, you're not translating an owner's vision through layers of bureaucracy. You're sitting close to the source. Budget variance conversations happen with people who built the asset. That's a different dynamic than most regionals experience.

The financial side is real. You're building annual budgets, managing pricing and renewal strategies inside Entrata, and digging into performance gaps before they show up as NOI problems on the T-12.
